docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Quick Start

### Build, preview, deploy Run the documentation pipeline from the repository root. 
make docs
make serve PORT=8001
make deploy

Pipeline

### Generated end to end The site is rebuilt from tracked shell sources every time. - `mise exec shdoc -- shdoc` renders structured script references when annotations exist - fallback pages still expose aliases, functions, and raw source when `shdoc` is not enough - `mkdocs-toc-md` writes the full navigation tree to [catalog/](catalog/) - `uv run --with-requirements` keeps the MkDocs toolchain ephemeral, at the exact versions in `scripts/mkdocs-requirements.txt`

Coverage

### Browse the full tree The homepage stays curated, while the complete generated table of contents lives on its own page. - [Open the full catalog](catalog/) - **104** source reference pages are generated from tracked shell assets - **29** chezmoi wrappers are mapped back to their source scripts

omp skills: which skills each omp launch and seat loads
docs.text: omp 18.11.3 (@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent, installed under ~/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent; paths below are relative to it) loads the shared skills under ~/.agents/skills and the pstack skills under ~/.agents/pstack/skills into the plain launch and the seats that skills.audience and skills.pstack.audience in the manifest name. This page names the settings that pin that, where the skills come from, how to prove what a seat loads, and how a seat's own skill coexists with the pstack set. Facts marked "measured" come from the U10 dry run of 2026-10-23 and the U87 dry run of 2026-10-25 under a scratch HOME.

docs.title: The key
docs.text:
skills.customDirectories in ~/.omp/agent/config.yml.

  • omp registers it at src/extensibility/settings.ts:65-69 (type array, default empty) and reads it in loadSkills at src/extensibility/skills.ts:471-480: each entry goes through expandTilde, is scanned one level deep for */SKILL.md, and is admitted under the provider id custom at level user with requireDescription: true.
  • The manifest home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml holds the list as omp.skills_directories (default ~/.agents/skills, the shared skill tree). scripts/generate-agent-configs.py validates it (~/ or absolute, no shell characters) and renders home/.chezmoitemplates/omp-config-managed.yml; make render-check fails when the template is stale.
  • home/dot_omp/private_agent/modify_private_config.yml merges modelRoles.default, skills.customDirectories, the top-level extensions list (docs/pi-claude-bridge.md, "Plain launch") and disabledProviders (the manifest's omp.disabled_providers, the same list the seat overlays carry; it keeps the retired openai-codex route unselectable on a plain launch too) into the live file and keeps every other key omp wrote. It writes the directories with ~ expanded to $HOME, because omp skill list resolves a non-absolute entry against the inspected directory before omp expands ~ (src/cli/skill-list.ts:58-64); measured, ~/.agents/skills lists nothing through that command while the absolute path lists the skills. A second apply is a no-op (tests/unit/test_omp_config_merge.py).
  • The merge reaches the default profile only. A seat started with omp --profile <name> reads ~/.omp/profiles/<name>/agent/config.yml instead (pi-utils src/dirs.ts:312-315), so a named profile gets the key, and its model route, from the per-role overlay below.

docs.title: Per-role overlays
docs.text:
~/.agents/omp/profiles/<role>.yml, one file per key of omp.roles in the manifest (orchestrator: deep, worker: standard, audit: audit). Each holds modelRoles.default from the mapped profile's omp.model and skills.customDirectories from omp.skills_directories; the seat launcher passes the role's file as a second --config beside the policy overlay (home/dot_agents/omp/policies/<role>.yml), so a named profile gets its model route and skill roots without a hand edit of ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml. The review and security roles, which no launcher started, were removed (U72); home/.chezmoiremove deletes their deployed overlays.

  • scripts/generate-agent-configs.py renders them as home/dot_agents/omp/profiles/<role>.yml.tmpl; make render-check fails when a file is stale, and the generator fails when omp.roles is missing, names an unknown profile, or carries a role name that is not launcher-safe. tests/unit/test_generate_agent_configs.py holds the cases and checks that every policy file has an overlay.
  • The committed file is a chezmoi template so that the deployed file carries the absolute home ({{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}/.agents/skills) while the repository stays machine-independent. The absolute form is needed because omp expands ~ in skills.customDirectories only on the session route (loadSkills, src/extensibility/skills.ts:471-473); omp skill list resolves a non-absolute entry against the inspected directory first (src/cli/skill-list.ts:58-64), and measured, the ~ form lists nothing there. modelRoles.default is a plain string copied from the layer (src/config/model-settings.ts:109, src/config/settings.ts:1626-1638) and gets no path handling.
  • Each overlay also carries setupVersion: 2 and startup.setupWizard: false. A seat profile has no ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml, so setupVersion reads its schema default 0 (src/modes/settings.ts:28), the cold-launch gate sees it below CURRENT_SETUP_VERSION 2 (src/main.ts:668-671, pi-tui src/setup/setup-version.ts:11) and runs the first-run wizard over the pane (measured 2026-10-23 on the worker and orchestrator seats: Setup step 1 of 5 / Sign in to your providers, where a keypress starts a provider login). startup.setupWizard: false (src/modes/settings.ts:1085-1095) empties the scene list (pi-tui src/setup/wizard.ts:52), and setupVersion: 2 keeps the gate from importing the wizard at all (src/main.ts:669-672).
  • An overlay wins over the profile's own config.yml key by key: runtime override → config overlay → project → global → schema default (src/config/settings.ts:879). --config and PI_CONFIG_FILES feed the same list (src/config/settings.ts:674-676) and the same strict loader, which refuses a missing file (Config overlay not found) or a non-mapping (src/config/settings.ts:2506-2528).
  • The listing and read-back commands take the overlay through PI_CONFIG_FILES only: omp skill list (src/cli/skill-list.ts:47) and omp config get (src/cli/config-cli.ts:164) call Settings.init without the parsed --config list, which an interactive or -p session passes (src/main.ts:1886). Measured, omp --profile u14test --config <overlay> --no-extensions skill list --json returns {"skills":[],"warnings":[]} under a profile that turns the agents provider off, while the same overlay through PI_CONFIG_FILES lists the skills.

Dry run of 2026-10-23, omp 18.11.3, wrapper HOME=$TMPDIR/u14-home, cwd an empty directory, ~/.omp/profiles/u14test/agent/config.yml = skills: {enableAgentsUser: false} (so only the overlay can supply the skills), ~/.agents/skills/{sharpen,unslop} linked from the pstack tree, overlay = the worker template rendered by chezmoi execute-template under the same HOME.

command result omp --profile u14test --no-extensions skill list --json {"skills":[],"warnings":[]} PI_CONFIG_FILES=<overlay> omp --profile u14test --no-extensions skill list --json sharpen and unslop, "source":"custom:user", "warnings":[] PI_CONFIG_FILES=<overlay with ~/.agents/skills> omp … skill list --json {"skills":[],"warnings":[]} PI_CONFIG_FILES=<missing file> omp … skill list --json skill list: Config overlay not found: <path> PI_CONFIG_FILES=<overlay> omp --profile u14test config get modelRoles --json "value": {"default": "claude-bridge/claude-opus-5-5"} omp --profile u14test config get modelRoles --json "value": {}

docs.title: Per-consumer audience
docs.text:
skills.audience in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml names, for every skill under home/dot_agents/skills and every installer-owned skill under ~/.agents/skills (crit, understand-*, terminal-browser), the agents that list it: claude, codex, omp (the plain launch) and omp-<role>. skills.pstack names the pstack audience and exclude, the pstack skills no agent lists (setup-pstack, which writes Cursor's ~/.cursor/rules). The generator refuses an unknown name, an empty or repeated audience, an undeclared home/dot_agents/skills directory, and a pstack audience naming Claude Code or Codex (neither reads the pstack root). For omp it renders, into the plain-launch config and each role overlay:

  • skills.ignoredSkills: every declared name the consumer is not given, and the pstack exclude list when it loads pstack. omp matches it against each skill's raw name from every source, custom directories included (src/extensibility/skills.ts:354-375, :495-496).
  • skills.customDirectories: omp.skills_directories, then ~/.agents/pstack/skills for a consumer in the pstack audience.
  • skills.enabled: false for a seat no skill names, the audit: it loads no skill from any source (:307-310).

Measured 2026-10-25 under a scratch HOME holding a copy of the deployed ~/.agents/skills (79 skills, the 57 pstack ones included), with the overlays rendered by chezmoi execute-template and the plain config by the modify script, omp --no-extensions skill list --json from an empty directory (PI_CONFIG_FILES=<overlay> for a seat):

consumer before: loaded, listed after: loaded, listed plain launch 79, 23 (hcom-*, project-map, setup-pstack listed) 75, 19 (none of those four) orchestrator 79, 23 76, 20 (hcom-orchestration, not hcom-worker) worker 79, 23 76, 20 (hcom-worker, not hcom-orchestration) audit 79, 23 0, 0

docs.title: The directory
docs.text:
~/.agents/skills (the shared skill tree, home/dot_agents/skills, and the installer-owned skills). omp scans it on two routes:

  • The agents provider (src/discovery/agents.ts:30 and :124-127, loader :158-174) scans ~/.agent/skills and ~/.agents/skills at the user level and .agent/skills and .agents/skills on the walk up from the project. Its user level is on by default: skills.enableAgentsUser defaults to true (src/extensibility/settings.ts:57, gate at src/extensibility/skills.ts:322), and .agents is not a foreign provider, so enabledProviders does not apply to it (src/capability/index.ts:363-373; upstream docs/skills.md, "Source toggles and filtering"). enabledProviders opts the foreign user roots in (~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.cursor; default off), but the agent-plugins provider, which reads the Claude Code marketplace registry under ~/.claude and refused pstack's plugin copy with 56 warnings, is not one of them: the seat overlays switch it off with disabledProviders: [agent-plugins] (omp.disabled_providers in the manifest, regime-cutover U22).
  • skills.customDirectories, the key above. It pins the root against a seat setting that turns the provider off (skills.enableAgentsUser: false, or disabledProviders naming agents).

With both routes on, each skill is listed once with no warning. Measured: source is agents:user, because the provider copy is admitted first and the custom copy of the same real path is skipped (src/extensibility/skills.ts:466-467).

docs.title: The instrument
docs.text:
omp skill list [dir] [--json] (src/cli/skill-list.ts:94-123) discovers skills for a directory exactly as a session would (:27-29) and prints one name<TAB>description row per skill, or the full result with --json. The --mode json session route of the pilot facts shows the same set through the system prompt, at the cost of a model turn; the listing command needs none.

Dry run of 2026-10-23, omp 18.11.3, wrapper HOME=$TMPDIR/u10-home, ~/.agents/skills/{sharpen,unslop} linked from the pstack tree, cwd an empty directory. Each row is the full stdout of omp skill list --json.

~/.omp/agent/config.yml result absent sharpen and unslop, "source":"agents:user", "warnings":[] skills: {enableAgentsUser: false} {"skills":[],"warnings":[]} the row above, then the modify script merged the rendered key (customDirectories: [/…/u10-home/.agents/skills]) sharpen and unslop, "source":"custom:user", "warnings":[] skills: {customDirectories: [/…/u10-home/.agents/skills]} (the deployed state) sharpen and unslop, "source":"agents:user", "warnings":[]

Both skills list with "hide":true: their front matter sets disable-model-invocation: true, which omp maps to hide (src/extensibility/skills.ts:463). A hidden skill is left out of the system prompt's <skills> listing and stays reachable through /skill:<name> and skill://<name> (:37-42). 56 of the 57 skills in pstack 0.15.30 set that flag.

docs.title: The pin
docs.text:
assets.pstack in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml: pin is a commit of cursor/plugins and sha256 the digest of GitHub's source archive of that commit (https://github.com/cursor/plugins/archive/<pin>.tar.gz). One chezmoi external in home/.chezmoitemplates/chezmoiexternal.d/common.yaml.tmpl reads both values from the manifest (include + fromYaml, so the pin lives in one place) and extracts harness/pstack/claude-code/skills/* into ~/.agents/pstack/skills and harness/pstack/claude-code/docs/** into ~/.agents/pstack/docs at every chezmoi apply, which make update runs. harness/pstack/claude-code is the Claude Code build of the plugin, the tree the cursor-plugins marketplace entry points at, so a seat reads the same bytes as the Claude Code plugin install; the docs land beside the skills because every skill's first paragraph links ../../docs/harness/claude-code.md. The directory is exact, so it holds the pinned archive's skills and nothing else: the pstack names are the archive's own at every apply, never a list kept in the repository, and a skill upstream drops is removed. No agent scans ~/.agents/pstack/skills by default, so Codex (whose listing budget the 56 manual-only skills would spend: it ignores disable-model-invocation) and Claude Code (which has the pstack plugin) never list them. skills.pstack.exclude is rendered as skills.ignoredSkills, not as an archive exclude: with both an include and an exclude list, chezmoi extracts every member that matches neither (chezmoiexternal-format, rule 5; measured, the other trees of the archive collided under the root and the apply failed with inconsistent state). No installer step, clone or receipt exists. chezmoi checks the download against sha256 and fetches the archive again only when the URL, that is the pin, changes, since refreshPeriod stays at its default of zero (chezmoi reference, .chezmoiexternal format: checksum.sha256, stripComponents, include, exact, refreshPeriod); chezmoi status reports drift in the deployed files.

Measured 2026-10-25 with the rendered external pointed at the pinned archive (its sha256 equal to assets.pstack.sha256; tests/unit/test_pstack_asset.py repeats the run with a fixture archive): chezmoi apply placed the 57 skill directories under ~/.agents/pstack/skills and the adapter at ~/.agents/pstack/docs/harness/claude-code.md; a second apply changed nothing; a stray directory under the root was removed at the next apply. The pstack skills used to land in ~/.agents/skills, and chezmoi does not delete what the retired external placed: scripts/update-agent-assets.sh (retire_shared_pstack_copies, run by make update) removes a ~/.agents/skills/<name> only when ~/.agents/pstack/skills/<name> exists and diff -r finds the trees identical (measured on a copy of this host's deployed tree: all 57 removed), and keeps a differing one, which make doctor then reports as listed by Codex outside its audience. make doctor runs scripts/update-agent-assets.sh check_pstack, which fails when poteto-mode/SKILL.md or the adapter file under ~/.agents/pstack is missing or when omp skill list does not name poteto-mode. A pstack name that skills.audience also declared would be listed twice by omp (the second copy namespaced, with a warning); tests/unit/test_pstack_asset.py keeps the two name sets disjoint.

docs.title: A seat's skill beside the pstack skills
docs.text:
A seat's own skill (hcom-worker, for example) is one more <name>/SKILL.md under home/dot_agents/skills, deployed to ~/.agents/skills, with a skills.audience entry naming the seat role (hcom-worker: [omp-worker]); the generator refuses the directory without one, and every other consumer ignores it. omp resolves same-named skills from its sources by name (src/extensibility/skills.ts:120-139; upstream docs/skills.md, "Collision and duplicate handling"):

  • Different names coexist. This is the normal case: pstack names are principle-*, correct, sharpen, unslop and so on; a seat skill carries the seat's name.
  • The same name with identical content is loaded once.
  • The same name with different content keeps the bare name for the higher-precedence copy (a custom-directory skill outranks a provider skill; otherwise the first admitted) and namespaces the other as <namespace>/<name> with a warning in the listing. Rename the seat skill rather than rely on that.
  • A seat skill the model should pick up on its own must not set disable-model-invocation: true; the pstack skills set it and are invoked by name, which is how poteto-mode addresses them.

docs.title: openai-siwc: omp provider for Sign in with ChatGPT
docs.text:
Design for the omp 18.11.3 extension at home/dot_agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc/. It gives the audit-side omp profiles ChatGPT plan inference through OpenAI's official Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC) route, which omp does not ship (issue can1357/oh-my-pi#13974, facts §3). The package loads in omp 18.11.3 and registers the provider, and gate G2 passed on 2026-10-23: a real login in the audit profile and a real -p turn (.orchestration/validation/025-pilot-facts.md, X2/X3). The points that one login and one turn did not measure still carry TODO(gate G2) and are listed under open questions.

Sources: .orchestration/validation/025-v13-facts-20261023.md (facts §3, §3b, §4), .orchestration/validation/025-pilot-facts.md #S0, the probe .orchestration/validation/025-pilot-s0-siwc-probe.py, red-team row R12R-07, the installed omp source under ~/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent (paths below are relative to it), and upstream docs/extensions.md and docs/provider-compat-reference.md (main, fetched 2026-10-23).

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
omp's built-in openai-responses transport already streams the Responses API, parses SSE, retries, and surfaces response.completed. The SIWC preview accepts a narrower request than omp builds. Measured against omp's real builder with a fake HTTP layer (the test tests/requests.test.ts), a provider named openai-siwc on https://api.openai.com/v1 sends prompt_cache_retention: "24h", max_output_tokens, and the system prompt as an input item with role: "developer". The preview rejects all three, and it needs store: false, stream: true, and full history instead of previous_response_id.

Login is the other gap. SIWC registers each host dynamically: the first authorize request uses client_id=dynamic_agent_client plus ext_agent_host_id, and the callback returns the issued client_id that every later exchange and refresh must use. pi-ai's OAuthCallbackFlow cannot carry that value, because its callback handler keeps only code and state (node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/registry/oauth/callback-server.ts:560-576).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The operator installs the package once and logs in once per profile:

omp --profile audit -e ~/.agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc
/login openai-siwc
/model openai-siwc/gpt-6.1-sol

What the extension does at load:

export default function openaiSiwc(pi: ExtensionAPI): void {
  pi.registerProvider("openai-siwc", {
    baseUrl: "https://api.openai.com/v1",
    api: "openai-responses",
    compat: SIWC_COMPAT,
    oauth: createSiwcOAuth({
      agentDir: pi.pi.getAgentDir(),
      agentName: "omp-dotfiles",
    }),
    models: MODELS,
  });
  pi.on("before_provider_request", (event, ctx) =>
    ctx.model?.provider === "openai-siwc"
      ? rewriteResponsesRequest(event.payload)
      : undefined,
  );
}

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Module Owns src/index.ts The registerProvider call, the static model rows, and the before_provider_request hook. src/oauth.ts The oauth block: authorize URL, PKCE, loopback receiver, code exchange, refresh, scope and nonce checks. src/requests.ts SIWC_COMPAT and rewriteResponsesRequest, the only place that knows the preview's request rules. src/store.ts The per-profile registration record: its path, validation, and atomic 0600 write. It is the record's single writer, called by oauth.ts.

The package has no runtime dependencies. It imports omp only as types (import type), which Bun erases.

docs.title: Registration record
docs.text:
One JSON file per omp profile at <agentDir>/openai-siwc/registration.json, where agentDir is getAgentDir() and therefore follows --profile (pilot facts #B3):

interface Registration {
  hostId: `urn:uuid:${string}`; // uuid4; a bare uuid was refused (pilot facts #S0 run 1)
  clientId?: string; // issued by the registration callback (prefix "oaiapp" measured)
  accountId?: string; // from the id_token account claim, when present
}

The record holds no secret. clientId is a public client identifier, and tokens never enter this file. Load rejects a malformed record instead of re-registering over it.

docs.title: OAuthCredentials mapping
docs.text:
Tokens live in omp's own credential store, <agentDir>/agent.db, which omp creates with directory mode 0700 and file mode 0600 (node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/auth/sqlite-credential-store.ts:587-594).

OAuthCredentials field Source access access_token; getApiKey returns it and omp sends it as the bearer. refresh refresh_token, replaced on every refresh. expires now + expires_in × 1000; expires_in measured as 3600. accountId id_token claim https://api.openai.com/auth → chatgpt_account_id (TODO(gate G2)). email id_token claim email. issued client_id Not in OAuthCredentials, which has no field for it; kept in the registration record.

docs.title: Login flow
docs.text:
1. Load the registration record. When none exists, create one with a fresh urn:uuid: host id and save it before opening the browser, so a retried first login reuses the same host id.
  2. Create a PKCE S256 pair, a fresh state, and a fresh OIDC nonce.
  3. Bind the loopback receiver on 127.0.0.1 (never localhost), port 1455 when free, otherwise a random port. The redirect URI is http://127.0.0.1:<port>/auth/callback.
  4. Build the authorize URL on https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/authorize with response_type=code, the scopes openid profile email offline_access resource.invoke chatgpt.tokens.use.direct, resource=https://api.openai.com/v1, the PKCE challenge, state, nonce, and ext_agent_host_id. A first login sends client_id=dynamic_agent_client and agent_name_hint=omp-dotfiles. A later login sends the saved client_id and no name hint.
  5. Hand the URL to omp through callbacks.onAuth; omp opens the system browser.
  6. The receiver answers only GET /auth/callback. A callback whose state is not ours gets a 400 page and is ignored, because any local process can send one. A callback with our state and error ends the login. A callback with our state and code resolves it. The wait honours callbacks.signal and a 5-minute timeout.
  7. Save the callback's client_id into the record when it differs from the saved one. The server is authoritative, and saving before the exchange keeps a failed exchange from causing a second registration.
  8. Exchange the code at https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/oauth/token, form-encoded, with grant_type=authorization_code, the issued client_id, code, code_verifier, the same redirect_uri, and the same resource. No client secret.
  9. Refuse the grant unless its scope contains chatgpt.tokens.use.direct. A valid ID token alone does not authorize plan usage (sign-in page, facts §4). Refuse an id_token whose nonce differs from ours.

docs.title: Refresh
docs.text: The access token lives 1 hour; the refresh token lives 30 days and rotates on every refresh (token reference, facts §4). refreshToken posts grant_type=refresh_token with the saved client_id, the stored refresh_token, and resource. It returns the replacement refresh token and keeps the old one only when a response omits it. Without a saved client_id it fails with an instruction to run /login openai-siwc. When a refresh response carries scope, the plan scope is checked again; an absent scope is accepted on refresh only (TODO(gate G2)).

docs.title: Request rewrite
docs.text:
Two layers, both on omp's own transport. SIWC_COMPAT stops omp from building most rejected shapes. rewriteResponsesRequest runs on every payload through before_provider_request, which omp passes to the transport as onPayload (src/sdk.ts:4345-4346), and the transport calls it for the first request and for both retry paths (node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/providers/openai-responses.ts:852-859, :1008, :1055). Line references below are in node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/providers/.

omp-emitted field or item Where omp emits it Handling role: "developer" system items in input openai-responses.ts:1640, when supportsDeveloperRole resolves true Compat supportsDeveloperRole: false sends the system prompt as instructions (:1660). The rewrite folds any remaining system or developer message item into instructions, which also covers the Juice item (:1779-1782). prompt_cache_retention: "24h" openai-responses.ts:1663 Compat supportsLongPromptCacheRetention: false; the rewrite deletes the field. max_output_tokens openai-responses.ts:1677, openai-shared.ts:4082 The rewrite deletes it. No compat key turns it off, and omitMaxOutputTokens is not accepted on an extension model row. temperature, top_p openai-shared.ts:4091-4092, only when sampling params are supported The rewrite deletes them. store openai-responses.ts:1671, true only with compat.storeResponses (:548) The rewrite forces store: false. previous_response_id with delta-only input openai-responses.ts:567 (PI_OPENAI_STATEFUL), :836 forces store: true Compat statefulResponses: false turns chaining off. PI_OPENAI_STATEFUL outranks compat, so the extension refuses to load when it is truthy (src/index.ts). The rewrite still throws on the field, but that only reports: omp's runner catches a hook throw and sends the unrewritten payload (src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:1590-1591, :1627-1632, :2121-2131). configuration_update input items Stable-effort policy (supportsConfigurationUpdate, provider-compat-reference) Compat supportsConfigurationUpdate: false. Other preview-rejected fields Not emitted by the 18.11.3 builder for this provider The rewrite deletes background, conversation, max_tool_calls, metadata, moderation, multi_agent, prompt, safety_identifier, top_logprobs, truncation, user in case a hook or a later omp adds them. prompt_cache_key, include, reasoning, stream_options Emitted (measured in the test's captured body) Kept. The preview does not list them as rejected. TODO(gate G2): confirm on the real endpoint.

stream: true is forced too. The rewrite copies the payload and never mutates omp's object.

docs.title: Error mapping
docs.text:
OpenAI's SIWC docs (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/llms-full.txt, "Errors and recovery", Structured Responses errors, read 2026-10-25) give each code its status and recovery. subscription_sharing_user_not_eligible (403) means "ChatGPT plan usage is unavailable for the selected user, workspace, or policy"; do not repeat the request. subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded (429) says to "Pause new requests that use the user's ChatGPT plan" and warns "Do not assume the entire plan is empty or infer a reset time from this code alone; an app-specific limit can also apply". subscription_sharing_usage_unavailable (503) means "Usage availability could not be checked. Preserve credentials and retry later with bounded backoff"; it is not a spent or unavailable plan. The extension adds no error code of its own: omp's classifier already handles all three, and tests/requests.test.ts proves it through omp's real transport with fake 403, 429 and 503 bodies.

Code Fake response What omp 18.11.3 does omp hook subscription_sharing_user_not_eligible HTTP 403 One request, then an error event naming the code. AIError.retriable is false, so the session does not retry the turn. isTransientStatus excludes 403 (pi-ai/src/error/retryable.ts:20-22); isProviderRetryableError treats every 4xx but 408/429 as terminal (:44-49). subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded HTTP 429 Classified Flag.UsageLimit (the code matches usage.?limit, pi-ai/src/error/rate-limit.ts:337), so isProviderRetryableError is false (retryable.ts:46) and the session hands it to omp's usage-limit recovery (wait for a reset within retry.maxDelayMs, or rotate to a sibling credential). The transport still sends 6 requests first. none reachable, see below subscription_sharing_usage_unavailable HTTP 503 A transient failure: the transport sends 6 requests, then an error event naming the code, and isProviderRetryableError is true, so the session may retry the turn. This matches the docs' bounded backoff; credentials are kept. none needed

The transport retry is the gap. postOpenAIStream sends through fetchWithRetry with 6 attempts (pi-ai/src/utils/openai-http.ts:33, :100-117), which retries every 429 unless the response carries a retry hint above 60 s or a proxy concurrency marker (pi-utils/src/fetch-retry.ts:375-382). The only caller gate, shouldRetryResponse, is built from omp-internal state (openai-responses.ts:903-905), and the fetch override reaches the transport only through SimpleStreamOptions.fetch (pi-ai/src/types.ts:716-723), which the session never sets for a built-in api. A before_provider_request hook sees only the payload, and after_provider_response fires only after a 2xx (openai-responses.ts:914, after postOpenAIStream has thrown on any other status). So on the built-in openai-responses transport no extension hook stops those 5 resends. With omp's default backoff they take about 15 s and spend nothing, because the server refuses each one. The custom-api candidate below would own the fetch; it is not taken, because it renames the session's model.api and so silently changes every omp branch keyed on "openai-responses" (src/utils/tool-choice.ts:17-23, src/tools/think.ts:31-36, src/session/agent-session.ts:11043, :11090-11094, src/sdk.ts:1610-1612). The test pins the 6 requests, so an omp release that adds a gate fails it.

Operating rules that follow from the docs and the SIWC Terms (https://openai.com/policies/sign-in-with-chatgpt-terms/, read 2026-10-25):

  • On subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded, stop sending new requests on the profile and read ChatGPT Settings > Usage, under App limits (help article https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001542). Do not probe the route to learn whether the limit has reset: the article says "An app can reach its own limit even when your ChatGPT plan still has usage available" and "Signing in again or repeatedly retrying does not restore your usage".
  • Keep one SIWC account per omp profile. omp's usage-limit recovery can rotate to a sibling credential of the same provider, and the Terms (§4) forbid enabling "Creating multiple accounts, splitting usage, rotating accounts, or otherwise bypassing usage limits". A second account stored under the same profile would let omp do exactly that.

docs.title: Synthesis decision
docs.text: The architect skill's single-runner form was used, with the arena skipped by the brief. Two whole shapes were sketched. The base is the payload-hook shape (built-in openai-responses transport, compat, and a before_provider_request rewrite). The rejected candidate registered a custom api with streamSimple, wrapping pi-ai's streamSimple with its own fetch. It would own error mapping at the HTTP layer, but built-in api ids are reserved (node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-ai/src/api-registry.ts:65-69), so it needs a new api id and must re-target each model to openai-responses before delegating, which ties the extension to omp's internal model shape. U3b confirmed it is the only shape that reaches the transport's 429 retry, and kept it rejected: renaming the session's model.api changes more omp behaviour than five refused resends cost (Error mapping above).

docs.title: Tradeoffs accepted
docs.text:
• We accept depending on before_provider_request reaching every request in exchange for reusing omp's transport, SSE parsing, and retries unchanged. Upstream documents that transports must invoke onPayload and that devin-agent does not; openai-responses does.
  • We accept a hand-written loopback receiver of about 40 lines in exchange for capturing the issued client_id, which OAuthCallbackFlow drops.
  • We accept static model rows in exchange for no discovery call. #S0's empty GET /v1/models result does not show that discovery is unavailable: the probe read data[].id, while the SIWC docs return a models array of {slug, visibility} ("Models and inference", step 1), so the list is unmeasured until the re-probe under open questions.
  • We accept one registration per profile, so three audit profiles mean three agent entries in the ChatGPT account (red-team R12R-06 proposed one shared record). The brief fixes the record per profile.

docs.title: Threat table
docs.text: Asset or boundary Threat Control Test Token store Another local user reads access or refresh tokens. Tokens stay in omp's agent.db (dir 0700, file 0600, sqlite-credential-store.ts:587-594). The extension writes no token anywhere. tests/oauth.test.ts: tokens only in returned credentials. Registration record Tampering or a half-written file causes a re-registration. Atomic write (temp file, rename) with 0600 file and 0700 directory; strict validation on load and save. tests/store.test.ts: modes 0600 and 0700, bare uuid refused. Loopback port Another process holds 1455 or listens on ::1. Bind 127.0.0.1 only, as the docs require; fall back to a random port, which the docs allow. tests/oauth.test.ts loopback test (skipped where binding is refused). Redirect validation A forged local request injects a code (login CSRF). Only GET /auth/callback; state must match; a foreign state is ignored, not fatal; the first accepted callback settles the wait; PKCE S256 binds the code to this process; id_token nonce must match when present. tests/oauth.test.ts: foreign state ignored, PKCE checked by the fake. Grant scope An identity-only grant is used for inference. Login refuses a grant without chatgpt.tokens.use.direct. tests/oauth.test.ts: scope refusal. Log redaction Tokens or codes reach logs or error messages. The extension logs nothing. Token errors carry only the OAuth error and error_description, capped at 200 characters; request bodies are never echoed. The callback page shows no parameters. Review only. Hosts Traffic leaves the two named hosts. Constants only: auth.openai.com for authorize and token, api.openai.com for inference. No discovery or telemetry call. tests/fake-auth-server.ts asserts both URLs.

docs.title: Open questions and risks
docs.text:
• Does a later sign-in with the issued client_id accept ext_agent_host_id? Default: send it, because the sign-in page marks it required. G2's second login per profile measures it.
  • Does a refresh response carry scope, and does the SIWC id_token carry the Codex account claim? Defaults: accept an absent scope on refresh; leave accountId empty when the claim is absent.
  • Does GET /v1/models list the plan's models? Unmeasured: #S0 read the wrong field (data[].id), so its models_total 0 says nothing. The probe now reads .models[] by slug and visibility (--selftest checks the documented shape). Re-probe, operator-only because it registers an agent through a browser login: uv run --no-project .orchestration/validation/025-pilot-s0-siwc-probe.py --name omp-dotfiles-models-probe, then delete that agent in ChatGPT settings as G6 did. If models_listed is non-empty, register fetchDynamicModels and drop the static rows; until then both static rows stay, and both have answered on this route (gpt-6.1-sol in #S0 and G2, gpt-6-astra in the audit verdicts from 2026-10-23 on).
  • What HTTP status carries each subscription error? Default: rely on omp's classifier, which handles a 403 and a 429 as the table above shows.
  • Should three profiles share one registration (R12R-06)? Default: one per profile, as the brief specifies.
  • Are prompt_cache_key, include, reasoning and stream_options accepted? Default: keep them.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Gate G2 passed (2026-10-23). The remaining measurements are the models re-probe above and the TODO(gate G2) points that need a second login per profile or a refresh response.

The rows below change a host outside that scope (old tool versions, stray binaries, retired worktrees, credential rows), so the operator runs them by hand. Agents never run them (standing order 30). Every row says how it was dry-run read-only, and when: the facts are from 2026-10-25 against origin/main c63415e5. Run the dry-run column again just before the command; if its output differs from the one below, stop and re-check.

docs.title: The orchestrator seat: stop gate, skill and doctor wiring
docs.text: Plan 025 W6b (U9). The orchestrator seat is the omp process that scripts/orchestrator/hcom-seat orchestrator starts in the repository checkout. This page covers the three pieces that make it able to run the program loop: the session_stop gate that keeps it from ending a turn while it owes the bus a reply, the hcom-orchestration skill that is its playbook, and the make doctor line that proves the bridge it talks through still loads. omp paths below are relative to ~/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent (omp 18.11.3); facts marked measured come from the U9 scratch runs of 2026-10-23 under HOME=$TMPDIR/u9-home.

docs.title: The stop gate
docs.text: home/dot_agents/omp/hooks/stop-gate.ts, applied to ~/.agents/omp/hooks/stop-gate.ts. It is an omp extension loaded with -e ~/.agents/omp/hooks: a configured directory without a package.json manifest or an index.ts is scanned one level deep for .ts files (src/extensibility/extensions/directory-resolution.ts:101-140, called from loader.ts:652), so the tests/ directory beside it is not loaded. hcom-seat passes -e ~/.agents/omp/hooks on every launch, whatever the role or --ext (U33c). Before U33c no seat loaded it: on 2026-10-24 the orchestrator, audit and worker seats ran omp with -e for the pi-claude-bridge, the openai-siwc extension and hcom's own hcom.ts only (ps, pids 42205, 8361 and 5621), so the gate described here never ran in an hcom seat until then.

docs.title: The event
docs.text:
omp fires session_stop when a main-agent turn is about to settle (src/extensibility/shared-events.ts:109-119, "handlers may request one continuation turn"); an extension subscribes with pi.on("session_stop", …) (src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts:1661). This is omp's native blocking stop hook, so no fallback is needed:

  • A handler result {decision: "block", reason} makes the runner return at once (src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:1689-1692) and the session queue a hidden continuation turn whose content is reason (src/session/agent-session.ts:5196-5198, :5291-5301). The model sees the reason as context and gets another turn.
  • event.stop_hook_active is true while a continuation the gate asked for is settling (agent-session.ts:5264, set at :5290).
  • A block is exempt from the continuation cap (agent-session.ts:5276), so a gate that blocked every settle could loop for as long as a RESULT never arrives. The gate therefore blocks the first settle and answers {continue: true, reason} while stop_hook_active is set, which the cap SESSION_STOP_CONTINUATION_CAP = 8 bounds (agent-session.ts:470, :5276-5283). After one block and eight continuations omp ends the turn with the warning still printed.
  • Subagents never see the event (agent-session.ts:5254), so the gate applies to the seat's own turns only.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
The gate reads the thread's rows since the seat started, ~/.local/bin/common/bus-history.sh <team> --limit 100000 --since <seat start>, and keeps the newest row per task_id among the rows that move a task. The script keeps the newest --limit rows (default 200), so the gate asks for far more than a program writes and treats a full window as unreadable (a warning, the turn ends unchecked) rather than as proof of no debt:

Row, by kind (the exact first word) and sender Effect on its task_id TASK from the seat open: awaiting RESULT RESULT from a seat the seat's TASK under that id went to (its to column) open: owes a VERDICT, MERGED or HOLD line VERDICT, MERGED or HOLD from the seat closed anything else (PING, every PONG, status=question included, another seat's TASK, MERGED or HOLD, a RESULT on a task the seat did not send to its author, a VERDICT from any other seat, …) no effect; the previous moving row keeps the state

The line kinds are the first word of a bus line: TASK, RESULT, VERDICT, PONG, MERGED and HOLD (plus PING, which moves nothing). Any other first word, such as the retired AGMSG-TASK, is not a kind and moves nothing. There is no audit seat on the bus: every audit is one fresh omp-run.sh --role audit run that the orchestrator starts and reads (the hcom-orchestration skill, step 4), so its verdict reaches the bus only as the orchestrator's own VERDICT line, and another seat's VERDICT closes nothing, on an -audit id or any other (U58).

Every seat loads the gate and shares the thread, so a row from another seat opens a debt only on a task this seat sent to that very seat (U33c): a worker seat never owes anything for a peer's RESULT, and the orchestrator owes a verdict on the RESULTs of the TASKs it sent.

One message lists the open items with their row ids and the ways out: answer them, wait with hcom listen, or send HOLD v1 task_id=<id> note=<why>, the auditable override that the skill names. OMP_STOP_GATE_ALLOW_OPEN=1 ends the turn with the warning instead of the block.

docs.title: The seat's environment
docs.text:
Variable Meaning Set by HCOM_DIR the program's private bus store, read by bus-history.sh the environment when set; else hcom-seat derives ~/.local/state/hcom/<slug> from the checkout (regime-env, U33) and exports it; hcom passes it to the seat HCOM_TEAM the thread every TASK line of the program names hcom does not pass it into the pane it launches (measured in the U33 pilot), so hcom-seat passes the team it was given, explicit or derived, as --hcom-team <team>; the gate reads that flag, else HCOM_TEAM, never a team derived from the cwd, and exports the result as HCOM_TEAM into the seat at session start (U33c) HCOM_NAME the seat's own hcom name; absent, hcom list self name hcom, when it exports it; else the command (hcom list --help) OMP_STOP_GATE_ALLOW_OPEN 1 ends the turn with the warning the operator, never the seat

<slug> is the main checkout's basename, lower-cased, [^a-z0-9_-] as -, at most 40 characters (README.md, "Run a program in another repository"). Without a team (no --hcom-team and no HCOM_TEAM, or one outside the team grammar) or a seat name the gate is inert and says so at every stop; a bus-history.sh failure ends the turn with the failure in the warning. Both are visible, never silent (M-20261023-01). In print mode (omp -p, omp-run.sh) there is no UI, so the warning goes to stderr, which omp-run.sh holds and replays; interactively it is ctx.ui.notify(…, "warning").

docs.title: Measured
docs.text:
• bun test home/dot_agents/omp/hooks/tests/stop-gate.test.ts: 7 tests, 25 assertions, pass (U9c run, 2026-10-23). They cover the open and closed transitions above, the three VERDICTs that settle nothing, the exact message, the block on the first settle and the capped continuation on the next, OMP_STOP_GATE_ALLOW_OPEN, the inert case, and the bus-history.sh argv (<team> --since <ISO second>Z).
  • U33c, 2026-10-24: bun test home/dot_agents/omp/hooks/tests/stop-gate.test.ts, 11 pass, adding the flag over HCOM_TEAM over nothing (a regime-env beside the installed bus-history.sh is never consulted), the team grammar, and a peer's RESULT that opens nothing. Under a scratch HOME, a probe extension that registers hcom-team saw getFlag undefined while loading and "custom" at session_start for omp -e probe.ts --hcom-team custom --mode rpc --no-session (also --hcom-team=regime), and omp without an extension that registers it exits 2 with Error: unknown flag: --hcom-team. tests/unit/test_hcom_seat.py test_the_team_crosses_the_launch_boundary_as_a_flag_and_the_gate_blocks_on_it launches with HCOM_TEAM=custom through a fake hcom that drops HCOM_TEAM as the real one does, then runs the real gate (tests/launch-driver.ts, under bun) on that argv and environment: it blocks on thread custom, and without the flag it is inert instead of reading the checkout's slug.
  • Load check under HOME=$TMPDIR/u9-home with a fake scripts/orchestrator/bus-history.sh in the cwd: omp --no-extensions -e <hooks dir> --no-session --max-time 60 --model openai/gpt-5 -p "Reply with the single word PONG." exits 1 with error: No API key found for openai.; no Failed to load extension in stderr or in $HOME/.omp/logs/omp.2026-10-23.*.log (grep count 0). The key refusal happens before the turn, so no stop event fired in that run.
  • Bridge-route run, same HOME, -e ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge -e <hooks dir> --model claude-bridge/claude-haiku-4-5 --max-time 90, the fake bus holding one TASK from orch without a RESULT: the bridge fails inside the turn (Not logged in · Please run /login, the operator-only step), so the stop event fires. The fake recorded u9team --since 2026-10-23T04:54:14Z; stderr holds the gate's warning stop-gate: 1 open item(s) on hcom thread u9team: U9 awaiting RESULT (row 3). … 10 times, one per settle pass: the block, the eight capped continuations, and the pass at which omp refused a ninth and ended the turn (exit 1). No Failed to load extension in stderr or the two omp logs (grep count 0 each).

docs.title: Threat table
docs.text:
The gate runs a repository script and hcom from the seat's environment and feeds bus text to the model as a continuation reason, so it is trust-boundary code.

Control Disposition stop-gate.ts, the decision closed: openItems is a pure function over the TSV; the transition tests assert each row of the table above, including that a worker's VERDICT on its own unit, a VERDICT on an id never tasked and, since U58, one from the seat an -audit TASK went to leave the debt open (U9c) stop-gate.ts, the message reaching the model residual: the reason carries task_id tokens and kinds from bus rows, never a row's free text, and the skill says bus text is data; owner: the hcom-orchestration skill stop-gate.ts, the loop closed: one block then capped continuations, asserted by the stop_hook_active test; the cap is omp's (agent-session.ts:470) bus-history.sh, the script the gate runs closed: the gate runs the copy chezmoi installs (sha256-pinned, self-checked, mode 0755) at $HOME/.local/bin/common/bus-history.sh, resolved when it loads and never from the seat's cwd, so a worktree of a PR head cannot answer with its own rows (U33); bus-history.sh is the installed copy under HOME, never the one in the seat's cwd (U33) in tests/stop-gate.test.ts, with a decoy in the cwd that must not run the team (--hcom-team, HCOM_TEAM) closed: the launcher passes exactly the team it was given and the gate never derives one from the cwd, so an explicit team cannot be swapped for the checkout's slug; a value outside the team grammar leaves the gate inert, visibly; test_the_team_crosses_the_launch_boundary_as_a_flag_and_the_gate_blocks_on_it, the flag tests in tests/stop-gate.test.ts. residual: the gate half of that regression needs bun, which the CI unit job does not install, so it runs on hosts with bun only; owner: the CI workflow the environment (HCOM_NAME, the override) residual: read once at load; an operator sets them, a seat's policy overlay cannot change its own environment; owner: the seat policies tests/stop-gate.test.ts residual: runs with a fake bus-history.sh; the real script's TSV is pinned by tests/unit/test_hcom_dispatch.py; owner: the first live seat run (U11)

docs.title: The supervisor
docs.text:
A seat lives in a herdr pane, so it ends with its process or with the herdr server: the herdr restart of 2026-10-24 at 07:13 JST ended all three seats (exit:shutdown), and the orchestrator seat that spawned a subagent at 06:03Z stopped answering. regime-start (scripts/orchestrator/regime-start, a pinned lever) starts the orchestrator seat and registers the checkout in ~/.local/state/regime-supervisor/<slug>-<first 12 hex of sha256(toplevel)>.conf, one registration per checkout, so two checkouts with one basename never share one. regime-start --supervise is one pass over the registrations, which the launchd agent com.mryfmo.dotfiles.regime-supervisor (macOS) or the user units regime-supervisor.service and .timer (Linux) run at login and every 60 seconds once the operator enables them; both ship disabled (the plist carries Disabled, launchd.plist(5), and only the operator's launchctl enable, kept across logins and boots per launchctl(1), loads it; make update installs the systemd units without enabling them; README, "Start here: the omp seats"). The pass relaunches a registered orchestrator that is not alive, unless the newest stop event hcom recorded for the last seat (hcom list --stopped <base name>, the (latest) line) is killed by:cli, an hcom kill, which ends the supervision like regime-stop does. A failed launch waits 60 seconds, doubling by saturation to 30 minutes, and the failure counter stops at 9999. regime-start, the pass and regime-stop (which is regime-start --stop) take one host lock: the kernel's flock(2) on ~/.local/state/regime-supervisor/supervisor.lock, held through a descriptor the script keeps open (perl takes it, because macOS ships no flock command). Start and stop wait for it, and a pass that finds it held skips. The kernel releases it only when its last holder exits or dies, so it is never taken over by age or by a pid, no other process can release it, and the file is never removed. A launch runs in subshells that keep the descriptor until the launch and its wait return, so killing regime-start cannot let a stop in while a launch is in flight; hcom-seat and every hcom call get the descriptor closed, so a seat never holds the lock after its launch (measured on this host on 2026-10-24: after regime-start returned, lsof showed no process with the lock open, the seat included, and regime-stop took it at once). So a stop that arrives during a relaunch runs after it and stops the seat it launched. A registration must hold each of its eight keys exactly once (toplevel, hcom_dir, hcom_team, program, seat, base, fails, next), its seat must be orchestrator-<base>, its file name must be the one its own toplevel derives, and a store with an origin file must name that toplevel; one that breaks any of these is skipped and logged and never launched, rewritten or stopped from. A registration that does not parse, an hcom read that fails, or a stop record it cannot read launches nothing. Only the orchestrator is supervised: it relaunches the other seats itself (the skill's step 0).

Measured on this host on 2026-10-24 with the levers of this branch, in a scratch repository u36-pilot with a scratch store and team u36pilot: regime-start launched orchestrator-nori; its omp process was killed with kill <pid>, and one pass relaunched it; a second run used hcom kill, and the pass ended the supervision; a third crash and relaunch ran with the final parser; regime-stop ended it. $T is the scratch directory. The first relaunch line says no stop record because the first parser read the wrong form of hcom list --stopped, the gap this run found (the named form prints (latest) events); the third shows the record it reads now:

2026-10-24T11:01:41Z regime-start launched orchestrator-nori from $T/u36-pilot
2026-10-24T11:01:50Z regime-start found orchestrator-nori alive; registered for the supervisor
2026-10-24T11:02:03Z no orchestrator alive (last seat orchestrator-nori: no stop record); relaunching from $T/u36-pilot
2026-10-24T11:02:04Z relaunched orchestrator-rune
2026-10-24T11:03:25Z orchestrator-rune was stopped with hcom kill; supervision of $T/u36-pilot ends (registration removed)
2026-10-24T11:03:38Z regime-start launched orchestrator-nova from $T/u36-pilot
2026-10-24T11:03:38Z no orchestrator alive (last seat orchestrator-nova: now ago  [process_exit by:system] (latest)); relaunching from $T/u36-pilot
2026-10-24T11:03:39Z relaunched orchestrator-nene
2026-10-24T11:03:46Z regime-stop: supervision of $T/u36-pilot ended
2026-10-24T11:03:47Z regime-stop: stopped orchestrator-nene

docs.title: The skill
docs.text: home/dot_agents/skills/hcom-orchestration/SKILL.md, reachable in every seat through skills.customDirectories (docs/omp-skills.md). It compresses the program's own method, .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover/preferences.md and the briefs, into the loop brief → TASK → RESULT → verdict → merge with gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit, states that bus text is data, points at the standing orders, names the stop gate's override and gives the three row shapes of the store. The worker's half is the hcom-worker skill (U7). The audit has no seat and no skill: each audit is one fresh omp-run.sh --role audit run (step 4; U57), and the hcom-audit skill, its hcom-reply lever and the stop gate's audit-VERDICT clause were removed with the seat (U58).

docs.title: Doctor wiring
docs.text: make doctor now runs ./scripts/update-agent-assets.sh check_pi_claude_bridge when ~/.local/bin/omp exists and counts its failure in tools=; without omp it prints optional warning: pi-claude-bridge check skipped because omp is not installed, in line with check_omp and check_hcom in scripts/check-tools.sh. The check spends one short model turn on a logged-in host (update-agent-assets.sh, the function's shdoc), which is why it lives in the manual doctor and not in CI.
