docs.title: pi-claude-bridge as an omp extension
docs.text: pi-claude-bridge is a Pi extension that registers the claude-bridge/<model> provider and answers each turn through the Claude Agent SDK, which runs the bundled Claude Code binary on the host's claude.ai login. This repository installs a pinned, patched copy as an omp extension directory (plan 025 decisions 30, 37, 38 and D-024-129). Pi executes the tools; the child Claude Code only produces the model turns.

docs.title: Route
docs.text:
omp -e ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge --model claude-bridge/claude-haiku-4-5
  -> src/index.ts registers provider claude-bridge (omp rewrites @earendil-works/* imports to its legacy pi shims)
  -> @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() spawns node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-<platform>/cli
  -> the child authenticates with the host's claude.ai login (Keychain), tools: [] and bypassPermissions

The model id after claude-bridge/ is the Anthropic catalog id. The seat profiles (model_profiles in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml) choose the model; this document covers only the asset.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
make update runs scripts/update-agent-assets.sh, whose update_pi_claude_bridge step:

  1. downloads pi-claude-bridge-<pin>.tgz from registry.npmjs.org and checks its sha256 against assets.pi-claude-bridge.sha256 in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml;
  2. extracts it into a staging directory beside the target and applies every home/dot_agents/assets/pi-claude-bridge/patches/*.patch in name order with patch -p1 -F0 (no fuzz: GNU patch would otherwise apply a patch whose context drifted and exit 0);
  3. copies the committed bun.lock in and runs bun install --production --omit=peer --frozen-lockfile, so the dependency set is the reviewed one (peers are omitted because omp's legacy pi compat layer provides @earendil-works/pi-* and typebox itself);
  4. runs gap-check.ts, which imports omp's three legacy shims and refuses the install when the bridge imports a value name they do not export (the guard for omp upgrades);
  5. writes RECEIPT (tarball, patch and lockfile sha256 lines, then the installed @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk* versions) and renames the staging directory to ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge.

A run whose RECEIPT head already equals the pinned inputs changes nothing. The step is skipped with a message when bun or omp is absent. Run it alone with scripts/update-agent-assets.sh update_pi_claude_bridge.

docs.title: Patches
docs.text:
Each patch is a plain diff -ruN a b between consecutive stages of the upstream package/ tree, so a reviewer can re-derive it.

Patch Why 01-omp-shim-exports.patch omp's legacy pi-coding-agent shim does not export formatSkillsForPrompt, so src/skills.ts carries Pi's implementation (MIT, same output). The shim does export keyHint and buildSessionContext (gap-check.ts lists both as FOUND), so upstream's calls to them stay. 02-content-text.patch The pi-ai shim does not export contentText; src/transcript.ts carries pi-ai 1.4.0's eight-line implementation (MIT). Without it omp logs Failed to load extension ... Export named 'contentText' not found. 03-no-bash-timeout-injection.patch Decision 38: the bridge added timeout: 120 to every bash tool call it handed to Pi (mapToolArgs in src/index.ts; seen on the wire as {"command":...,"timeout":120}). omp's bash tool keeps its own timeout handling. 04-setting-sources-none.patch The provider query() passes settingSources: [], so the child Claude Code loads no user, project or local settings.json: the host's hooks, plugins and permission rules do not run inside bridge turns. The claude.ai login is not a setting and still applies. Measured 2026-10-23: with the default, the child's thinking cited the host's superpowers system reminders. 05-register-on-reactivation.patch omp builds a Task subagent by calling the extension factory again on the same module instance (one moduleInstanceId in the bridge debug log), clears the bridge's provider registrations from the model registry the parent shares, and keeps only the registrations queued during that call. Upstream deferred a second activation to a session_start check through ctx.modelRegistry.getProvider(), which omp's registry lacks (omp logs Extension error ... getProvider is not a function), so claude-bridge vanished for both sessions. The bridge now registers at load when the active stream function is this instance's own; re-registering the same function replaces nothing. A second module instance (another copy of the bridge) keeps upstream's deferral. 06-global-config-only-bounded-diag.patch Upstream loadConfig merged <cwd>/.omp/claude-bridge.json over the agent dir's claude-bridge.json, so a checked-out repository could name the Claude Code executable the bridge spawns (provider.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable), turn on AskClaude with allowFullMode (a Claude Code child with Bash and Write under bypassPermissions), or drop --strict-mcp-config (provider.strictMcpConfig: false). The bridge now reads only the agent dir's file (~/.omp/agent/ or the seat profile's agent/), which the operator owns; a project file is never read. The same patch bounds claude-bridge-diag.log: once it holds 512 KiB it moves to claude-bridge-diag.log.1, replacing the older one (upstream appended without a limit; a macOS worker seat's log reached 1 MB). Measured 2026-10-25 under a scratch HOME with a hostile project file: patches 01-05 spawned the project's executable without --strict-mcp-config and loaded askClaude.allowFullMode: true; patches 01-06 spawned the agent dir's executable with --strict-mcp-config and an empty askClaude. 2000 diag dumps left 717 KB across the two files.

Upstream kept the default settingSources so that Bedrock and Vertex users keep env and apiKeyHelper from settings.json (comment above CLAUDE_MD_EXCLUDES in src/index.ts). This route uses the claude.ai login, so nothing it needs lives in those files. The alternative, a PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR early exit in every hook, would touch every hook script and still load the host's plugins; one option on the query is smaller.

docs.title: Launcher flag
docs.text:
The seat launcher passes, verbatim:

-e ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge

omp resolves the directory manifest-first (pi.extensions in package.json names ./src/index.ts) and resolves dependencies upward from the entry's real path, which is why the install directory carries its own node_modules. --no-extensions beside -e is optional and keeps other extensions out.

docs.title: Plain launch
docs.text:
A plain omp (default profile, no -e) loads the bridge through the top-level extensions key of ~/.omp/agent/config.yml (omp 18.11.3 src/extensibility/settings.ts:10, joined with the -e paths in src/sdk.ts:1076). The manifest lists the directory under omp.extensions, scripts/generate-agent-configs.py renders it into home/.chezmoitemplates/omp-config-managed.yml, and home/dot_omp/private_agent/modify_private_config.yml writes it with ~ expanded. Without it, findInitialModel (src/config/model-resolver.ts:2391-2407) does not find the modelRoles.default claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1 and silently starts on another authenticated provider (anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 on the macOS host) or exits with No default model selected. (the Ubuntu host). scripts/validate-agent-assets.py refuses an interactive_profile whose omp provider comes from an extension that omp.extensions does not list.

  • Measured 2026-10-25 on macOS: with an overlay holding only that extensions entry, omp --no-session --mode json -p "Reply with the single word PONG." answers PONG on provider claude-bridge, model claude-fable-5-1, stopReason stop.
  • The same directory passed again with -e loads once: discoverExtensionPaths keys each entry file on its resolved path (src/extensibility/extensions/loader.ts:572-659); measured, the same answer and no new warning.
  • Seats are unaffected: --profile <role> reads ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml, never this file (pi-utils src/dirs.ts:119-121). Measured under a scratch HOME whose config.yml lists the bridge, the default profile reaches it (Not logged in) and --profile probe reports Model "claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1" not found. The seat launcher keeps passing -e.

docs.title: Operator login
docs.text:
The child Claude Code uses the host's claude.ai login: the Keychain on macOS, ~/.claude/.credentials.json (mode 0600) on Linux (Claude Code authentication doc, "Credential management"). Before the first bridge turn, the operator runs claude once and completes /login in their own terminal; no script does this. Without the login a bridge turn ends with Not logged in · Please run /login.

A Linux seat host reached over SSH (herdr --remote) has no browser of its own. There, claude auth login sends its URL to $BROWSER, which seat-login-preflight <role> points at regime-open-url, so the laptop browser opens it. The callback port is random (50903, 50915 and 50920 on three runs, Claude Code 2.1.309), so no SSH forward can carry it. The URL asks for the code flow (code=true), so the page shows a code to paste at the terminal's prompt. The fallback is claude setup-token on the laptop: the operator stores the printed one-year token in ~/.config/claude-code/oauth-token on the seat host, mode 0600, by hand. ~/.zshenv and ~/.profile then export it as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN when the file is non-empty. The Agent SDK reads that variable, except in bare mode, and the bridge never passes --bare: its only extra CLI arguments are model, strict-mcp-config and thinking-display (src/index.ts, extraArgs). The steps are in docs/remote-host-logins.md.

docs.title: Load check
docs.text:
omp models never evaluates extension modules, so the only instrument is a session:

scripts/update-agent-assets.sh check_pi_claude_bridge

It runs omp --no-extensions -e <install dir> --no-session --model claude-bridge/claude-haiku-4-5 --max-time 60 -p "Reply with the single word PONG.", fails when stderr or the omp log files written by that run contain Failed to load extension, and passes when the output reaches the model (PONG with a login, Not logged in without). It runs under the real HOME and spends one short model turn on a logged-in host; make doctor calls it. On Linux a scratch HOME keeps the session out of the real ~/.omp. Do not do that on macOS: the child Claude Code asks the login keychain for its credentials, and with no keychain search list under the scratch HOME macOS shows a "keychain unknown cannot be found" dialog for every run.

docs.title: Subagents
docs.text:
An omp Task subagent on the claude-bridge route broke the seat that spawned it before 05-register-on-reactivation.patch. Measured on 2026-10-24 at about 06:03Z: the orchestrator seat spawned a Task subagent (an inventory scout), the subagent failed with No API key for provider: claude-bridge, and from then on every hcom delivery into that seat failed with Extension sendUserMessage failed, so the seat was dead to the loop; the two worker seats on the same route and the host login were unaffected. So every seat policy denies the task tool (tools.approval.task: deny in home/dot_agents/omp/policies/{orchestrator,worker,audit}.yml, U34 in U36), and the seats do their reading with their own tools. omp refuses the call before the tool runs: tests/unit/test_omp_seat_policy.py OmpTaskDenyLiveTest drives the installed omp against a local fake model that asks for a task call and gets back Tool "task" is blocked by user policy. To allow: remove "tools.approval.task: deny" from config. for each role.

Measured on 2026-10-24 at about 22:10Z (omp 18.11.3, macOS) with omp --no-session -e <tree> --model claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1 --mode json --max-time 240 -p "Use the task tool exactly once to spawn one subagent whose whole job is to reply with the single word PONG, then reply with what it returned.":

  • patches 01-04: the subagent resolved claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1 and failed after 44 ms with No API key found for claude-bridge.; the parent's next turn ended "stopReason":"error", "errorMessage":"No API key for provider: claude-bridge", exit 1;
  • patches 01-05: the subagent answered PONG on claude-bridge/claude-fable-5-1, the parent's final turn ended "stopReason":"stop", exit 0;
  • patches 01-05 with task.agentIdleTtlMs: 3000 in a --config overlay and a prompt that spawns one subagent, runs sleep 15 and spawns a second: the first subagent was parked (disposed) mid-run, which runs the bridge's session_shutdown handler (clearing ACTIVE_STREAM_SIMPLE_KEY in the debug log); the second subagent registered again, both answered, and the run ended stop, exit 0;
  • patches 01-05, one plain Reply with the single word PONG. turn: PONG, stop; the same directory given twice (-e <tree> -e <tree>/, or -e <tree> plus a --config overlay listing it under extensions:) runs the bridge's factory once.

These are print-mode runs. The seat failure ran through hcom delivery into an interactive seat, which these runs do not cover, so the seat policies keep the deny until a seat measurement shows a Task subagent and the next hcom delivery both succeed.

The plain launch (above) loads the bridge through extensions instead of -e and hit the same failure before patch 05: measured 2026-10-25 on macOS with patches 01-04, a plain print-mode session asked to spawn one Task subagent saw the subagent fail in 74 ms with No API key found for claude-bridge. and its own next turn end with No API key for provider: claude-bridge (exit 1). A plain session has no task deny, so the plain-launch extensions key depends on patch 05 being installed (make update installs both).

docs.title: Fallbacks
docs.text:
• anthropic/<model> with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is omp's built-in provider and needs no extension; use it when the bridge cannot load or the login is unavailable.
  • An exported ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL redirects the child Claude Code to that gateway (upstream README), so the bridge seat must not inherit them unless that is intended.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Change pin and sha256 in assets.pi-claude-bridge, run uv run --no-project --with pyyaml scripts/generate-agent-configs.py to render the constants into scripts/update-agent-assets.sh, regenerate bun.lock from the new tarball (bun install --omit=peer --lockfile-only inside its package/), re-check that every patch still applies, and run the load check. An omp upgrade needs no change here unless gap-check.ts reports a MISSING row; then the missing name gets a patch like 01 or 02.

docs.title: Seat logins on a remote host
docs.text: regime-cutover U37. The laptop (macOS: Ghostty, herdr, omp) reaches the Ubuntu host with herdr --remote <ssh-target> over SSH inside the tailnet. omp seats run on Ubuntu, but the Claude and ChatGPT sign-ins end in a browser consent, and the browser is on the laptop. A login is per host: each host signs in once, keeps its own tokens and refreshes them, and nothing copies a token between hosts. SIWC refresh tokens rotate, so one session cannot serve two hosts. The human acts are the consent click and, for Claude, pasting a code.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Route Login record on the seat host Browserless flow ChatGPT (openai-siwc, the audit profile) ~/.omp/profiles/<profile>/agent/openai-siwc/registration.json (host id and issued client id, no token) and the profile's agent.db (tokens) The callback is a 127.0.0.1 loopback, the only redirect SIWC allows. OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT=1455 pins it, and the laptop's LocalForward 1455 127.0.0.1:1455 carries the browser's redirect to the seat host's listener. Claude (claude-bridge, the orchestrator and worker profiles; the bridge child uses the host login) ~/.claude/.credentials.json (0600), or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN claude auth login with BROWSER=regime-open-url. The callback port is random, so the browser shows a code to paste at the prompt. The fallback is claude setup-token on the laptop, with the token stored in ~/.config/claude-code/oauth-token (0600) on the seat host.

The URL reaches the laptop browser through regime-open-url on the seat host. It posts the URL over RemoteForward 127.0.0.1:1456 127.0.0.1:1456 to regime-url-opener, a launchd agent on the laptop, which opens allow-listed sign-in hosts only.

docs.title: Pieces
docs.text:
• home/private_dot_ssh/private_config.tmpl: on macOS only, Match tagged seat-host adds the two forwards. The operator's own host entry in ~/.ssh/conf.d/ carries Tag seat-host, so no machine name enters this public repository (README "Private credentials and keys"). A second session to the same host only warns that a port is taken. The Linux render is the old file, byte for byte.
  • regime-url-opener (laptop, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.mryfmo.dotfiles.url-opener.plist) and regime-open-url (seat host). launchd opens an agent's output files before the program runs, and a fresh home has no log directory, so the agent's stdout and stderr are /dev/null; the opener creates its log's parent itself and records its start, a failed bind and every request there.
  • seat-login-preflight (scripts/orchestrator/, installed to ~/.local/bin/common/, pinned in claude.levers.sha256). With --check it backs the "Seat logins" section of make doctor from metadata only. Given a seat profile (orchestrator, worker or audit), it checks that a seat can use the login: an openai-siwc login stored in the profile's agent.db, counted by the extension's src/credentials.ts without reading a token, and for Claude the variable, the credentials file or the Keychain item, never a token file the shell has not exported. hcom-seat runs it with the seat's role before it creates or starts anything.
  • openai-siwc: OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT and src/seed.ts, which seeds a registration with the laptop's issued client id and a fresh host id, so the ChatGPT account shows one client with one host per machine. The seat host still signs in once.
  • ~/.zshenv and ~/.profile: export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from the token file when it is non-empty, and from nothing else. ~/.zshenv runs in every zsh, not only login shells (it also serves the non-interactive SSH commands that bootstrap Mosh and herdr), so every zsh child process, a Claude Code hook or Bash command included, inherits the variable. The managed Claude settings withhold it from sandboxed commands: sandbox.credentials.envVars denies the variable and sandbox.credentials.files denies the token file, so a sandboxed zsh cannot read it back (U68).

docs.title: Measurements (2026-10-24, this laptop)
docs.text:
• omp 18.11.3 ignores BROWSER. openPath runs open <url> on macOS and xdg-open <url> on Linux (src/utils/open.ts:73-87). omp login prints Open this URL in your browser: and the full URL before it opens anything (src/cli/oauth-terminal.ts:163-176). The CLI login loads extensions from settings only, not from -e: Unknown OAuth provider 'openai-siwc'. A one-command PI_CONFIG_FILES overlay naming the extension works without touching ~/.omp. In a scratch HOME, omp --profile audit login openai-siwc printed an authorize URL with redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A1455%2Fauth%2Fcallback, handed the same URL to the fake open, wrote registration.json with mode 0600, and waited for the callback.
  • Claude Code 2.1.309 honours BROWSER. Three claude auth login runs in scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIRs handed https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize?code=true&… to a fake browser, with redirect_uri=http://localhost:50903/callback, then :50915, then :50920. The port is not fixed, so no forward can carry it, and the paste-code flow is the route.
  • The bridge child never runs in bare mode. grep -rn -- '--bare' over the installed bridge src and the five patches prints nothing, and its only extra CLI arguments are model, strict-mcp-config and thinking-display (src/index.ts, extraArgs).
  • Forwards were measured through a scratch sshd on 127.0.0.1:22337 (user-run, keys and config under $TMPDIR). A request to the client's 21455 reached a server-side listener on 1455, and the far end's 127.0.0.1:21456 reached a client-side listener on 1456. Both ports are shifted on the client side, because one host has one loopback. ssh -O check reported Master running. Match tagged seat-host gave the forwards to the tagged host only. A Unix-socket RemoteForward was mode 0600, but the socket outlived its session and the next bind failed, even with StreamLocalBindUnlink yes on macOS sshd (unix_listener: cannot bind … Address already in use). The TCP form survived three sessions in a row, so it is the one used.
  • herdr 0.9.5 has no API request that opens a given URL on the attached client. pane.link.activate takes a pane cell (pane_id, viewport_row, col), and notification show takes a title, a body and a sound. So the opener is a launchd agent, not a herdr call. herdr --remote runs the system ssh, which reads ~/.ssh/config.
  • Not measured, because each would change the live tailnet: Tailscale SSH carrying -L/-R (tailscale/tailscale #6575 and #5091 reported it did not), and tailscale serve for the opener. The forwards therefore go through OpenSSH over the tailnet. The opener stays a loopback agent behind the RemoteForward: tailscale serve would expose it to every tailnet peer until an ACL in the admin console narrowed it.

docs.title: Threat table
docs.text: Path or control Control Disposition LocalForward 1455 (SIWC callback) Loopback on both ends; only while an SSH session to the tagged host is open; OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT makes the seat's listener fail closed when the port is taken instead of moving to a random port. residual: any local user on the seat host can bind 127.0.0.1:1455 before the seat does and receive the authorization code. That user would also need the PKCE verifier, which only the seat's own process holds, unless the user started the flow themselves (next row). The design assumes a single-user seat host. RemoteForward 1456 and regime-url-opener Loopback only; https only; exact host allow-list; no user info, no port but 443; X-Regime-Open: 1 header (a cross-origin page cannot send it without a CORS preflight, which the server never answers); body of at most 8 KB; open/xdg-open with an argument list, never a shell; a log of every decision with scheme, host and path, never the query. residual: any process on the seat host that reaches 127.0.0.1:1456 while the operator's SSH session is open can make the laptop browser open an allow-listed authorize URL with its own client and challenge. That includes a process of the operator's own account, a yolo omp seat among them (it runs as the operator, and its policy does not stop a loopback POST), as well as a local user on a multi-user seat host. The consent page is the gate, and a returning sign-in may skip it, so such a process could obtain a grant the operator never read (inferred, not exercised); the decision log on the laptop records each opened host and path. Single-user seat host assumed; containing the seats (U85) is what removes the same-account case. regime-open-url Posts to 127.0.0.1 only, with proxies disabled; never logs the URL; on failure the caller has already printed the URL. closed: tests/unit/test_remote_host_logins.py (test_the_client_hands_the_url_to_the_opener, test_no_opener_is_a_named_failure…). ~/.config/claude-code/oauth-token Created by the operator, mode 0600, outside the repository; read by every zsh (~/.zshenv) and by sh and bash login shells (~/.profile), and exported only when non-empty; no seat writes or prints it. Sandboxed Claude Code commands get neither the variable nor the file (sandbox.credentials, U68). residual: once exported, the variable is in every child process of that shell, including the seats, which need it, Claude Code hooks and the two excluded commands git push and gh (each prompts every time), and any other program the operator runs there. That is the vendor's documented mechanism. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is not set: it would also turn sandbox auto-allow off. seat-login-preflight --check and make doctor Metadata only. It reads registration.json (host id and client id, which carry no token), held to the extension's record schema as exactly one JSON document (store.ts reads it with JSON.parse, so concatenated records are unreadable), and never opens agent.db or a credentials file; it checks the Keychain item's attributes only (security find-generic-password -s, no -w/-g). An unreadable or schema-breaking record, and a failed uname, stat, date or security read (other than the Keychain's "not found", exit 44), is a failure, never "absent" or "local". closed: test_an_unreadable_record_is_never_read_as_absent, test_a_failing_jq_with_a_valid_record_is_unreadable_not_absent, test_check_reports_each_claude_route_without_printing_a_token, test_a_record_that_breaks_the_store_schema_is_unreadable_not_registered, test_a_failed_producer_is_unreadable_never_absent_or_local, and the check_seat_logins bats cases. seat-login-preflight <profile> (readiness and logins) Accepts the three seat profiles of omp.roles (orchestrator, worker, audit) and refuses any other name, a deployed overlay or not. A seat starts only on a login it can use: an openai-siwc login counted in agent.db (an issued client is saved before the token exchange, so a record alone proves nothing), and a Claude token in this shell's environment when the token file is the only Claude login. Runs a login only with stdin and stdout on a TTY and HCOM_LAUNCHED unset, so only in the operator's own terminal and never in a seat (standing order 4); elsewhere it refuses with exit 2 and names the command. The opener shims and the overlay live in a mktemp -d directory removed on exit. A failed or ineffective login exits 1, so the seat does not start. closed: test_without_the_operators_terminal_a_missing_login_refuses_and_runs_nothing, test_a_failed_or_ineffective_login_keeps_the_seat_from_starting, test_the_retired_review_and_security_seat_profiles_are_refused_even_with_a_deployed_overlay, test_a_registration_without_a_stored_login_is_not_ready, test_a_token_file_this_shell_has_not_exported_is_refused, test_a_remote_seat_without_a_login_starts_nothing (tests/unit/test_hcom_seat.py). src/credentials.ts (login count) Opens agent.db read-only and selects a count over provider and disabled_cause, never data; a missing database or table counts 0, any other failure exits 2, which the pre-flight reports as unreadable. closed: tests/credentials.test.ts (an unreadable agent.db is an error, never zero, the command prints the count and never the stored data). launchd agent com.mryfmo.dotfiles.url-opener stdout and stderr are /dev/null, which exists on every host, so launchd never needs a log directory a fresh home lacks; the opener creates its log's parent (0700) before it binds and records its start and a failed bind there. closed: test_launchd_starts_the_opener_on_the_loopback_port_and_keeps_it_alive, test_a_fresh_home_gets_the_log_parent_and_the_start_is_recorded, test_a_failed_bind_is_recorded_in_the_log_it_creates. src/seed.ts Never replaces a record; refuses an unreadable one; validates the client id and the profile name; writes the record 0600 in a 0700 directory through the store. closed: tests/seed.test.ts. Match tagged seat-host (~/.ssh/config) macOS only; applies only to a host entry the operator tags; the Linux render is unchanged. closed: SshForwardTest. residual: needs an OpenSSH client that knows Tag and Match tagged (measured with OpenSSH_10.3p1).

docs.title: Nix-first architecture plan
docs.text:
Note (2026-10-04): the Nix flake was removed in #247; the commands and paths below no longer apply.

This document describes the intended direction for an optional Nix layer in this dotfiles repository. It is a plan, not the default bootstrap path.

docs.title: Current authority model
docs.text:
• setup.sh and chezmoi remain the default and authoritative bootstrap path.
  • Public dotfiles under home/ remain managed by chezmoi.
  • Private dotfiles and secrets remain outside this repository in the private chezmoi source.
  • The new Nix files are opt-in and should not change existing machines unless a user explicitly runs Home Manager or nix-darwin commands.

docs.title: Initial Nix scope
docs.text:
The initial scaffold provides:

  • A flake with Home Manager standalone outputs:
  • mryfmo-linux
  • mryfmo-darwin
  • A nix-darwin output:
  • mryfmo-mac
  • A shared conservative package list based mostly on the existing mise, apt, and Homebrew bootstrap intent.
  • A development shell with Nix-related tooling.
  • A formatter output for nix fmt.

The initial Home Manager module intentionally manages only packages and Home Manager metadata. It must not define home.file or xdg.configFile for paths already represented in home/, because those files are currently owned by chezmoi.

docs.title: Package ownership
docs.text:
Near-term package ownership can be split as follows:

  • Chezmoi remains responsible for configuration files, scripts, and templates.
  • Nix may install a conservative base toolset such as Git, GnuPG, Vim, Zsh, tmux, CMake, jq, yq, fd, eza, uv, ShellCheck, shfmt, Starship, chezmoi, age, GitHub CLI, Rust via rustup, Node.js, Python 3.11, ripgrep, yazi, and AWS CLI when available.
  • Existing mise usage may continue for project-local language versions and tools that are not yet migrated. If both Nix and mise provide Rust, Node.js, or Python, mise remains the project-specific version selector while Nix provides only the baseline interactive toolchain. Go is intentionally not part of the default Nix package set.

AWS CLI ownership is explicit:

  • Default macOS: Homebrew owns the AWS CLI version and installation integrity. Repository snapshot pinning for Homebrew is outside Plan004's scope.
  • Default Ubuntu: the signed AWS archive installer owns the user-local installation.
  • Opt-in Nix activation: awscli2 owns the active AWS CLI on PATH. Deactivating Nix returns AWS CLI ownership to the operating-system default.
  • Chezmoi never mutates the Nix store.

docs.title: Future target
docs.text:
A fuller Nix-first design may eventually move these areas into Nix after explicit migration decisions:

  • Language toolchains and developer CLIs currently installed by mise.
  • macOS package declarations currently installed manually or through Homebrew.
  • Linux packages currently installed through apt scripts.
  • Machine roles such as client, server, or work-specific hosts.

Configuration files should move from chezmoi to Home Manager only after collision risks are resolved and rollback behavior is documented.

docs.title: Activation examples
docs.text:
Home Manager standalone on Linux:

nix run github:nix-community/home-manager/release-26.05 -- switch --flake .#mryfmo-linux

Home Manager standalone on Apple Silicon macOS:

nix run github:nix-community/home-manager/release-26.05 -- switch --flake .#mryfmo-darwin

nix-darwin on Apple Silicon macOS:

sudo darwin-rebuild switch --flake .#mryfmo-mac

Evaluate without activation:

nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file
nix eval --no-update-lock-file .#homeConfigurations.mryfmo-linux.activationPackage.drvPath
nix eval --no-update-lock-file .#homeConfigurations.mryfmo-darwin.activationPackage.drvPath
nix eval --no-update-lock-file .#darwinConfigurations.mryfmo-mac.system.drvPath

The nix-darwin configuration enables Homebrew management, but homebrew.enable does not install Homebrew itself. Install Homebrew before activating nix-darwin if Homebrew management is needed.

docs.title: Non-goals for the initial scaffold
docs.text:
• Keep setup.sh in place.
  • Avoid migrating existing files under home/ into Home Manager.
  • Exclude private secrets, host-specific credentials, SSH keys, GnuPG secret keyrings, or VPN profiles.
  • Retain chezmoi as the default source of truth.

docs.title: Nix migration
docs.text: Historical document (moved 2026-10-05, dotfiles-T99); the AWS CLI ownership statements remain current and are pinned by tests/unit/test_aws_cli_acquisition.py.

docs.title: Nix migration plan
docs.text:
Note (2026-10-04): the Nix flake was removed in #247; the commands and paths below no longer apply.

This plan keeps Nix optional while introducing a path toward reproducible package and host management.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Preserve existing behavior by default.
  2. setup.sh remains the normal bootstrap entry point.
  3. chezmoi apply remains authoritative for files in home/.
  4. Keep public and private state separate.
  5. Public dotfiles stay in this repository.
  6. Private files and secrets stay in the private chezmoi source or on the target host.
  7. Avoid file ownership collisions.
  8. Do not add Home Manager home.file or xdg.configFile entries for existing chezmoi-managed paths until they are deliberately migrated.
  9. Make every migration reversible.
  10. Document the owner of each migrated package or config path.
  11. Prefer small changes that can be rolled back independently.

docs.title: Phase 0: Opt-in scaffold
docs.text:
Status: initial implementation.

  • Add flake.nix.
  • Add a shared package module at nix/shared/packages.nix.
  • Add a minimal Home Manager module at nix/home-manager/default.nix.
  • Add a minimal nix-darwin module at nix/nix-darwin/default.nix.
  • Add documentation describing architecture and migration rules.

Validation target:

nix fmt --no-update-lock-file
nix flake show --no-update-lock-file
nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file

If Nix is unavailable on a machine, CI evaluates every declared output on Linux and macOS. Never hand-edit flake.lock; regenerate it with nix flake lock.

AWS CLI follows the ownership boundary in the architecture plan: Homebrew owns the default macOS installation, the signed user-local installer owns the default Ubuntu installation, and opt-in Nix activation puts Nix awscli2 first on PATH. Deactivating Nix restores the operating-system default, and chezmoi never mutates the Nix store. Homebrew repository snapshot pinning remains outside Plan004's scope.

docs.title: Phase 1: Package-only adoption
docs.text:
Goal: use Nix to install common packages without changing dotfile ownership.

Candidate packages:

  • Core: git, gnupg, vim, zsh, tmux, cmake
  • CLI data tools: jq, yq
  • Search and listing tools: fd, eza, ripgrep
  • Development helpers: uv, shellcheck, shfmt, starship, chezmoi, age, gh
  • Language runtimes: rustup, nodejs, python311
  • Optional tools: yazi, awscli2 when available

Acceptance criteria:

  • Home Manager standalone activation does not overwrite existing dotfiles.
  • nix-darwin activation does not assume Homebrew is already installed beyond documented behavior.
  • Existing chezmoi commands continue to work before and after Nix activation.

docs.title: Phase 2: Host roles and package ownership
docs.text:
Goal: make package sets explicit by host or role.

Possible role modules:

  • common
  • linux-client
  • linux-server
  • darwin-client
  • work

Each role should document whether a package is owned by Nix, mise, apt, Homebrew, or another installer.

docs.title: Phase 3: Selective config migration
docs.text:
Goal: migrate selected dotfile paths to Home Manager only when there is a clear benefit.

Before migrating a path:

  1. Identify the current chezmoi source path under home/.
  2. Confirm whether private chezmoi overlays or templates affect the same target path.
  3. Remove or disable the chezmoi source for that path in the same change that adds Home Manager ownership.
  4. Document rollback steps.

Paths that should not be migrated early:

  • SSH private material
  • GnuPG secret keyrings
  • VPN credentials
  • Any host-specific or work-specific secret

docs.title: Phase 4: Optional Nix-first bootstrap
docs.text:
Goal: provide a Nix-first bootstrap path for users who explicitly choose it.

This should remain separate from setup.sh unless the repository owner decides to change the default bootstrap model. A future bootstrap may install Nix, activate Home Manager or nix-darwin, and then run chezmoi for public and private dotfiles.

docs.title: Rollback notes
docs.text:
Home Manager standalone rollback is generally handled with Home Manager generations. nix-darwin rollback is handled with system generations. Package-only changes should be low risk, but any future file ownership migration must include explicit rollback instructions because ownership collisions can block activation or overwrite expected state.

Useful rollback entry points:

home-manager generations
home-manager switch --rollback
sudo darwin-rebuild --rollback

For flake input regressions, revert the Git commit that changed flake.nix or flake.lock, then re-run the relevant Home Manager or nix-darwin switch command.

docs.title: home/dot_claude/hooks/executable_enforce-uv.sh
docs.text: Emit PreToolUse permissionDecision deny for direct pip or python usage; other input exits successfully without output. Contract verified 2026-10-05. Advisory, not a boundary: it nudges toward uv. A Bash line is parsed by shfmt (on PATH from the mise config) into its syntax tree, and every simple command in it is judged on its own text. shfmt's JSON must match the pinned node table of scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py (regime-cutover U105). Every read of a producer keeps its three outcomes apart (standing order 21): what it found is judged; an empty result (a line with no simple command) is no decision, exit 0 without output; a failed read is a blocking error, exit 2 with the probe and the status on stderr, never a silent "no decision". Failed reads: no shfmt on PATH, shfmt exiting nonzero (a line it cannot parse included), a JSON that does not match the table, jq exiting nonzero or printing another shape or another number of lines than the probe has, a tree whose statements the walk cannot see, a chezmoi source-path that exits nonzero or names no directory. The one fail-open left is a deployed copy that finds no contract module (contract_module): no chezmoi on PATH, or none under the source directory it names; it decides nothing, exit 0.

docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

# @file home/dot_claude/hooks/executable_enforce-uv.sh
# @brief Block direct Python and pip commands in favor of `uv`.
# @description
#   Emit PreToolUse permissionDecision deny for direct `pip` or `python` usage;
#   other input exits successfully without output. Contract verified 2026-10-05.
#   Advisory, not a boundary: it nudges toward uv. A Bash line is parsed by shfmt (on PATH from the mise config)
#   into its syntax tree, and every simple command in it is judged on its own text. shfmt's JSON must match the
#   pinned node table of scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py (regime-cutover U105). Every read of a producer keeps
#   its three outcomes apart (standing order 21): what it found is judged; an empty result (a line with no simple
#   command) is no decision, exit 0 without output; a failed read is a blocking error, exit 2 with the probe and
#   the status on stderr, never a silent "no decision". Failed reads: no shfmt on PATH, shfmt exiting nonzero (a
#   line it cannot parse included), a JSON that does not match the table, jq exiting nonzero or printing another
#   shape or another number of lines than the probe has, a tree whose statements the walk cannot see, a `chezmoi
#   source-path` that exits nonzero or names no directory. The one fail-open left is a deployed copy that finds no
#   contract module (contract_module): no chezmoi on PATH, or none under the source directory it names; it decides
#   nothing, exit 0.
# @see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#pretooluse-decision-control

# @description Encode the denial reason from stdin using the current hook contract.
# @stdout PreToolUse deny JSON with the original multiline reason.
function deny_command() {
    jq -Rsc '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "deny", permissionDecisionReason: rtrimstr("\n")}}'
}

# @description Emit the `uv` replacement message for `pip install`.
# @arg $1 string Parsed `pip` subcommand beginning with `install`.
function handle_pip_install() {
    local pip_cmd="$1"
    local packages
    packages=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed 's/install//' | sed 's/--[^ ]*//g' | xargs)

    # -r requirements.txt
    if [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ -r\ .*\.txt ]]; then
        local req_file
        req_file=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed -n 's/.*-r \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')
        deny_command <<- EOF
        📋 requirements.txtからインストール:

        ✅ 推奨方法:
        uv add -r $req_file

        これにより:
        • requirements.txt内のすべての依存関係をpyproject.tomlに追加
        • uv.lockファイルを自動生成/更新
        • 仮想環境を自動的に同期

        💡 制約ファイルがある場合:
        uv add -r $req_file -c constraints.txt

        📌 注意: この方法が最も確実で、バージョン指定も正しく処理されます
        EOF
        exit 0
    fi

    # 開発依存関係
    if [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ --dev ]] || [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ -e ]]; then
        deny_command <<- EOF
        🔧 開発依存関係をインストール:

        uv add --dev $packages

        編集可能インストール: uv add -e .
        EOF
        exit 0
    fi

    # 通常のインストール
    deny_command <<- EOF
    📦 パッケージをインストール:

    uv add $packages

    💾 'uv add' はpyproject.tomlに依存関係を保存します
    🔒 uv.lockで再現可能な環境を保証

    💡 特殊なケース:
    • URLからのインストール: パッケージを手動でダウンロードしてから追加
    • 開発版: uv add --dev $packages
    • ローカルパッケージ: uv add -e ./path/to/package
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Emit the `uv remove` replacement message for `pip uninstall`.
# @arg $1 string Parsed `pip` subcommand beginning with `uninstall`.
function handle_pip_uninstall() {
    local pip_cmd="$1"
    local packages
    packages=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed 's/uninstall//' | sed 's/-y//g' | xargs)
    deny_command <<- EOF
    🗑️ パッケージを削除:

    uv remove $packages

    ✨ 依存関係も自動的にクリーンアップされます
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Explain the `uv` alternatives for `pip list` and `pip freeze`.
function handle_pip_list() {
    deny_command <<- 'EOF'
    📊 パッケージ一覧を確認:

    • プロジェクト依存関係: cat pyproject.toml
    • ロックファイル詳細: cat uv.lock
    • インストール済み一覧: uv tree
    • requirements.txt形式でエクスポート: uv export --format requirements-txt

    💡 'uv tree'はプロジェクトの依存関係ツリーを表示します
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Fall back to a generic `uv` recommendation for other pip commands.
# @arg $1 string Parsed `pip` subcommand.
function handle_pip_other() {
    local pip_cmd="$1"
    deny_command <<- EOF
    🔀 pipコマンドをuvで実行:

    uv $pip_cmd

    💡 パッケージのインストール/削除には 'uv add/remove' を使用してください
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Handle `python -m pip ...` by mapping it to the right `uv` advice.
# @arg $1 string Parsed module arguments after `python -m pip`.
function handle_python_m_pip() {
    local pip_cmd="$1"

    # Parse pip install commands
    if [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ ^install ]]; then
        local packages
        packages=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed 's/install//' | sed 's/--[^ ]*//g' | xargs)
        if [[ "$pip_cmd" =~ -r\ .*\.txt ]]; then
            local req_file
            req_file=$(echo "$pip_cmd" | sed -n 's/.*-r \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')
            deny_command <<- EOF
            📋 requirements.txtからインストール:

            ✅ 推奨方法:
            uv add -r $req_file

            💡 これによりすべての依存関係がpyproject.tomlに追加されます
            EOF
        else
            deny_command <<- EOF
            📦 パッケージをインストール:

            uv add $packages

            💡 'uv add' はpyproject.tomlに依存関係を保存します
            EOF
        fi
    else
        deny_command <<- EOF
        🔀 pipコマンドをuvで実行:

        uv $pip_cmd

        💡 パッケージ管理には 'uv add/remove' を使用してください
        EOF
    fi
    exit 0
}

# @description Rewrite `python -m module` invocations to `uv run`.
# @arg $1 string Module invocation after `python -m`.
function handle_python_m_module() {
    local module="$1"
    deny_command <<- EOF
    uvでモジュールを実行:

    uv run python -m $module

    🔄 uvは自動的に環境を同期してから実行します。
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Rewrite direct Python execution to `uv run`.
# @arg $1 string The simple command as written (interpreter and arguments, quotes kept).
function handle_python_run() {
    local segment="$1"
    deny_command <<- EOF
    uvでPythonを実行:

    uv run $segment

    ✅ 仮想環境のアクティベーションは不要です！
    EOF
    exit 0
}

# @description Find scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py: relative to this file in the dotfiles checkout
#   (home/dot_claude/hooks/), else under the chezmoi source directory the deployed copy came from. The source-path
#   read keeps its three outcomes (regime-cutover U105 round 6): no chezmoi on PATH is an absence, a directory it
#   names is searched (the module there is found, or absent), and a nonzero status, no path, several lines, a
#   relative path or a path that is no directory is a failed read, named in REFUSAL for main to report (exit 2).
# @set MODULE string On return 0, the module path; empty otherwise.
# @set REFUSAL string On return 2, why the line cannot be judged.
# @exitcode 0 Found.
# @exitcode 1 No module beside this file, and no chezmoi on PATH or no module under the directory it names: the fail-open.
# @exitcode 2 chezmoi source-path exited nonzero or printed no directory.
function contract_module() {
    local here source status=0
    case ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} in
    */*) here=${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*} ;;
    *) here=. ;;
    esac
    MODULE="${here}/../../../scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py"
    [[ -f ${MODULE} ]] && return 0
    MODULE=""
    command -v chezmoi > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    source=$(chezmoi source-path) || status=$?
    read_or_refuse "chezmoi source-path naming the source directory" "$status" "$source" '^/' "an absolute path" one || return 2
    if [[ ! -d ${source} ]]; then
        REFUSAL="chezmoi source-path named '${source}', which is no directory; the line cannot be judged"
        return 2
    fi
    MODULE="${source}/../scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py"
    [[ -f ${MODULE} ]] && return 0
    MODULE=""
    return 1
}

# @description Judge one probe's read of a producer. The status, the shape of every non-empty output line and the
#   number of such lines are checked: a status 0 with lines of the given shape, as many as the probe has, is a found
#   result; a status 0 without output is an empty one where the probe allows it; anything else is a failed read,
#   named in REFUSAL for main to report (exit 2).
# @arg $1 string The probe, as the refusal names it ("jq counting the statements the tree lists").
# @arg $2 int The tool's exit status.
# @arg $3 string The tool's output.
# @arg $4 string An extended regular expression every non-empty output line must match.
# @arg $5 string What a line of that shape is called ("a count").
# @arg $6 string The cardinality of a found result: `one` (exactly one line, as a count or a path is printed: none
#   or several is a failed read, never an empty result) or `any` (zero or more lines, as offset pairs are; none is
#   the empty result).
# @set REFUSAL string On return 2, why the line cannot be judged.
# @exitcode 0 Found or empty.
# @exitcode 2 A failed read.
function read_or_refuse() {
    local probe="$1" status="$2" output="$3" shape="$4" called="$5" cardinality="$6" row lines=0
    if ((status != 0)); then
        REFUSAL="${probe} exited ${status}; the line cannot be judged"
        return 2
    fi
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        [[ -n "$row" ]] || continue
        if [[ ! "$row" =~ $shape ]]; then
            REFUSAL="${probe} printed '${row}', not ${called}; the line cannot be judged"
            return 2
        fi
        lines=$((lines + 1))
    done <<< "$output"
    if [[ ${cardinality} == one ]] && ((lines == 0)); then
        REFUSAL="${probe} printed nothing, not ${called}; the line cannot be judged"
        return 2
    elif [[ ${cardinality} == one ]] && ((lines > 1)); then
        REFUSAL="${probe} printed ${lines} lines, not ${called}; the line cannot be judged"
        return 2
    fi
}

# @description Collect the simple commands of a Bash line from shfmt's syntax tree (`shfmt -ln bash --to-json`):
#   every statement whose command is a call (`CallExpr`), in tree order, nested ones (in a pipeline, a list, a
#   subshell, `$(...)`) included, each as its source text from the statement's start to its end offset, so the
#   suggestion keeps its quotes and redirections. Comments and here-document bodies are no statements, and quoting,
#   escapes and line continuations are shfmt's, not this script's. Before the walk, the contract module proves the
#   parser still produces these nodes; a line whose tree lists statements the walk then cannot see is refused too.
#   Each probe's three outcomes (regime-cutover U105 rounds 5 and 6); a failed read is named by read_or_refuse,
#   contract_module or here:
#   | probe                                | found           | empty                           | failed read (return 2)                     |
#   | command -v shfmt                     | a path          |                                 | no shfmt on PATH                           |
#   | shfmt -ln bash --to-json on the line | the tree        |                                 | nonzero status (a parse error too), no tree |
#   | contract_module: beside this file    | the module path | none: chezmoi is asked          |                                            |
#   | contract_module: chezmoi source-path | one directory   | no chezmoi on PATH: return 1    | nonzero status, no path, several lines, a  |
#   |                                      |                 | (open); a directory without the | relative path, a path that is no directory |
#   |                                      |                 | module: return 1 (open)         |                                            |
#   | python3 -I on the module (contract)  | status 0        |                                 | 2: the JSON does not match; other: named   |
#   | jq: statements the tree lists        | one count       | 0                               | nonzero status, no count, several, no digit|
#   | jq: statement nodes the walk sees    | one count       | 0 (refused when any was listed) | nonzero status, no count, several, no digit|
#   | jq: the call statements' offsets     | start-end lines | none: no segment, no decision   | nonzero status, or a line of another shape |
# @arg $1 string The command line.
# @set SEGMENTS array The simple commands, in order.
# @set REFUSAL string On return 2, why the line cannot be judged.
# @exitcode 0 The line parsed; SEGMENTS holds its simple commands, possibly none.
# @exitcode 1 No contract module beside this file, and no chezmoi on PATH or none under its source directory: the fail-open.
# @exitcode 2 A failed read (chezmoi source-path included), a contract mismatch, or a tree whose statements the walk cannot see: main exits 2.
function split_segments() {
    local line="$1" tree spans start end listed visited status found=0
    SEGMENTS=()
    REFUSAL=""
    if ! command -v shfmt > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        REFUSAL="shfmt is not on PATH, so no Bash line can be judged; home/dot_mise/config.toml installs the pinned one"
        return 2
    fi
    tree=$(printf '%s' "$line" | shfmt -ln bash --to-json)
    read_or_refuse "shfmt parsing the line" "$?" "" "" "" any || return 2
    if [[ -z "$tree" ]]; then
        REFUSAL="shfmt printed no tree for the line; the line cannot be judged"
        return 2
    fi
    contract_module || found=$?
    ((found == 0)) || return "$found"
    python3 -I "$MODULE"
    status=$?
    if ((status == 2)); then
        REFUSAL="shfmt's JSON does not match the pinned node table; no Bash line can be judged"
        return 2
    elif ((status != 0)); then
        REFUSAL="python3 -I ${MODULE} exited ${status} proving the contract; the line cannot be judged"
        return 2
    fi
    # The statements the tree lists against the statement nodes the walk can see: a renamed field would leave the
    # walk empty and the line silently undecided.
    listed=$(jq -r '.Stmts // [] | length' <<< "$tree")
    read_or_refuse "jq counting the statements the tree lists" "$?" "$listed" '^[0-9]+$' "a count" one || return 2
    visited=$(jq -r '[.. | objects | select(has("Cmd"))] | length' <<< "$tree")
    read_or_refuse "jq counting the statement nodes the walk sees" "$?" "$visited" '^[0-9]+$' "a count" one || return 2
    if ((listed > 0 && visited == 0)); then
        REFUSAL="shfmt's tree lists ${listed} statement(s) but the walk saw none; the line cannot be judged"
        return 2
    fi
    spans=$(jq -r '.. | objects | select(.Cmd.Type? == "CallExpr") | "\(.Pos.Offset) \(.End.Offset)"' <<< "$tree")
    read_or_refuse "jq reading the call statements' offsets" "$?" "$spans" '^[0-9]+ [0-9]+$' "an offset pair" any || return 2
    # shfmt's offsets count bytes, so slice the line byte-wise.
    local LC_ALL=C
    while read -r start end; do
        if [[ -n "$start" && -n "$end" ]]; then
            SEGMENTS+=("${line:start:end-start}")
        fi
    done <<< "$spans"
}

# @description Emit the deny for one simple command that runs pip or Python directly; return for any other.
# @arg $1 string One simple command.
function classify_segment() {
    local segment="$1"
    case "$segment" in
    # ===== pip関連コマンド =====
    pip\ * | pip3\ *)
        # pipコマンドの詳細な解析
        local pip_cmd
        pip_cmd=$(echo "$segment" | sed -E 's/^pip[0-9]? *//' | xargs)

        case "$pip_cmd" in
        install\ *)
            handle_pip_install "$pip_cmd"
            ;;
        uninstall\ *)
            handle_pip_uninstall "$pip_cmd"
            ;;
        list* | freeze*)
            handle_pip_list
            ;;
        *)
            handle_pip_other "$pip_cmd"
            ;;
        esac
        ;;

    # ===== 直接的なPython実行の処理 =====
    python* | py\ *)
        # -m オプションの特別処理
        local args
        args=$(echo "$segment" | sed -E 's/^python[0-9]? //' | xargs 2> /dev/null)
        if [[ "$args" =~ ^-m ]]; then
            local module
            module=${args/-m /}

            case "$module" in
            pip\ *)
                local pip_cmd
                pip_cmd=${module/pip /}
                handle_python_m_pip "$pip_cmd"
                ;;
            *)
                handle_python_m_module "$module"
                ;;
            esac
        fi

        # 基本的なPython実行: the command as written, so `python3 -c 'print(1)'` keeps its quotes.
        handle_python_run "$segment"
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Read hook input JSON, classify each simple command of a Bash call, and emit a decision.
function main() {
    local input
    input=$(cat)

    # Validate input
    if [ -z "$input" ]; then
        exit 0
    fi

    # Extract fields with error handling
    local tool_name
    tool_name=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_name' 2> /dev/null || echo "")
    local command
    command=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""' 2> /dev/null || echo "")

    if [[ "$tool_name" == "Bash" ]]; then
        local segment parsed=0
        split_segments "$command" || parsed=$?
        # 1 is the one fail-open: no contract module on this host, so no decision. Any other failure is a refusal,
        # reported the way a contract mismatch is: the tool call is blocked and the reason reaches the caller.
        if ((parsed == 1)); then
            exit 0
        elif ((parsed != 0)); then
            echo "enforce-uv: ${REFUSAL}" >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        for segment in "${SEGMENTS[@]}"; do
            classify_segment "$segment"
        done
    fi

    exit 0
}

main

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Format files reported by Claude Code hook JSON input.

The hook reads the complete JSON event from stdin, extracts every edited file path
from the Write and Edit payload shapes, filters by suffix, and runs the
formatter for that suffix without going through a shell. ruff and prettier come
from PATH: the versions home/dot_mise/config.toml pins for make format and CI (U97), and
ruff.toml and .prettierignore keep vendored and record paths untouched.

The hook runs outside the Claude sandbox, so it never loads configuration that a
sandboxed command could have written as code: prettier runs with --no-config
(a prettier.config.js, .prettierrc.js or plugin in the edited tree is ignored and
the built-in defaults apply). ruff reads only TOML, which is data.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

PYTHON_COMMANDS = [
    ["ruff", "format"],
]
MARKDOWN_COMMANDS = [
    # --no-config: project prettier configs may be JavaScript, and plugins they name are code.
    ["prettier", "--write", "--no-config"],
]


def collect_paths(value: Any) -> set[Path]:
    paths: set[Path] = set()
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key, item in value.items():
            if key in {"file_path", "path"} and isinstance(item, str):
                paths.add(Path(item))
            else:
                paths.update(collect_paths(item))
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for item in value:
            paths.update(collect_paths(item))
    return paths


def repository_root(path: Path) -> Path:
    """The git work tree containing path, else its directory: where the formatter configs live."""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(path.parent), "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return path.parent
    root = result.stdout.rstrip("\n")
    return Path(root) if result.returncode == 0 and root else path.parent


def run_commands(commands: list[list[str]], files: list[Path]) -> int:
    status = 0
    # Run from each file's repository root: prettier reads .prettierignore from
    # its working directory, and the session's directory may be another tree.
    by_root: dict[Path, list[str]] = {}
    for path in files:
        resolved = path.resolve()
        by_root.setdefault(repository_root(resolved), []).append(str(resolved))
    for root, file_args in sorted(by_root.items()):
        for command in commands:
            config = root / "ruff.toml"
            if command[0] == "ruff" and config.is_file():
                # Pin the root config: ruff otherwise picks each file's nearest
                # pyproject.toml (vendor/compactiondb) and skips the root exclusions.
                command = [*command, "--config", str(config)]
            try:
                result = subprocess.run(command + file_args, cwd=root, check=False)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                # make update installs every declared mise tool, so a missing formatter means that step was skipped or failed.
                print(
                    f"{command[0]} is not installed; run `make update` (it installs every declared mise tool)",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
                status = max(status, 1)
                continue
            status = max(status, result.returncode)
    return status


def main() -> int:
    raw = sys.stdin.read()
    if not raw.strip():
        return 0
    try:
        payload = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
        print(f"failed to parse Claude hook input: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0

    paths = sorted(path for path in collect_paths(payload.get("tool_input", payload)) if path.exists())
    python_files = [path for path in paths if path.suffix == ".py"]
    markdown_files = [path for path in paths if path.suffix == ".md"]

    status = 0
    status = max(status, run_commands(PYTHON_COMMANDS, python_files))
    status = max(status, run_commands(MARKDOWN_COMMANDS, markdown_files))
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/bin/bash

# @file home/dot_claude/hooks/executable_project-map-reload.sh
# @brief Reload the visible project map after a Claude file edit.
# @description
#   Pass CDP on both calls to avoid terminal-browser issue 60.
#   Pin tab selection and guard reloads against navigation away from a project map.
#   Match the event file path before choosing an existing map tab.
#   Canonicalize event paths and file URLs with the installed isolated Python stdlib.
#   Reject encoded URL separators before decoding them into filesystem paths.
#   Bind the reload guard to the canonical-matched URL, encoded as a JSON string.
#   Open a separate right split using half the width when the parsed listing yields no map tab.
#   shortcut: rejected map metadata or racing writes can open another pane; tighten selection in the hook follow-up.
# @exitcode 0 Always, including unavailable tools or browsers.

# @description Return the physical absolute path of a local path or file URL.
# @arg $1 path Event path or file URL, including home and relative forms.
# @stdout Canonical path.
canonical_path() {
    python3 -I -S -c '
import os
import sys
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit

path = sys.argv[1]
if path.startswith("file://"):
    url = urlsplit(path)
    if url.netloc not in ("", "localhost") or "%2f" in url.path.lower():
        sys.exit(1)
    path = unquote(url.path, errors="strict")
if path == "~" or path.startswith("~/"):
    path = os.path.expanduser("~") + path[1:]
print(os.path.realpath(path))
' "$1" 2> /dev/null
}

file_path=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty' 2> /dev/null) || exit 0
[[ -n "$file_path" ]] || exit 0
event_path=$(canonical_path "$file_path") || exit 0
[[ "$event_path" == */.project-map/index.html ]] || exit 0

listing=$(terminal-browser ls --all --json 2> /dev/null) || exit 0
candidates=$(jq -c '
    [.browsers[]? | .cdpPort as $port
     | select($port | type == "number")
     | select($port >= 1 and $port <= 65535 and $port == ($port | floor))
     | .tabs[]?
     | select(.url | strings | startswith("file://"))
     | select(.targetId | strings | test("^[A-Fa-f0-9]{32}\\z"))
     | [$port, .targetId, .url]][]
' <<< "$listing" 2> /dev/null) || exit 0
selection=""
while IFS= read -r candidate; do
    [[ -n "$candidate" ]] || continue
    tab_path=$(canonical_path "$(jq -r '.[2]' <<< "$candidate")") || continue
    [[ "$tab_path" == "$event_path" ]] || continue
    selection=$(jq -r '.[0:2] | @tsv' <<< "$candidate")
    selected_url=$(jq -c '.[2]' <<< "$candidate")
    break
done <<< "$candidates"
if [[ -z "$selection" ]]; then
    terminal-browser open "$file_path" --split right --size 0.5 --no-merge > /dev/null 2>&1
    exit 0
fi
IFS=$'\t' read -r port target_id <<< "$selection"

agent="${TERMINAL_BROWSER_AGENT:-$HOME/.local/share/terminal-browser/app/agent-browser/bin/agent-browser}"
"$agent" --cdp "$port" --session project-map-reload --pin-tab tab "$target_id" > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
"$agent" --cdp "$port" --session project-map-reload --pin-tab eval "if (location.href === new URL($selected_url).href) location.reload()" > /dev/null 2>&1
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_config/alias/common.sh
# @brief Shared shell aliases used across machines.
# @description
#   These aliases wrap common repository and local workflow commands.

# Use eza for ls command. In eza 0.23.5 `--icons` takes an optional WHEN value,
# so the bare flag swallows the first path argument and `ls dir` fails.
alias ls="eza --long --group --header --binary --time-style=long-iso --icons=auto"

# Alias for private chezmoi configuration
# ref. https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/frequently-asked-questions/design/#can-chezmoi-support-multiple-sources-or-multiple-source-states
alias chezmoi-private="chezmoi --source ~/.local/share/chezmoi-private --config ~/.config/chezmoi-private/chezmoi.yaml"

# Alias to checkout the default branch in git
alias gm='git checkout $(git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD | sed "s@^refs/remotes/origin/@@")'

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Approximate session staleness from public managed-asset mtimes.

This command never reads undocumented harness or session state. It compares a
caller-provided session epoch with public plugin-cache directories, managed
asset roots, and rendered settings. Detection is intentionally approximate.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import re
import signal
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator

# The SessionStart hook runs synchronously with a 3 s timeout (agent-config.yaml); the
# scan stops here first and exits 0 without output. Measured runtime: about 0.04 s.
WALL_LIMIT_S = 2
MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES = 10_000
MAX_HOOK_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024
MAX_STATE_FILES = 1_000
MAX_OUTPUT_LINES = 5
STATE_MAX_AGE_S = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60
EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES = {
    ".git",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".venv",
    "__pycache__",
    "health",
    "spool",
    "state",
}
MANAGED_ROOTS = (
    ("compactiondb", Path(".agents/compactiondb")),
    ("skills", Path(".agents/skills")),
    ("plugins", Path(".agents/plugins")),
)

Update = tuple[float, str, Path]


class QuietParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message: str) -> None:
        raise ValueError(message)


def version_key(version: str) -> tuple[tuple[int, int | str], ...]:
    return tuple((0, int(token)) if token.isdigit() else (1, token.lower()) for token in re.split(r"(\d+)", version))


def display_path(path: Path, home: Path) -> str:
    try:
        return "~/" + str(path.relative_to(home))
    except ValueError:
        return str(path)


def excluded(path: Path, home: Path) -> bool:
    relative = path.relative_to(home)
    if any(part in EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES for part in relative.parts):
        return True
    return ".sqlite" in path.name.lower()


def scan_files(root: Path, home: Path, deadline: float) -> Iterator[tuple[Path, float]]:
    if not root.is_dir():
        return
    pending = [root]
    scanned = 0
    while pending:
        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            raise TimeoutError("managed asset scan exceeded 5 seconds")
        directory = pending.pop()
        with os.scandir(directory) as entries:
            for entry in entries:
                scanned += 1
                # ponytail: bounded scan favors hook latency; raise only if 10k entries miss real updates.
                if scanned > MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES:
                    return
                path = Path(entry.path)
                if excluded(path, home):
                    continue
                if entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
                    pending.append(path)
                elif entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False) or entry.is_symlink():
                    yield path, entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_mtime


def plugin_cache_updates(home: Path, since: float | None, deadline: float) -> list[Update]:
    cache = home / ".claude/plugins/cache"
    if not cache.is_dir():
        return []
    updates: list[Update] = []
    scanned = 0
    for marketplace in os.scandir(cache):
        if not marketplace.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
            continue
        for plugin in os.scandir(marketplace.path):
            if not plugin.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
                continue
            versions: list[tuple[str, float, Path]] = []
            for version in os.scandir(plugin.path):
                scanned += 1
                if scanned > MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    raise TimeoutError("plugin cache scan exceeded its bound")
                if version.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
                    stat_result = version.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
                    versions.append((version.name, stat_result.st_mtime, Path(version.path)))
            if since is None:
                updates.extend(
                    (mtime, f"claude-plugin:{marketplace.name}/{plugin.name}", path) for _, mtime, path in versions
                )
                continue
            highest = max(versions, key=lambda item: version_key(item[0]), default=None)
            older = [item for item in versions if item[1] <= since]
            baseline = max(older, key=lambda item: version_key(item[0]), default=None)
            if (
                highest
                and highest[1] > since
                and (baseline is None or version_key(highest[0]) > version_key(baseline[0]))
            ):
                updates.append(
                    (
                        highest[1],
                        f"claude-plugin:{marketplace.name}/{plugin.name}",
                        highest[2],
                    )
                )
    return updates


def collect_updates(home: Path, since: float | None, deadline: float) -> list[Update]:
    updates = plugin_cache_updates(home, since, deadline)
    for label, relative_root in MANAGED_ROOTS:
        for path, mtime in scan_files(home / relative_root, home, deadline):
            if since is None or mtime > since:
                updates.append((mtime, label, path))
    settings = [("claude-settings", home / ".claude/settings.json")]
    codex_root = home / ".codex"
    if codex_root.is_dir():
        settings.extend(("codex-settings", path) for path in codex_root.glob("*.toml"))
    for label, path in settings:
        if path.is_file():
            mtime = path.stat().st_mtime
            if since is None or mtime > since:
                updates.append((mtime, label, path))
    return updates


def prune_state_files(state_dir: Path, deadline: float) -> None:
    cutoff = time.time() - STATE_MAX_AGE_S
    try:
        with os.scandir(state_dir) as entries:
            for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
                if index >= MAX_STATE_FILES or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    return
                try:
                    if entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False) and entry.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_mtime < cutoff:
                        os.unlink(entry.path)
                except OSError:
                    pass
    except OSError:
        pass


def run_hook(home: Path, deadline: float) -> int:
    try:
        raw_payload = sys.stdin.read(MAX_HOOK_PAYLOAD_BYTES + 1)
        if len(raw_payload) > MAX_HOOK_PAYLOAD_BYTES:
            return 0
        payload = json.loads(raw_payload)
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            return 0
        session_id = payload.get("session_id")
        source = payload.get("source")
        if not isinstance(session_id, str) or not session_id or (source is not None and not isinstance(source, str)):
            return 0

        state_dir = home / ".local/state/agent-staleness"
        state_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        state_dir.chmod(0o700)
        prune_state_files(state_dir, deadline)
        state_file = state_dir / f"{hashlib.sha256(session_id.encode()).hexdigest()}.epoch"
        flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
        descriptor = os.open(state_file, flags, 0o600)
        os.fchmod(descriptor, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "r+") as baseline_file:
            fcntl.flock(baseline_file, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            baseline = baseline_file.read().strip()
            if not baseline:
                baseline_file.write(f"{time.time()}\n")
                baseline_file.flush()
                return 0
        lines = stale_lines(home, parse_since(baseline), deadline)
        if lines:
            # systemMessage is shown to the user and additionalContext reaches Claude; both only
            # from a synchronous hook (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks).
            message = "\n".join(lines)
            print(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "systemMessage": message,
                        "hookSpecificOutput": {
                            "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
                            "additionalContext": message,
                        },
                    }
                )
            )
        return 0
    except Exception:
        return 0


def run(argv: list[str], home: Path, deadline: float) -> int:
    if not argv:
        updates = sorted(collect_updates(home, None, deadline), reverse=True)[:10]
        for mtime, label, path in updates:
            timestamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(mtime, timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
            print(f"{timestamp} {label} {display_path(path, home)}")
        return 0

    if argv[0] == "hook":
        return run_hook(home, deadline) if len(argv) == 1 else 0

    parser = QuietParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    check = subparsers.add_parser("check")
    check.add_argument("--since", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    for line in stale_lines(home, parse_since(args.since), deadline):
        print(line)
    return 0


def parse_since(value: str) -> float:
    since = float(value)
    if not math.isfinite(since) or since < 0:
        raise ValueError("--since must be a finite non-negative epoch")
    return since


def stale_lines(home: Path, since: float, deadline: float) -> list[str]:
    """One `restart recommended:` line per asset label updated after since, newest first."""
    latest_by_label: dict[str, Update] = {}
    for update in collect_updates(home, since, deadline):
        current = latest_by_label.get(update[1])
        if current is None or update[0] > current[0]:
            latest_by_label[update[1]] = update
    return [
        f"restart recommended: {label} ({display_path(path, home)})"
        for _mtime, label, path in sorted(latest_by_label.values(), reverse=True)[:MAX_OUTPUT_LINES]
    ]


def guarded_main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, home: Path | None = None) -> int:
    arguments = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    target_home = Path(os.environ.get("HOME", str(Path.home()))) if home is None else home
    previous_handler = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGALRM)

    def timeout_handler(_signum: int, _frame: object) -> None:
        raise TimeoutError("wall limit exceeded")

    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, timeout_handler)
    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, WALL_LIMIT_S)
    try:
        return run(arguments, target_home, time.monotonic() + WALL_LIMIT_S)
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"agent-session-staleness: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
    finally:
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, previous_handler)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(guarded_main())
