<pre><code>#!/bin/bash
# @file hcom-seat
# @brief Start one omp seat for a role in a herdr pane through `hcom omp`, with its profile, policy overlay and extensions wired in.
# @description
#   Plan 025 W5b (U7), the minimal form before X. A seat is one omp process that
#   `hcom omp` starts in a herdr pane (`hcom omp --help`: `hcom [N] omp [args...]`,
#   `--tag <name>`, `--dir <path>`, `--terminal <preset>`; hcom gives the seat
#   HCOM_LAUNCHED=1, HCOM_TAG and HCOM_DIR). For `<role>` the launch line is
#   `hcom omp --tag <name> --dir <dir> --terminal herdr --go -- --profile <role>
#   --config ~/.agents/omp/policies/<role>.yml --config ~/.agents/omp/profiles/<role>.yml
#   --append-system-prompt ~/.agents/omp/rules/<role>.md -e <ext>...`; hcom drops the `--` and forwards what follows to omp verbatim
#   (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31, measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; `extract_launch_flags`,
#   `src/commands/launch.rs:572-581` at v0.7.30). `--go`
#   is hcom's launch gate: inside an AI tool, hcom without it prints `== LAUNCH
#   PREVIEW == / Add --go to proceed.` and starts nothing (`launch.rs:48,388-389`,
#   measured on the real host 2026-10-23), and `extract_launch_flags` consumes it
#   only before the `--` (`launch.rs:650-652`). The profile equals the role. A
#   named profile reads its own `~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml`
#   (pi-utils `src/dirs.ts:312-315`, U10),
#   so the manifest's `modelRoles.default` and `skills.customDirectories` reach the
#   seat only through the second overlay, rendered per role (U14); the first overlay
#   owns the approval mode (U6). Both are required. The seat's standing rules, rendered per role from the manifest's
#   standing_rules (U75), ride `--append-system-prompt`: the overlays disable the native provider (U66), so no profile
#   context file loads, and the explicit flag also wins over any project APPEND_SYSTEM.md. The rules file is required
#   and must be non-empty, since omp reads a missing path as literal text. The extensions default to the
#   pi-claude-bridge, which the role's model route needs, plus the openai-siwc when it
#   is present; `--ext` replaces that list. The roles are orchestrator and worker; every audit is
#   one fresh `omp-run.sh --role audit` run, never a seat (regime-cutover U57, U58). The stop gate's directory
#   `~/.agents/omp/hooks` is loaded on every launch, whatever `--ext` says, and the
#   launch line ends with `--hcom-team <HCOM_TEAM>`: hcom passes HCOM_DIR into the
#   pane but not HCOM_TEAM, so the flag, which the gate registers, carries exactly the
#   team this launch was given, an explicit one included (regime-cutover U33c; omp
#   refuses the flag when no loaded extension registers it, so a launch without the
#   gate fails instead of running unguarded). Every directory, a default, `--ext` or
#   the gate's, must resolve to an entry of `claude.levers.extensions` in the manifest
#   the self-check reads (regime-cutover U31), else the launch is refused. The
#   orchestrator sits in the repository
#   this command runs in; every other role gets the worktree `<seats-root>/<name>`,
#   which is created detached from `origin/main` (HEAD in a repository without it)
#   when absent and reused when it is a worktree of this repository (any other
#   directory at that path is refused). HCOM_DIR, HCOM_TEAM and the seats root come
#   from the environment or `--seats-root` when set, else from the checkout through
#   the sourced regime-env helper (regime-cutover U33: `~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>`,
#   `<slug>`, `~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>`), and are exported to the seat.
#   The seat's omp runs under OS containment (regime-cutover U85): Anthropic's sandbox-runtime `srt`
#   (sandbox-exec on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux) with per-seat settings, through an `omp` shim at
#   `<seats-root>/.sandbox/<name>/bin/omp` that is put first on PATH, so hcom pins it as the pane's tool;
#   the shim runs a canary under the settings and refuses to start omp unless a write into the sandbox
#   directory and reads of the settings and `~/.ssh` fail inside (seat_sandbox_write below). srt and omp
#   run by their physical argv (pin_exec), and so do hcom (exec'd by it) and herdr (through wrappers in the
#   shim directory); none of their files may be or lie under a write root of any seat.
#   Every input path (HOME, --seats-root, HCOM_DIR, REGIME_SEATS_ROOT, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) and every path
#   written into the srt settings must be clean: absolute, components of [A-Za-z0-9._@+-] only, no '.' or
#   '..' component and no trailing '/', since srt reads a settings path as a pattern. The settings are
#   written by the shell (no JSON tool) and read back by /usr/bin/plutil on macOS, /usr/bin/jq on Linux.
#   No caller PATH entry runs anything: the first statement sets PATH to the system directories, the complete protected set is built by (device, inode) identity before mise or any other
#   tool runs, and the tools beyond them (git, hcom, herdr, omp, srt, node, bun, claude, jq; bwrap, socat and
#   rg on Linux) are resolved through `mise which` under `env -i` from `/`, else `command -v` on the
#   caller's PATH, checked (absolute, no control character, an executable regular file, no shim, neither
#   it nor a directory above it with the identity of a seat write root) and linked into
#   `~/.local/state/hcom-seat/tools`; PATH is then that directory and the system
#   directories, for hcom-seat, hcom, the shim and srt (whose Linux settings name bwrap, socat and rg).
#   Inside the sandbox omp gets that PATH followed by the caller's absolute entries.
#   Every executable is checked with its interpreter chain, and hcom-seat, the shim and the wrappers run
#   under `#!/bin/bash`. The git state host git reads for this repository's worktrees (config,
#   config.worktree, info, hooks, commondir, gitdir, the worktree's .git file) is denied to every seat,
#   and a launch over such state holding a key host git would act on is refused (git_state_check) before
#   the first git command; every git command hcom-seat runs has hooks, fsmonitor and worktree config off.
#   Every program's seats root is read-denied but the seat's own paths.
#   No seat launches a seat: the orchestrator's sandbox, like the worker's, has no herdr socket and no
#   write to the seats root, and a launch from inside a seat is refused; seats are started from a
#   terminal outside every seat (the operator or the coordinator, as gate G7 was).
#   Every input is checked before anything is created or started: an unknown role, a launch inside a
#   seat, a name or team outside `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`, a store regime-env refuses, an absent
#   policy or profile overlay or extension directory, a cwd outside a git checkout, a required tool
#   that is missing, a shim or a file that is or lies under a seat write root, or no sandbox-exec
#   (macOS) or bubblewrap, socat and ripgrep (Linux)
#   is exit 2 with the reason. A seat directory that holds `.omp` is refused too, after the worktree exists and
#   before hcom starts (U66: omp applies the cwd's `.omp/config.yml` at start, which no setting turns off).
#   `--dry-run` prints the launch line, and the derived environment and
#   sandbox on stderr, and creates and starts nothing but the private tool links. Otherwise hcom's own
#   exit status is returned (`hcom omp --help`:
#   0 ready, 1 launch failed, 2 still launching or blocked on user attention).
# @arg $1 string Role: orchestrator or worker.
# @option --name <name> Seat name, passed as the hcom tag (default: the role; `<role>-<n>` for a second seat of a role).
# @option --seats-root <dir> Parent of the seat worktrees (default: ~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>, regime-env).
# @option --ext <dir> Extension directory in claude.levers.extensions, repeatable; replaces the role's default list.
# @option --dry-run Print the launch line and exit 0 without creating a worktree or starting hcom.
# @env HCOM_DIR The program's private hcom store (default: ~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>, regime-env).
# @env HCOM_TEAM The team thread (default: the repository slug, regime-env); passed to the seat as --hcom-team.
# @stdout The launch line with --dry-run, else hcom's output.
# @exitcode 0 Dry run printed, or hcom reports the seat ready.
# @exitcode 2 A refusal, before anything is created or started.
# @exitcode * hcom's own status otherwise.
# @example
#   HCOM_DIR=/path/to/.hcom scripts/orchestrator/hcom-seat worker --name worker-2 --dry-run
set -euo pipefail
# No caller PATH entry runs anything (regime-cutover U85): before the first external command PATH holds the fixed
# system directories only, and the tools hcom-seat needs beyond them are resolved below into a private directory.
caller_path=${PATH:-}
system_path=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
PATH=${system_path}
# Git is steered by no inherited environment (regime-cutover U85): every `GIT_*` variable the caller exported
# (GIT_DIR, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_CONFIG_* and the rest) is removed before the first git command, so host
# git, and the seat, find the repository from the working directory alone. hcom-seat takes no input that way.
inherited=$(compgen -e) || {
    echo 'hcom-seat: refused: cannot list the environment' >&2
    exit 2
}
while IFS= read -r inherited_name; do
    case ${inherited_name} in
    GIT_*) unset "${inherited_name}" ;;
    esac
done <<< "${inherited}"

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

usage='usage: hcom-seat <orchestrator|worker> [--name <name>] [--seats-root <dir>] [--ext <dir>]... [--dry-run]'
refuse() {
    echo "hcom-seat: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

(($# >= 1)) || refuse "${usage}"
role=$1
shift
name=${role} seats_root='' dry_run=0 user_exts=()
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --dry-run) dry_run=1 ;;
    --name | --seats-root | --ext)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        case $1 in
        --name) name=$2 ;;
        --seats-root) seats_root=$2 ;;
        --ext) user_exts+=("$2") ;;
        esac
        shift
        ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
    shift
done

bridge=${HOME}/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge
siwc=${HOME}/.agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc
gate=${HOME}/.agents/omp/hooks
# The extension the role's model route needs first, the optional one second.
case ${role} in
orchestrator | worker) exts=("${bridge}" "${siwc}") ;;
*) refuse "unknown role '${role}'; expected orchestrator or worker" ;;
esac
[[ ${name} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || refuse "name '${name}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$"
# A seat never launches a seat (regime-cutover U85): a launch is the operator's or the coordinator's step from a
# terminal outside every seat (gate G7). hcom marks the seat's environment and the shim marks its own; the
# filesystem probe after the seats root is known catches a seat that unset them.
for marker in HCOM_LAUNCHED HCOM_PROCESS_ID HCOM_SEAT_SANDBOX; do
    [[ -z ${!marker:-} ]] || refuse "refused inside a seat (${marker} is set): launch seats from a terminal outside every seat"
done

# @description Succeed when `$1` is a clean absolute path that srt cannot read as a pattern: `/` followed by
#   components of `[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]` only (no glob metacharacter `*?[]{}`, no whitespace, no quote or backslash), none
#   of them empty, `.` or `..`, and no trailing `/`. srt 0.0.81 turns a settings path into a Seatbelt regex or a glob,
#   so `/private/tmp/hcom*` would grant its siblings; a clean path names exactly itself.
# @arg $1 string The path.
# @exitcode 1 The path is not clean.
clean_path() {
    [[ $1 =~ ^(/[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]+)+$ ]] || return 1
    [[ /$1/ != */./* && /$1/ != */../* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow a component test on one path, no path compare
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless `$2` is a clean absolute path (clean_path).
# @arg $1 string What the path is, for the refusal.
# @arg $2 string The path.
require_clean_path() {
    clean_path "$2" ||
        refuse "$1 '$2' is not a clean absolute path: every component must be [A-Za-z0-9._@+-] and neither '.' nor '..', with no trailing '/'"
}

# Every input path that reaches the srt settings is clean before anything is created or run (regime-cutover U85).
require_clean_path HOME "${HOME}"
if [[ -n ${seats_root} ]]; then require_clean_path --seats-root "${seats_root}"; fi
for var in HCOM_DIR REGIME_SEATS_ROOT CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; do
    if [[ -n ${!var:-} ]]; then require_clean_path "${var}" "${!var}"; fi
done

# @description Print a JSON array of the arguments, each a clean path (clean_path), so no JSON escaping is needed and
#   no settings tool runs. An argument that is not clean is a refusal.
# @arg $1 string What the list is, for the refusal.
# @arg $@ string The paths after it.
json_paths() {
    local what=$1 path out='' sep=''
    shift
    for path in "$@"; do
        require_clean_path "${what}" "${path}"
        out+=${sep}\"${path}\"
        sep=,
    done
    printf '[%s]' "${out}"
}

# @description Print the `filesystem.allowWrite` entries of the seat settings file `$2`, one per line: by
#   `/usr/bin/plutil` on macOS (`-extract … raw -expect array` prints the count, `-expect string` each entry; macOS
#   12 and later, plutil(1)), by `/usr/bin/jq` on Linux (from install/ubuntu/common/dependencies.sh). Each entry must
#   be a clean path.
# @arg $1 string The system name (`uname -s`).
# @arg $2 string The settings file.
# @exitcode 1 The file cannot be read, has no such array, or holds an entry that is not a clean path.
allow_write_list() {
    local n i entry line
    case $1 in
    Darwin)
        n=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract filesystem.allowWrite raw -expect array -o - "$2") || return 1
        [[ ${n} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
        for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
            # -n prints no newline of plutil's own, and the 'x' keeps an entry's trailing newlines from the command
            # substitution, so "/tmp/root\n" reaches clean_path whole and is refused.
            entry=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract "filesystem.allowWrite.${i}" raw -expect string -n -o - "$2" && printf x) ||
                return 1
            entry=${entry%x}
            clean_path "${entry}" || return 1
            printf '%s\n' "${entry}"
        done
        ;;
    *)
        [[ -x /usr/bin/jq ]] || return 1
        # Every entry must be a string without a newline, or the line-per-entry output below would drop or split it.
        /usr/bin/jq -e '.filesystem.allowWrite | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string" and (test("\n") | not))' \
            "$2" > /dev/null || return 1
        n=$(/usr/bin/jq -e '.filesystem.allowWrite | length' "$2") || return 1
        # No -e here: an empty array prints nothing, which -e would report as a failure; so jq's status is checked
        # unconditionally, and an empty read with a nonzero n fails the count check below.
        entry=$(/usr/bin/jq -r '.filesystem.allowWrite[]' "$2") || return 1
        i=0
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            [[ -n ${line} ]] || continue
            clean_path "${line}" || return 1
            printf '%s\n' "${line}"
            i=$((i + 1))
        done <<< "${entry}"
        ((i == n)) || return 1
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Set `ancestors` to the absolute path `$1` and every directory above it, up to `/` (regime-cutover
#   U85). Every ancestor walk of hcom-seat goes through this: a relative path (a `#!sh` interpreter line) would never
#   reach `/`, so it is refused before the walk, and the walk itself stops at `/` and refuses after 4096 steps.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @set ancestors The paths, `$1` first.
ancestors_of() {
    local p=$1 n=0
    [[ ${p} == /* && ${p} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
        refuse "'${p}' is not an absolute path free of control characters"
    ancestors=()
    while :; do
        ancestors+=("${p}")
        [[ ${p} != / ]] || return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow the walk ends at the root, no path compare
        n=$((n + 1))
        ((n <= 4096)) || refuse "the path ${1} has more than 4096 components"
        p=${p%/*}
        [[ -n ${p} ]] || p=/
    done
}

# @description Set `dir_list` to every entry of directory `$1`, dot names included, `.` and `..` excluded, in glob
#   order (regime-cutover U95): `dotglob` and `nullglob` for this one glob, then restored. Every directory whose
#   entries matter (the worktree git directories, a seats root, a `.sandbox`) is listed this way, so no consumer sees
#   a dot-named entry that another misses. Fail-closed, so `nullglob` cannot pass a failed read off as an empty
#   directory: an absent `$1` lists nothing; one that exists must be a real directory, no link, readable and
#   searchable, and `/bin/ls -A` (its status checked) must count exactly the entries the glob saw. Anything else, an
#   unreadable directory or one whose read fails, refuses (exit 2).
# @arg $1 string A directory.
# @set dir_list The entries, as `$1/<name>`.
dir_entries() {
    local de_dot=0 de_null=0 de_p de_listing de_line de_n=0
    dir_list=()
    if [[ ! -e $1 && ! -L $1 ]]; then return 0; fi
    [[ -d $1 && ! -L $1 ]] || refuse "cannot list $1: it is not a real directory (a symbolic link or another file)"
    [[ -r $1 && -x $1 ]] || refuse "cannot list $1: it is not readable"
    if shopt -q dotglob; then de_dot=1; fi
    if shopt -q nullglob; then de_null=1; fi
    shopt -s dotglob nullglob
    for de_p in "$1"/*; do
        case ${de_p##*/} in
        . | ..) ;;
        *) dir_list+=("${de_p}") ;;
        esac
    done
    if ((! de_dot)); then shopt -u dotglob; fi
    if ((! de_null)); then shopt -u nullglob; fi
    de_listing=$(/bin/ls -A -- "$1" && printf .) || refuse "cannot list $1: reading it failed"
    de_listing=${de_listing%.}
    if [[ -n ${de_listing} ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r de_line; do
            [[ -n ${de_line} ]] || refuse "cannot list $1: reading it gave an empty name"
            de_n=$((de_n + 1))
        done <<< "${de_listing%$'\n'}"
    fi
    ((de_n == ${#dir_list[@]})) ||
        refuse "cannot list $1: reading it gave ${de_n} entries, the glob ${#dir_list[@]} (a failed or changing read)"
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) when `$1`, a seats root's `.sandbox`, exists and cannot be listed (regime-cutover
#   U85): every seat's sandbox denies reads of it, so this process runs inside a seat that unset the environment
#   markers. Checked before the directory is enumerated (dir_entries), which would refuse with a generic message.
# @arg $1 string A `.sandbox` directory.
refuse_inside_a_seat() {
    if [[ -e $1 ]] && ! /bin/ls "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        refuse "refused inside a seat sandbox ($1 is unreadable): launch seats from a terminal outside every seat"
    fi
}

# @description Set `settings_files` to the srt settings file of every seat under each seats root `$@`, dot-named
#   sandbox entries included (dir_entries), whether or not the file exists (the caller skips absent ones).
# @arg $@ string Seats roots.
# @set settings_files The paths.
seat_settings_files() {
    local root seat
    settings_files=()
    for root in "$@"; do
        refuse_inside_a_seat "${root%/}/.sandbox"
        dir_entries "${root%/}/.sandbox"
        for seat in ${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"}; do settings_files+=("${seat}/srt-settings.json"); done
    done
}

# @description Succeed when `$1`, a path read from a git pointer file (a `.git` file's `gitdir:`, a `commondir`, a
#   `gitdir` back-pointer), is in git's own form (regime-cutover U95): non-empty, no control character, no empty
#   component (`//`), no trailing `/`, no `.` component, and `..` only as the leading components of a relative path
#   (git's relative form, `../..` or `../../.git/worktrees/x`). git writes its pointers so. Anything else refuses at
#   the caller before any type test, since a trailing `/` or `/.` makes `[[ -L … ]]` follow a link and a `..` after
#   a link resolves differently from the text. Builtins only.
# @arg $1 string The path as read.
# @exitcode 1 It is not in git's form.
git_form_path() {
    local rest c lead=1
    [[ -n $1 && $1 != */ && $1 != *//* && $1 != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow a form test on one path, no compare
    rest=$1
    if [[ ${rest} == /* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path test
        rest=${rest#/}
        lead=0
    fi
    while [[ -n ${rest} ]]; do
        c=${rest%%/*}
        if [[ ${rest} == */* ]]; then rest=${rest#*/}; else rest=''; fi # lint-comparisons: allow splitting one path into components
        case ${c} in
        .) return 1 ;;
        ..) ((lead)) || return 1 ;;
        *) lead=0 ;;
        esac
    done
}

# @description Print the physical form of the absolute path `$1`: every symlink followed (at most 40 hops in all,
#   one budget for the whole resolution) and the directory in its `pwd -P` form. A path that does not exist yet is
#   its nearest existing ancestor's physical form with the rest appended, so a write root a launch has not created
#   yet still compares with what it will be. Iterative (regime-cutover U85): a dangling link that names a path
#   under itself (`.state/<name> -> <name>/child`) spends the one budget and fails instead of recursing. Only shell
#   builtins and `/usr/bin/readlink` run.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @stdout The physical path.
# @exitcode 1 Not absolute, a control character in it or in a link, more than 40 links, or a directory that cannot
#   be resolved.
physical_path() {
    local p=$1 tail='' link dir n=0
    [[ ${p} == /* && ${p} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
    while :; do
        # p is absolute, so each step shortens it and the walk ends at `/`, which exists.
        while [[ ! -e ${p} && ! -L ${p} ]]; do
            tail=/${p##*/}${tail}
            p=${p%/*}
            [[ -n ${p} ]] || p=/
        done
        [[ -L ${p} ]] || break
        n=$((n + 1))
        ((n <= 40)) || return 1
        # The '.' keeps a target's own trailing newlines from the command substitution.
        link=$(/usr/bin/readlink "${p}" && printf .) || return 1
        link=${link%.}
        link=${link%$'\n'}
        [[ -n ${link} && ${link} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1
        case ${link} in
        /*) p=${link} ;;
        *) p=${p%/*}/${link} ;;
        esac
    done
    if [[ ${p} == / ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the root itself, whose `cd //` form pwd prints as `//`
        printf '%s\n' "${tail:-/}"
    elif [[ -d ${p} ]]; then
        dir=$(cd "${p}/" && pwd -P) || return 1
        printf '%s%s\n' "${dir%/}" "${tail}"
    else
        dir=$(cd "${p%/*}/" && pwd -P) || return 1
        printf '%s/%s%s\n' "${dir%/}" "${p##*/}" "${tail}"
    fi
}

# @description Print the physical file `$1` names (physical_path); it must be a regular executable file.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @stdout The physical path.
# @exitcode 1 physical_path failed, or the result is not a regular executable file.
physical_file() {
    local p
    p=$(physical_path "$1") || return 1
    [[ -f ${p} && -x ${p} ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${p}"
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) when the physical path `$2`, or any directory above it, has the identity of a
#   protected write root (`root_ids`).
# @arg $1 string A label for the refusal.
# @arg $2 string A physical path.
refuse_if_seat_writable() {
    local ids id i named probe=()
    # The physical file and every directory above it, up to /, each compared by (device, inode): a case alias on a
    # case-insensitive file system or a hardlink of a writable file has the identity of what it aliases.
    ancestors_of "$2"
    probe=("${ancestors[@]}")
    ids=$(/usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" -- "${probe[@]}") || refuse "cannot read the identity of $1 $2 or a directory above it"
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r id; do
        if [[ ${root_ids} == *$'\n'"${id}"$'\n'* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
            named=$(root_named "${id}") || named=${id}
            refuse "$1 $2 is or lies under the seat write root ${named} (${probe[i]} has its identity ${id})"
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "${ids}"
}

# @description Print the write root whose identity is `$1`.
# @arg $1 string A `<device>:<inode>` identity.
root_named() {
    local i
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#root_id_list[@]}; i++)); do
        [[ ${root_id_list[i]} != "$1" ]] || { # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
            printf '%s\n' "${root_path_list[i]}"
            return 0
        }
    done
}

# @description Add the (device, inode) identity of every argument that exists, file or directory, every link
#   followed, to the protected set (`root_ids`, `root_id_list`, `root_path_list`). A path that does not exist holds
#   no executable; one that exists and cannot be read is a refusal.
# @arg $@ string Absolute paths.
add_roots() {
    local present=() path ids id i=0 named
    for path in "$@"; do
        [[ ${path} == /* && ${path} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || refuse "the seat write root '${path}' is not an absolute path" # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
        [[ -e ${path} || -L ${path} ]] || continue
        present+=("${path}")
    done
    ((${#present[@]})) || return 0
    ids=$(/usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" -- "${present[@]}") || refuse "cannot read the identity of a seat write root among: ${present[*]}"
    while IFS= read -r id; do
        [[ ${id} =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "unexpected identity '${id}' of ${present[i]}"
        root_ids+=${id}$'\n'
        root_id_list+=("${id}")
        named=$(physical_path "${present[i]}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seat write root ${present[i]}"
        root_path_list+=("${named}")
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "${ids}"
}

# @description Succeed when a tool is a shim, as scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh decides it (U61): its physical file
#   is named mise in any letter case or is the mise binary, or the directory it was found in or resolves to is named
#   shims in any letter case. A mise shim picks its version from the cwd's config files, which a seat writes.
# @arg $1 string The path the tool was found at.
# @arg $2 string Its physical path.
is_shim() {
    local d
    [[ ${2##*/} == [Mm][Ii][Ss][Ee] ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow a file-name test, not a comparison of two paths
    [[ -n ${mise_real} && $2 -ef ${mise_real} ]] && return 0
    for d in "${1%/*}" "${2%/*}"; do
        d=$(physical_path "${d:-/}") || return 0
        [[ ${d}/ == */[Ss][Hh][Ii][Mm][Ss]/* ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow a directory-name test, not a comparison of two paths
    done
    return 1
}

# @description Print the first executable `$1` on PATH, which hcom-seat has set: the system directories, then the
#   private tool directory before them once it is filled.
# @arg $1 string The command name.
# @stdout The path, symlinks not yet followed.
# @exitcode 1 None found.
find_on_path() {
    local path_dir path_dirs=()
    IFS=: read -r -a path_dirs <<< "${PATH}"
    for path_dir in "${path_dirs[@]}"; do
        [[ -n ${path_dir} && -x ${path_dir}/$1 && ! -d ${path_dir}/$1 ]] || continue
        printf '%s\n' "${path_dir}/$1"
        return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# @description Print the value of the git pointer file `$1` (a `.git` file, `commondir`, `gitdir`) read whole
#   (regime-cutover U85). git consumes the complete content less its trailing newlines, so only a single line is a
#   value: content that cannot be read, is empty, or holds any control character once one final newline is dropped (a
#   second line, a carriage return) fails, and the caller refuses. Pointer files are read this way only where git
#   cannot be asked yet (before the git state is checked); everywhere after, git answers (git_paths_of). A NUL
#   byte, or a byte count other than the file's size, fails too.
# @arg $1 string The file.
# @stdout The value.
# @exitcode 1 It cannot be read, is empty, or is not a single line free of control characters.
pointer_value() {
    local LC_ALL=C content size
    # Bash drops NUL bytes from a command substitution, so they are made \001 (a control character, refused) in the
    # same pass, and the bytes read must number the file's size: what is checked is what git reads.
    content=$({ /bin/cat -- "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\000' '\001'; } && printf .) || return 1
    content=${content%.}
    size=$(/usr/bin/wc -c < "$1") || return 1
    size=${size//[[:space:]]/}
    [[ ${size} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ((${#content} == size)) || return 1
    content=${content%$'\n'}
    [[ -n ${content} && ${content} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${content}"
}

# @description Set `size_list` to the byte size of each file `$@`, links followed, in order, from one
#   `/usr/bin/stat` run (regime-cutover U95). Fail-closed: the run's status (xargs passes a failed stat on), every
#   line a bare number, and exactly one line per file; anything else refuses (exit 2) before a size is used.
# @arg $@ string Files.
# @set size_list The sizes.
sizes_of() {
    local out line
    size_list=()
    (($#)) || return 0
    out=$(printf '%s\0' "$@" | /usr/bin/xargs -0 /usr/bin/stat "${size_args[@]}" --) || refuse 'cannot read the size of the git state files'
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ ${line} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "cannot read the size of a git state file ('${line}')"
        size_list+=("${line}")
    done <<< "${out}"
    ((${#size_list[@]} == $#)) || refuse "cannot read the size of every git state file (${#size_list[@]} of $#)"
}

# @description Set `pointer_list` to the value of each git pointer file `$@`, with the rule of pointer_value
#   (regime-cutover U95): all are read in one pass (`cat | tr`, NUL bytes made \001 there) and cut at the sizes one
#   `stat` gave (sizes_of). The pass counts only when its pipeline succeeded (the `.` sentinel follows its status)
#   and the bytes read number the sizes' sum, checked before any value is cut, so a failed or short read is never
#   used. A file that is empty, or not a single line free of control characters once one final newline is dropped,
#   refuses (exit 2).
# @arg $@ string Pointer files.
# @set pointer_list The values.
pointer_values() {
    local LC_ALL=C all value off=0 total=0 i=0 files=("$@")
    pointer_list=()
    (($#)) || return 0
    sizes_of "$@"
    all=$({ printf '%s\0' "$@" | /usr/bin/xargs -0 /bin/cat -- | /usr/bin/tr '\000' '\001'; } && printf .) ||
        refuse 'cannot read the git pointer files'
    all=${all%.}
    for ((i = 0; i < $#; i++)); do total=$((total + size_list[i])); done
    ((total == ${#all})) || refuse "cannot read the git pointer files whole (${#all} of ${total} bytes)"
    for ((i = 0; i < $#; i++)); do
        value=${all:off:size_list[i]}
        off=$((off + size_list[i]))
        value=${value%$'\n'}
        [[ -n ${value} && ${value} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] ||
            refuse "cannot read ${files[i]} as one line free of control characters${pointer_hint:-}"
        pointer_list+=("${value}")
    done
}

# @description Resolve `$2` to the argv that runs it with no lookup left: its physical file, preceded by the physical
#   interpreter when it is a `#!` script (`#!/abs/interp` or `#!/usr/bin/env <name>`, no arguments; an interpreter
#   that is itself a script is refused). No part may be, or lie under, a write root of any seat (`root_ids`), since
#   a seat that could rewrite a file the launch runs would run uncontained on the next launch. A failure exits 2
#   naming `$1`.
# @arg $1 string A label for the refusal.
# @arg $2 string The executable's path.
# @set pinned The argv.
# @set pinned_spelled The interpreter as the `#!` line spells it (what the kernel follows), or empty.
pin_exec() {
    local label=$1 file first magic interp name extra interp_path
    pinned_spelled=''
    # The spelling the kernel will follow, every link hop, is held to the identity check too: a link in a write root
    # that points outside it passes the physical check today and can be retargeted before the next exec.
    refuse_if_link_chain_writable "${label}" "$2"
    file=$(physical_file "$2") || refuse "cannot resolve ${label} to a physical executable file: $2"
    refuse_if_seat_writable "${label}" "${file}"
    [[ -r ${file} ]] || refuse "cannot read ${label}: ${file}"
    # Each read's status is checked (pipefail covers head; /usr/bin/od on macOS exits 0 on a read error, so it only
    # formats): a failed read is refused, never taken for a file without an interpreter line.
    magic=$(/usr/bin/head -c 2 -- "${file}" | /usr/bin/od -An -tx1) || refuse "cannot read ${label}: ${file}"
    first=''
    if [[ ${magic//[[:space:]]/} == 2321 ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the hex bytes of `#!`, no path compare
        first=$(/usr/bin/head -n 1 -- "${file}") || refuse "cannot read the interpreter line of ${label}: ${file}"
    fi
    pinned=("${file}")
    case ${first} in
    '#!'*)
        extra=''
        read -r interp name extra <<< "${first#??}"
        pinned_spelled=${interp}
        if [[ ${interp} == /usr/bin/env ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the literal interpreter line, no path compare
            [[ -n ${name} && -z ${extra} && ${name} != -* ]] ||
                refuse "${label}: unsupported interpreter line '${first}' in ${file}"
            interp_path=$(find_on_path "${name}") || refuse "${label}: interpreter ${name} not found on PATH"
        else
            [[ -z ${name} ]] || refuse "${label}: unsupported interpreter line '${first}' in ${file}"
            # The kernel would not run a relative interpreter as written; it is refused before any walk over it.
            [[ ${interp} == /* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path test
                refuse "${label}: interpreter line '${first}' in ${file} names no absolute path"
            interp_path=${interp}
        fi
        refuse_if_link_chain_writable "the interpreter of ${label}" "${interp_path}"
        interp=$(physical_file "${interp_path}") || refuse "cannot resolve the interpreter of ${label}: ${interp_path}"
        refuse_if_seat_writable "${label}" "${interp}"
        [[ -r ${interp} ]] || refuse "cannot read the interpreter of ${label}: ${interp}"
        magic=$(/usr/bin/head -c 2 -- "${interp}" | /usr/bin/od -An -tx1) || refuse "cannot read the interpreter of ${label}: ${interp}"
        [[ ${magic//[[:space:]]/} != 2321 ]] || refuse "${label}: its interpreter ${interp} is itself a script" # lint-comparisons: allow the hex bytes of `#!`, no path compare
        pinned=("${interp}" "${file}")
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) an optional tool whose `#!` line spells its interpreter outside the trusted system
#   directories (regime-cutover U85, a best-effort reduction of the G17 residual, README "Boundary"): the directory
#   the line names, followed physically, must be or lie under `/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/sbin`, `/usr/sbin` or
#   `~/.local/share/mise/installs`, by (device, inode) identity (`trusted_ids`), however the spelling reaches it, so
#   a directory alias into a seat write root (`alias -> $HCOM_DIR/subdir`) is refused. A binary passes.
# @arg $1 string The tool's name, for the refusal.
trusted_interpreter_check() {
    local dir ids id
    [[ -n ${pinned_spelled} ]] || return 0
    dir=${pinned_spelled%/*}
    dir=$(physical_path "${dir:-/}") || refuse "cannot resolve the interpreter directory of $1: ${pinned_spelled}"
    ancestors_of "${dir}"
    ids=$(/usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" -- "${ancestors[@]}") || refuse "cannot read the identity of ${dir}"
    while IFS= read -r id; do
        [[ ${trusted_ids} != *$'\n'"${id}"$'\n'* ]] || return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
    done <<< "${ids}"
    refuse "$1: its interpreter ${pinned_spelled} lies outside /bin, /usr/bin, /sbin, /usr/sbin and ~/.local/share/mise/installs (${dir})"
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) when any hop of the symlink chain `$2` (the spelling itself, then each link target in
#   turn) is, or lies under, a protected write root (refuse_if_seat_writable on each hop as spelled, which compares
#   the hop's target and every directory above the spelling), so the path the kernel follows at exec time cannot be retargeted by a seat.
# @arg $1 string A label for the refusal.
# @arg $2 string An absolute path.
refuse_if_link_chain_writable() {
    local p=$2 link n=0
    [[ ${p} == /* ]] || refuse "$1 ${p} is not an absolute path" # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path test
    while :; do
        # The hop as spelled: stat follows it to its target, and every directory above the spelling is compared too.
        refuse_if_seat_writable "$1" "${p}"
        [[ -L ${p} ]] || return 0
        n=$((n + 1))
        ((n <= 40)) || refuse "$1 ${2}: too many symbolic links"
        link=$(/usr/bin/readlink "${p}") || refuse "cannot read the link $1 ${p}"
        case ${link} in
        /*) p=${link} ;;
        *) p=${p%/*}/${link} ;;
        esac
    done
}

# The tools (regime-cutover U85, the pattern of scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh, U61). First the complete protected
# set, by identity: the (device, inode) of every write root any seat may have that exists, files and directories,
# computed with builtins, /usr/bin/stat, /usr/bin/readlink and the system's settings reader only, before any tool outside the
# system directories runs. It holds the seats roots and the hcom stores of every program, ~/Workspace, the checkout
# this runs in and its git directories, the omp profiles and leases, the Claude Code state, srt's implicit write paths,
# and every `allowWrite` entry of every existing seat settings file (another program's checkout outside ~/Workspace
# included). Then mise's own physical file is held to it before mise runs. Every tool beyond the system directories
# is what `mise which` answers under `env -i` from `/` (no project config, no caller environment), else what
# `command -v` finds on the caller's PATH; an answer is only a name until it passes: absolute, no control character,
# a regular executable file once every link is followed, no shim, and neither its physical file nor any directory
# above it has the identity of a protected root. A passing tool is linked into the private directory
# ~/.local/state/hcom-seat/tools (0700, this user's, outside every seat write root), and PATH becomes that directory
# followed by the system directories; no caller entry is inherited.
os=$(/usr/bin/uname -s) || refuse 'cannot read the operating system name (uname -s)'
if [[ ${os} == Linux && ! -x /usr/bin/jq ]]; then
    refuse 'the system jq /usr/bin/jq is absent; it reads the seat sandbox settings on Linux (apt install jq)'
fi
case ${os} in
Darwin) stat_args=(-L -f '%d:%i') size_args=(-L -f '%z') ;;
Linux) stat_args=(-L -c '%d:%i') size_args=(-L -c '%s') ;;
*) refuse "no seat sandbox for ${os}; srt supports macOS and Linux" ;;
esac
# srt 0.0.81 keeps its own TMPDIR writable whatever the policy says (SANDBOX_OWN_WRITE_PATHS in
# dist/sandbox/sandbox-utils.js:499-508 lists /tmp/claude and /private/tmp/claude on every OS). /private exists on
# macOS only; on Linux srt can bind only what exists, so /private/tmp/claude is a write root there only if it exists
# (a nonexistent /private would resolve to no path a seat can write).
# @description Set `srt_tmp_roots` to srt's own writable TMPDIR paths on the operating system `$1` (`uname -s`).
# @arg $1 string Darwin or Linux.
# @set srt_tmp_roots The paths.
srt_tmp_roots_for() {
    srt_tmp_roots=(/tmp/claude /private/tmp/claude)
    if [[ $1 != Darwin && ! -e ${srt_tmp_roots[1]} ]]; then srt_tmp_roots=("${srt_tmp_roots[0]}"); fi
}
srt_tmp_roots_for "${os}"
root_ids=$'\n' root_id_list=() root_path_list=()
roots=("${HOME}/.local/state/omp-seats" "${HOME}/.local/state/hcom" "${HOME}/Workspace" "${HOME}/.omp/profiles"
    "${HOME}/.omp/run" "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-${HOME}/.claude}" "${HOME}/.claude" "${HOME}/.claude.json"
    "${HOME}/.npm/_logs" "${srt_tmp_roots[@]}")
for root in ${HCOM_DIR:+"${HCOM_DIR}"} ${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:+"${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT}"} ${seats_root:+"${seats_root}"}; do
    roots+=("${root}")
done
# The checkout this runs in, found with builtins: the nearest ancestor with a `.git`, and for a worktree the git
# directory its `.git` file names and that directory's common directory and main checkout. Type before content, as in
# git_state_check (regime-cutover U95): `.git` is a regular file or a real directory, never a link; the git directory
# a `.git` file names is a real directory; its `commondir` is absent or a regular file, no link. A FIFO there would
# leave the guess at the admin directory, so the scan below would miss it and the first git command would block on
# it. A linked worktree's admin directory (git writes a `gitdir` file only there) must hold its `commondir`: without
# it git takes the admin directory for the common directory. All before any git command runs.
cwd_real=$(pwd -P) || refuse 'cannot resolve the working directory'
top=${cwd_real}
while [[ ! -e ${top}/.git && -n ${top} ]]; do top=${top%/*}; done
if [[ -n ${top} || -e /.git ]]; then
    top=${top:-/}
    gitdir=${top}/.git
    [[ ! -L ${gitdir} && (-f ${gitdir} || -d ${gitdir}) ]] ||
        refuse "${gitdir} is not a regular file or a real directory (a symbolic link, FIFO, device or socket), which git would follow or block on; launch from a checkout git made"
    if [[ -f ${gitdir} ]]; then
        line=$(pointer_value "${gitdir}") || refuse "cannot read ${gitdir} as one line free of control characters"
        [[ ${line} == 'gitdir: '* ]] || refuse "${gitdir} holds no 'gitdir: ' line" # lint-comparisons: allow the literal prefix git writes, no path compare
        gitdir=${line#gitdir: }
        git_form_path "${gitdir}" ||
            refuse "${top}/.git names '${gitdir}', not a path in git's own form (no trailing /, no . component, .. only leading a relative path); repair the worktree (\`git worktree repair\`)"
        case ${gitdir} in # lint-comparisons: allow a relative operand is made absolute, no path compare
        /*) ;;
        *) gitdir=${top}/${gitdir} ;;
        esac
        [[ -d ${gitdir} && ! -L ${gitdir} ]] ||
            refuse "the git directory ${gitdir} that ${top}/.git names is not a real directory (absent, a symbolic link or another file); repair the worktree (\`git worktree repair\`) or launch elsewhere"
    fi
    common_guess=${gitdir}
    if [[ -e ${gitdir}/commondir || -L ${gitdir}/commondir ]]; then
        [[ -f ${gitdir}/commondir && ! -L ${gitdir}/commondir ]] ||
            refuse "the git state ${gitdir}/commondir is not a regular file (a symbolic link, FIFO, device, socket or directory), which git would follow or block on; replace it with a regular file holding ../.., or delete the worktree and run \`git worktree prune\` from the main checkout"
        line=$(pointer_value "${gitdir}/commondir") ||
            refuse "cannot read ${gitdir}/commondir as one line free of control characters"
        git_form_path "${line}" ||
            refuse "${gitdir}/commondir holds '${line}', not a path in git's own form (no trailing /, no . component, .. only leading a relative path); replace it with ../.."
        case ${line} in # lint-comparisons: allow a relative operand is made absolute, no path compare
        /*) common_guess=${line} ;;
        *) common_guess=${gitdir}/${line} ;;
        esac
    elif [[ -e ${gitdir}/gitdir || -L ${gitdir}/gitdir ]]; then
        refuse "the worktree git directory ${gitdir} has no commondir, so git would take it for its own common directory; delete the worktree and run \`git worktree prune\` from the main checkout"
    fi
    roots+=("${top}" "${gitdir}" "${common_guess}")
    # The main checkout is the common directory's parent only when that parent's `.git` is the common directory, by
    # identity (a `.GIT` spelling on a case-insensitive volume included); a separate git directory
    # (`git init --separate-git-dir`) has no checkout above it, and its checkout is `top`.
    common_parent=$(physical_path "${common_guess}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common_guess}"
    common_parent=${common_parent%/*}
    common_parent=${common_parent:-/}
    if [[ -d ${common_parent}/.git && ! -L ${common_parent}/.git && ${common_parent}/.git -ef ${common_guess} ]]; then
        roots+=("${common_parent}")
    fi
fi
# Every existing seat settings file, read by the system's reader (allow_write_list); an entry that cannot be read, or
# that is not a clean path, is a refusal.
dir_entries "${HOME}/.local/state/omp-seats"
seat_settings_files ${seats_root:+"${seats_root}"} ${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:+"${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT}"} ${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"}
for settings_file in ${settings_files[@]+"${settings_files[@]}"}; do
    [[ -e ${settings_file} ]] || continue
    listed=$(allow_write_list "${os}" "${settings_file}") ||
        refuse "cannot read a clean allowWrite list from ${settings_file}"
    while IFS= read -r root; do
        if [[ -n ${root} ]]; then roots+=("${root}"); fi
    done <<< "${listed}"
done
add_roots "${roots[@]}"
tools_dir=${HOME}/.local/state/hcom-seat/tools
/bin/mkdir -p "${tools_dir}" || refuse "cannot create the private tool directory ${tools_dir}"
/bin/chmod 700 "${tools_dir%/*}" "${tools_dir}" || refuse "cannot restrict the private tool directory ${tools_dir}"
for dir_check in "${tools_dir%/*}" "${tools_dir}"; do
    [[ -d ${dir_check} && ! -L ${dir_check} && -O ${dir_check} ]] ||
        refuse "the private tool directory ${dir_check} is not this user's own directory"
done
tools_dir=$(physical_path "${tools_dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the private tool directory ${tools_dir}"
[[ ${tools_dir} != *:* ]] || refuse "the private tool directory ${tools_dir} holds a ':'" # lint-comparisons: allow a ':' content test
refuse_if_seat_writable 'the private tool directory' "${tools_dir}"
# mise runs only once its physical file and its interpreter chain have passed the complete protected set above, and
# it runs by the argv that check pinned.
mise_cmd=()
mise_real=''
# Absence (command -v fails) means no mise; a mise that is found but does not resolve is refused.
if mise_found=$(PATH=${caller_path} && command -v mise && printf .); then
    mise_found=${mise_found%.}
    mise_found=${mise_found%$'\n'}
    mise_real=$(physical_file "${mise_found}") || refuse "mise is not an executable file ('${mise_found}')"
fi
if [[ -n ${mise_real} ]]; then
    pin_exec mise "${mise_real}"
    mise_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
fi
required_tools=(git hcom herdr omp srt)
# claude, regime-open-url and its python3 serve seat-login-preflight's interactive login handoff (U37); jq reads the
# openai-siwc registration there (macOS 14 ships no /usr/bin/jq, so a mise or Homebrew jq is resolved and checked
# like every tool). hcom-seat itself never runs it: the settings are read by plutil or /usr/bin/jq. security (macOS)
# is the preflight's one Keychain reader, resolved like every tool, so the preflight's login check has one seam.
optional_tools=(node bun claude python3 regime-open-url jq security)
case ${OSTYPE} in
linux*) required_tools+=(bwrap socat rg) ;;
esac
for tool in "${required_tools[@]}" "${optional_tools[@]}"; do
    found=$(cd / && {
        { [[ -n ${mise_real} ]] && /usr/bin/env -i PATH="${system_path}" HOME="${HOME}" "${mise_cmd[@]}" which "${tool}" 2> /dev/null; } ||
            { PATH=${caller_path} && command -v "${tool}"; }
    } && printf .) || found=''
    found=${found%.}
    found=${found%$'\n'}
    real=''
    if [[ -n ${found} ]]; then
        real=$(physical_file "${found}") || refuse "${tool} is not an executable file ('${found}')"
        ! is_shim "${found}" "${real}" || refuse "no ${tool} outside a shims directory ('${found}')"
        refuse_if_seat_writable "${tool}" "${real}"
    fi

            [[ ${tool} != "${required}" ]] || refuse "${tool} not found (mise which, then the caller's PATH); run make update"
        done
        /bin/rm -f "${tools_dir}/${tool}" || refuse "cannot clear ${tools_dir}/${tool}"
        continue
    fi
    if ! /bin/rm -f "${tools_dir}/.${tool}.$$" || ! /bin/ln -s -- "${real}" "${tools_dir}/.${tool}.$$" ||
        ! /bin/mv -f -- "${tools_dir}/.${tool}.$$" "${tools_dir}/${tool}"; then

    fi
