PATH=${tools_dir}:${system_path}
# The trusted interpreter directories of the optional tools (trusted_interpreter_check), by identity.
trusted_dirs=(/bin /usr/bin /sbin /usr/sbin)
if [[ -d ${HOME}/.local/share/mise/installs ]]; then trusted_dirs+=("${HOME}/.local/share/mise/installs"); fi
trusted_ids=$(/usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" -- "${trusted_dirs[@]}") ||
    refuse "cannot read the identity of the trusted interpreter directories ${trusted_dirs[*]}"
trusted_ids=$'\n'${trusted_ids}$'\n'
# Every linked tool's interpreter chain (`#!/abs/interp`, or `#!/usr/bin/env X` with X looked up on this PATH, as it
# will be when the tool runs) passes the same identity check before anything runs it; git runs next (regime-env).
# Plain `*` here: the private tool directory is hcom-seat's own (0700, outside every write root), and its only dot
# entries are its own `.<tool>.<pid>` link temporaries, which no lookup by name finds.
for link in "${tools_dir}"/*; do
    [[ -e ${link} || -L ${link} ]] || continue
    pin_exec "${link##*/}" "${link}"
    for tool in "${optional_tools[@]}"; do
        if [[ ${tool} == "${link##*/}" ]]; then trusted_interpreter_check "${tool}"; fi
    done
done
# Host git runs by the argv pin_exec checked (interpreter first when git is a script), never by a lookup.
git_path=$(find_on_path git) || refuse 'git not found in the private tool directory'
pin_exec git "${git_path}"
git_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
# Inside the sandbox the seat works with its tools (gh, uv, linters) from the caller's absolute PATH entries after
# these; every process there is contained, and nothing outside the sandbox runs from that list.
seat_path=${PATH}
IFS=: read -r -a caller_dirs <<< "${caller_path}"
for caller_dir in "${caller_dirs[@]}"; do
    if [[ ${caller_dir} == /* && ${caller_dir} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]]; then seat_path+=:${caller_dir}; fi # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
done

# @description Collect the git state host git reads for the worktrees of this repository into `git_state`, make sure
#   each file exists, and refuse (exit 2) a launch over state a seat may have written. The set: the common `config`,
#   `config.worktree`, `info/` and `hooks/`; for every linked worktree `worktrees/<n>/config.worktree`, `info/`,
#   `commondir` and `gitdir`; and the seat worktree's own `.git` file. None may be a symbolic link. Every
#   `config.worktree` may hold only the keys `git sparse-checkout` writes (`core.sparseCheckout`,
#   `core.sparseCheckoutCone`): anything else (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`, `filter.*`, `diff.*.textconv`,
#   `include.*`, `includeIf.*`, `extensions.*` among them) is a refusal, read with `git config --no-includes`, which
#   runs nothing the file names. Every `commondir` must lead to this common directory, and the seat worktree's
#   `.git` file into its `worktrees/`. An absent `config.worktree` is created empty and an absent `info/` or `hooks/`
#   empty, which git reads as no setting.
#   It runs before the first host git command (with the seat directory empty) and again before each git command in
#   the seat directory and when the settings are written.
# @arg $1 string The physical git common directory.
# @arg $2 string The physical seat directory, or empty.
# @set git_state The paths, for the seat's write denies.
# The repair a refusal over a worktree's git files names (regime-cutover U95).
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # literal backquotes in a message
git_fix_hint='; repair or drop the worktree first (`git worktree move`, `git worktree remove` or `git worktree prune`)'
git_state_check() {
    local common_real=$1 dir_real=$2 wt f names name line target i pointers=() configs=() missing=()
    git_state=("${common_real}/config" "${common_real}/config.worktree" "${common_real}/info" "${common_real}/hooks")
    # Git's own shape for every linked worktree (regime-cutover U95, from git 2.56's source, PR body "Admin directory
    # files"): `worktrees` is a real directory; each admin directory is a real directory holding `commondir`, or git
    # would take the admin directory for its own common directory (setup.c get_common_dir_noenv) and read its
    # `config` and `hooks`, which a seat can write; and it holds none of the names path.c's common_list sends to the
    # common directory (git never writes them into an admin directory; `refs`, `logs` and `info` it does).
    [[ ! -L ${common_real}/worktrees ]] ||
        refuse "the worktree git directories ${common_real}/worktrees are a symbolic link, which host git would follow${git_fix_hint}"
    # One enumeration, dot names included, as git's own readdir_skip_dot_and_dotdot (worktree.c:203): every entry
    # must be a real directory (admin_dirs_match later holds it to the worktrees git lists, one to one).
    dir_entries "${common_real}/worktrees"
    admin_dirs=(${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"})
    for wt in ${admin_dirs[@]+"${admin_dirs[@]}"}; do
        [[ -d ${wt} && ! -L ${wt} ]] ||
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${wt} is not a real directory (a symbolic link, file or other entry), which host git would follow or no worktree owns${git_fix_hint}"
        [[ -e ${wt}/commondir || -L ${wt}/commondir ]] ||
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${wt} has no commondir, so git would take it for its own common directory and read its config and hooks${git_fix_hint}"
        for f in branches common hooks lost-found objects remotes worktrees rr-cache svn config gc.pid packed-refs shallow; do
            [[ ! -e ${wt}/${f} && ! -L ${wt}/${f} ]] ||
                refuse "the worktree git directory ${wt} holds ${f}, which git keeps in the common directory and never writes there${git_fix_hint}"
        done
        git_state+=("${wt}/config.worktree" "${wt}/info")
        for f in commondir gitdir; do
            if [[ -e ${wt}/${f} || -L ${wt}/${f} ]]; then git_state+=("${wt}/${f}"); fi
        done
    done
    if [[ -n ${dir_real} && -f ${dir_real}/.git ]]; then git_state+=("${dir_real}/.git"); fi
    # The file type comes first, before any size or content is read (U95): a FIFO reads as size 0 and would block
    # a read or a write, and a device or socket is no file git means. Each entry is absent, or a real directory
    # (`info`, `hooks`), or a regular file, never a symbolic link.
    for f in "${git_state[@]}"; do
        [[ ! -L ${f} ]] || refuse "the git state ${f} is a symbolic link${git_fix_hint}"
        [[ -e ${f} ]] || continue
        case ${f##*/} in
        info | hooks) [[ -d ${f} ]] || refuse "the git state ${f} is not a directory${git_fix_hint}" ;;
        *) [[ -f ${f} ]] || refuse "the git state ${f} is not a regular file (a FIFO, device, socket or directory)${git_fix_hint}" ;;
        esac
        if [[ ${f##*/} == commondir && ${f} == "${common_real}"/worktrees/* ]]; then pointers+=("${f}"); fi # lint-comparisons: allow a fixed file name below the common directory
    done
    # Read here before any git may run (the first call precedes the first git command); git has no query for
    # another worktree's commondir. One line or a refusal: git would consume every line. All in one read (U95).
    pointer_values ${pointers[@]+"${pointers[@]}"}
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#pointers[@]}; i++)); do
        wt=${pointers[i]%/commondir}
        line=${pointer_list[i]}
        git_form_path "${line}" ||
            refuse "${pointers[i]} holds '${line}', not a path in git's own form (no trailing /, no . component, .. only leading a relative path)${git_fix_hint}"
        case ${line} in # lint-comparisons: allow a relative operand is made absolute, no path compare
        /*) target=${line} ;;
        *) target=${wt}/${line} ;;
        esac
        [[ ${target} -ef ${common_real} ]] || refuse "${wt}/commondir leads to ${line}, not to ${common_real}"
    done
    # A dry run validates and creates nothing: an absent file holds no setting, and the real launch creates it. The
    # absent `info/` and `hooks/` directories are made in one `mkdir` (U95), without -p: each parent is a real
    # directory checked above, so an entry that appeared since the check fails the run, which refuses. Each is then
    # checked to be a real directory, no link. An empty `config.worktree` is made by a builtin.
    if ((! dry_run)); then
        for f in "${git_state[@]}"; do
            case ${f##*/} in
            info | hooks) [[ -d ${f} ]] || missing+=("${f}") ;;
            config.worktree) [[ -f ${f} ]] || : >> "${f}" || refuse "cannot create ${f}" ;;
            esac
        done
        if ((${#missing[@]})); then
            /bin/mkdir -- "${missing[@]}" || refuse "cannot create the git state directories (${missing[*]})"
            for f in "${missing[@]}"; do
                [[ -d ${f} && ! -L ${f} ]] || refuse "the git state ${f} is not a real directory after it was created"
            done
        fi
    fi
    for f in "${git_state[@]}"; do
        if [[ ${f##*/} == config.worktree && -e ${f} ]]; then configs+=("${f}"); fi
    done
    # An empty config.worktree (what a launch creates) holds no key, so git reads only the others (U95): one size read.
    # The rest cost one git each: git config validates one --file per run, and joining files would let one file's
    # section run into the next. A sparse checkout's file is the only non-empty one git writes (none on this host).
    sizes_of ${configs[@]+"${configs[@]}"}
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#configs[@]}; i++)); do
        ((size_list[i] > 0)) || continue
        f=${configs[i]}
        # From /, so no repository around the cwd is discovered or read; git() adds the overrides.
        names=$(cd / && git config --file "${f}" --no-includes --name-only --list) ||
            refuse "cannot read the git config ${f}"
        while IFS= read -r name; do
            case ${name} in
            '' | core.sparsecheckout | core.sparsecheckoutcone) ;;
            *) refuse "the git config ${f} sets ${name}, which host git would act on; a seat may have written it" ;;
            esac
        done <<< "${names}"
    done
    # The seat worktree's `.git` file is git's to read (relative forms, `--relative-paths`, included): once the
    # state it reads has passed, git names the git directory and common directory it resolves there.
    if [[ -n ${dir_real} && -f ${dir_real}/.git ]]; then
        git_paths_of 2 -C "${dir_real}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
        [[ ${git_paths[0]%/*} -ef ${common_real}/worktrees && ${git_paths[1]} -ef ${common_real} ]] ||
            refuse "${dir_real}/.git leads to ${git_paths[0]}, outside ${common_real}/worktrees"
    fi
}

# @description Run host git (git, the checked argv) with `$2...` and read its whole answer into `git_paths`
#   (regime-cutover U85): exactly `$1` newline-terminated lines, each an absolute path free of control characters. A
#   failing git, an unterminated line, another count (a path holding a newline splits into more), a relative path or
#   a control character refuses (exit 2).
# @arg $1 int The number of paths.
# @arg $@ string git's arguments after it.
# @set git_paths The paths.
git_paths_of() {
    local count=$1 out line
    shift
    out=$(git "$@" && printf .) || refuse "git $* failed"
    out=${out%.}
    git_paths=()
    while [[ -n ${out} ]]; do
        [[ ${out} == *$'\n'* ]] || refuse "git $* printed an unterminated line"
        line=${out%%$'\n'*}
        out=${out#*$'\n'}
        [[ ${line} == /* && ${line} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
            refuse "git $* printed '${line}', not an absolute path free of control characters"
        git_paths+=("${line}")
    done
    ((${#git_paths[@]} == count)) || refuse "git $* printed ${#git_paths[@]} paths, not ${count}"
}

# @description Run git with nothing a repository's config or hooks name: no hooks (`core.hooksPath=/dev/null`), no
#   fsmonitor program, no per-worktree config, no transport, and no system config (regime-cutover U85). Every host git
#   command of hcom-seat and the sourced regime-env goes through this function, before and after the git state is
#   checked.
# @arg $@ string git's arguments.
git() {
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 "${git_cmd[@]}" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false \
        -c extensions.worktreeConfig=false -c protocol.allow=never "$@"
}

# The git state is checked before the first git command: the common directory found with builtins above.
if [[ -n ${top} || -e /.git ]]; then
    early_common=$(physical_path "${common_guess}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common_guess}"
    [[ -d ${early_common} ]] || refuse "the git common directory ${early_common} is not a directory"
    # The checkout and its git directories reach the srt settings: clean before anything (metadata included) is made.
    for root in "${top}" "${gitdir}" "${early_common}"; do
        root=$(physical_path "${root}") || refuse "cannot resolve ${root}"
        require_clean_path 'the checkout or its git directory' "${root}"
    done
    git_state_check "${early_common}" ''
fi

# HCOM_DIR, HCOM_TEAM and the seats root come from the environment when set, else from this checkout (regime-env,
# regime-cutover U33). hcom passes HCOM_DIR into the seat but not HCOM_TEAM, so the team rides --hcom-team below.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || refuse "regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
regime_env hcom-seat || exit 2
# The derived store and seats root reach the srt settings as well.
for var in HCOM_DIR REGIME_SEATS_ROOT; do
    if [[ -n ${!var:-} ]]; then require_clean_path "${var}" "${!var}"; fi
done
command -v hcom > /dev/null || refuse 'hcom not found on PATH'
[[ ${HCOM_TEAM:-} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || refuse "team '${HCOM_TEAM:-}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$"
policy=${HOME}/.agents/omp/policies/${role}.yml
profile=${HOME}/.agents/omp/profiles/${role}.yml
[[ -f ${policy} ]] || refuse "policy overlay absent: ${policy}"
[[ -f ${profile} ]] || refuse "profile overlay absent: ${profile}"
rules=${HOME}/.agents/omp/rules/${role}.md
[[ -f ${rules} && -s ${rules} ]] || refuse "standing rules absent or empty: ${rules}"
if ((${#user_exts[@]})); then
    exts=("${user_exts[@]}")
elif [[ ! -d ${exts[1]} ]]; then
    exts=("${exts[0]}")
fi
# The stop gate rides every launch, after the route's extensions; --ext never drops it (U33c).
exts+=("${gate}")
# The extension allow-list (regime-cutover U31): claude.levers.extensions in the manifest the self-check read, so the
# installed copy reads it from ~/.agents, outside every sandbox write root. A read failure is a refusal, not an empty list.
allowed=$(awk '
    /^  levers:$/ { levers = 1; next }
    levers && /^  [^ ]/ { levers = 0 }
    levers && /^    extensions:$/ { list = 1; next }
    list && /^      - / { sub(/^      - /, ""); print; next }
    list { list = 0 }
' "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || refuse "cannot read the extension allow-list in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
[[ -n ${allowed} ]] || refuse "no extension allow-list (claude.levers.extensions) in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
# The launch passes the canonical allow-list entry (`pwd -P` of the listed path), never the caller's spelling: a
# symlink the caller controls could be swapped between this check and omp resolving `-e`.
checked=()
for ext in "${exts[@]}"; do
    [[ -d ${ext} ]] || refuse "extension directory absent: ${ext}"
    real=$(cd "${ext}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve extension directory: ${ext}"
    listed=''
    while IFS= read -r entry; do
        entry=${entry/#\~/${HOME}}
        # An entry that is absent or cannot be resolved lists nothing, so the extension stays refused.
        [[ -d ${entry} ]] || continue
        entry_real=$(cd "${entry}" && pwd -P) || continue
        if [[ ${entry_real} -ef ${real} ]]; then listed=${entry_real}; fi
    done <<< "${allowed}"
    [[ -n ${listed} ]] || refuse "extension directory is not in the allow-list (claude.levers.extensions): ${ext}"
    checked+=("${listed}")
done
exts=("${checked[@]}")
# git names the checkout and its git directories; they must be the ones found (and checked) before git ran, by
# identity, or git reads state the check never saw (GIT_DIR, core.worktree, a pointer git reads differently).
[[ -n ${top} ]] || refuse 'run hcom-seat inside the repository checkout'
git_paths_of 3 rev-parse --path-format=absolute --show-toplevel --git-dir --git-common-dir
repo=${git_paths[0]}
launch_gitdir=${git_paths[1]}
common=${git_paths[2]}
[[ ${repo} -ef ${top} && ${git_paths[1]} -ef ${gitdir} && ${common} -ef ${early_common} ]] ||
    refuse "git resolves the checkout ${repo}, git directory ${git_paths[1]} and common directory ${common}, not ${top}, ${gitdir} and ${early_common} found before it ran"
seats_root=${seats_root:-${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:-}}
[[ -n ${seats_root} ]] || refuse 'no seats root: pass --seats-root or run inside a checkout'
case ${role} in
orchestrator) dir=${repo} ;;
*) dir=${seats_root}/${name} ;;
esac

# @description Fill the identity table for the physical paths `$@` (regime-cutover U95), which every containment
#   decision of the overlap check reads: per path, whether it exists, the (device, inode) identities of its deepest
#   existing ancestor (the path itself when it exists) and of every directory above it, and the absent remainder below
#   that ancestor, ASCII case-folded by ascii_lower (builtins only). One `/usr/bin/stat` (through xargs, order kept)
#   serves every path, instead of several processes per pair. Fail-closed per record: every input must be a clean path; every identity line must be `<dev>:<ino>`, and
#   their number exactly what the ancestor walks asked for; every folded remainder must have its input's length and
#   the grammar `(/<lower-case component>)*/`; each table must hold one entry per input.
# @set tbl_exists 1 or 0 per path.
# @set tbl_first The identity of the deepest existing ancestor per path.
# @set tbl_chain `\n<id>\n<id>…\n` per path: that ancestor's identity first, then each directory above it.
# @set tbl_rest The absent remainder per path, case-folded, ending in `/` (`/` when the path exists).
identity_table() {
    local p d rest ids line folded chain='' i=0 k=0 all=() counts=()
    tbl_exists=() tbl_first=() tbl_chain=() tbl_rest=()
    for p in "$@"; do
        require_clean_path 'a seat path' "${p}"
        # Absolute, so each step shortens it and the walk ends at `/`, which exists.
        d=${p} rest=''
        while [[ ! -e ${d} && ! -L ${d} ]]; do
            rest=/${d##*/}${rest}
            d=${d%/*}
            [[ -n ${d} ]] || d=/
        done
        if [[ -e ${p} ]]; then tbl_exists+=(1); else tbl_exists+=(0); fi
        ancestors_of "${d}"
        all+=("${ancestors[@]}")
        counts+=("${#ancestors[@]}")
        rest=${rest}/
        ascii_lower "${rest}" folded || refuse "cannot fold the absent part of ${p}"
        [[ ${#folded} == "${#rest}" && ${folded} =~ ^(/[a-z0-9._@+-]+)*/$ ]] ||
            refuse "cannot fold the absent part of ${p} ('${folded}')"
        tbl_rest+=("${folded}")
    done
    (($#)) || return 0
    ids=$(printf '%s\0' "${all[@]}" | /usr/bin/xargs -0 /usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" --) ||
        refuse "cannot read the identity of a seat path or a directory above it"
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ ${line} =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "cannot read the identity of a seat path ('${line}')"
        ((i < ${#counts[@]})) || refuse 'more identities than seat paths were read'
        if ((k == 0)); then tbl_first+=("${line}"); fi
        chain+=${line}$'\n'
        k=$((k + 1))
        if ((k == counts[i])); then
            tbl_chain+=($'\n'"${chain}")
            chain='' k=0 i=$((i + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "${ids}"
    ((i == $# && k == 0)) || refuse "cannot read the identity of every seat path (${i} of $#)"
    ((${#tbl_exists[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_first[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_chain[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_rest[@]} == $#)) ||
        refuse 'the identity table does not hold one entry per seat path'
}

# @description Set the variable named `$2` to `$1` with A-Z made a-z (regime-cutover U95), by builtins only (a case
#   table, no `tr` and no locale; bash 3.2 has no `${x,,}`), so no producer's output is read back.
# @arg $1 string ASCII text.
# @arg $2 string The name of the variable to set.
# @exitcode 1 The variable cannot be set.
ascii_lower() {
    # The locals carry a prefix, so the caller's variable `$2` is never one of them (printf -v sets the nearest).
    local LC_ALL=C al_text=$1 al_out='' al_c al_before al_upper=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
    local al_lower=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
    [[ $2 != al_* && $2 != LC_ALL ]] || return 1
    while [[ -n ${al_text} ]]; do
        al_c=${al_text:0:1}
        al_text=${al_text:1}
        case ${al_c} in
        [ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ])
            al_before=${al_upper%%"${al_c}"*}
            al_c=${al_lower:${#al_before}:1}
            ;;
        esac
        al_out+=${al_c}
    done
    printf -v "$2" '%s' "${al_out}"
}

# @description Decide from the identity table whether path `$2` is path `$1` or lies under it (regime-cutover U85,
#   U95), by identity for everything that exists, so a case alias on a case-insensitive volume is the path it aliases.
#   When `$1` exists: yes iff `$1`'s identity is in `$2`'s chain (`$2`'s deepest existing ancestor or a directory
#   above it). When `$1` does not exist, an existing `$2` cannot lie under it (no). When neither exists, `$2` can lie
#   under `$1` only if both have the same deepest existing ancestor; below it nothing exists, so no link or alias can
#   intervene, and the absent remainders decide: yes iff `$1`'s is `$2`'s or a prefix of it on a component boundary
#   (`a/b` is no prefix of `a/bc`), compared ASCII case-folded, since on a case-insensitive volume two spellings that
#   differ by case become one directory once made. No process runs.
# @arg $1 int The table index of the outer path.
# @arg $2 int The table index of the inner path.
# @exitcode 0 `$2` is `$1` or lies under it.
# @exitcode 1 It does not.
within_ix() {
    if ((tbl_exists[$1])); then
        [[ ${tbl_chain[$2]} == *$'\n'"${tbl_first[$1]}"$'\n'* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
        return
    fi
    ((! tbl_exists[$2])) || return 1
    [[ ${tbl_first[$1]} == "${tbl_first[$2]}" ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
    [[ ${tbl_rest[$2]} == "${tbl_rest[$1]}"* ]]              # lint-comparisons: allow absent components below one ancestor of the same identity, compared on component boundaries
}

# @description Set `phys_list` to the physical form of each absolute path `$@`, in order (regime-cutover U95), or
#   refuse (exit 2), in one subshell for all of them, present or absent. In that subshell a path's deepest existing entry is found with builtins (physical_path's
#   walk); it must be a directory, which `cd -P` resolves, and the absent rest is appended, as physical_path does.
#   The inputs are worktree records (git's list and the admin directories' `gitdir`) and seat directories: a path
#   that is, or lies below, a regular file or a dangling link is no directory-backed worktree but a corrupt record,
#   and refuses, naming `git worktree prune` and `git worktree repair` (no per-record fallback). Fail-closed per record: the subshell writes exactly one record per path,
#   `ok<TAB><physical path>` after a `cd -P` whose status was 0, `notdir` for a path not backed by a directory, or
#   `fail` after a failed `cd`, and fails when a record cannot be written. Each record is checked against its
#   grammar and its result assigned to its own index (nothing is printed and read back): only `ok` with a clean
#   path passes. Anything else, a record too many or too few, or an index left without its result refuses.
# @arg $@ string Absolute paths free of control characters.
# @set phys_list The physical paths, one per input.
physical_paths() {
    local out line resolved i=0 args=("$@")
    phys_list=()
    (($#)) || return 0
    out=$(for p in "$@"; do
        rest=''
        while [[ ! -e ${p} && ! -L ${p} ]]; do
            rest=/${p##*/}${rest}
            p=${p%/*}
            [[ -n ${p} ]] || p=/
        done
        if [[ ! -d ${p} ]]; then
            printf 'notdir\n' || exit 1
        elif [[ ${p} == / ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the root itself, whose `cd //` form pwd prints as `//`
            printf 'ok\t%s\n' "${rest:-/}" || exit 1
        elif cd -P -- "${p}/" 2> /dev/null; then
            printf 'ok\t%s%s\n' "${PWD%/}" "${rest}" || exit 1
        else
            printf 'fail\n' || exit 1
        fi
    done) || refuse 'cannot resolve the paths (the resolving subshell failed)'
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        ((i < $#)) || refuse 'cannot resolve the paths (more records than paths)'
        case ${line} in
        notdir) refuse "the worktree record ${args[i]} is not backed by a directory: it, or its deepest existing ancestor, is a regular file or a dangling symbolic link, so the record is corrupt; run \`git worktree prune\` if the worktree is gone, or \`git worktree repair\` if it moved" ;;
        ok$'\t'*) resolved=${line#ok$'\t'} ;;
        *) refuse "cannot resolve the path ${args[i]} ('${line}')" ;;
        esac
        clean_path "${resolved}" || refuse "the path ${args[i]} resolves to '${resolved}', not a clean absolute path"
        phys_list[i]=${resolved}
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "${out}"
    ((i == $# && ${#phys_list[@]} == $#)) || refuse "cannot resolve every path (${#phys_list[@]} of $#)"
}

# @description Set `worktree_paths` to the worktrees git records for this repository, main worktree first, and
#   `main_bare` to 1 when that record is a bare repository (regime-cutover U85). `git worktree list --porcelain -z`
#   is read whole: NUL-terminated fields, each turned into one line (a newline inside a field becomes \001, a control
#   character, refused in a path); every path must be absolute and free of control characters.
# @set worktree_paths The worktree paths, as git prints them.
# @set main_bare 1 for a bare main record, else 0.
worktree_records() {
    local listing line record=0
    listing=$({ git -C "${repo}" worktree list --porcelain -z | /usr/bin/tr '\0\n' '\n\001'; } && printf .) ||
        refuse "git cannot list the worktrees of ${repo}"
    listing=${listing%.}
    worktree_paths=()
    main_bare=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case ${line} in
        '') record=$((record + 1)) ;;
        'worktree '*)
            line=${line#worktree }
            [[ ${line} == /* && ${line} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
                refuse "git names the worktree '${line}', not an absolute path free of control characters"
            worktree_paths+=("${line}")
            ;;
        bare) if ((record == 0)); then main_bare=1; fi ;;
        esac
    done <<< "${listing}"
    ((${#worktree_paths[@]} > 0)) || refuse "git lists no worktree of ${repo}"
}

# The main checkout, by identity, never by the common directory's spelling (a `.GIT` on a case-insensitive volume is
# `.git`): the common directory's parent when that parent's `.git` is the common directory; else the main worktree
# git records. A bare repository has none, and the launch checkout stands in. For a separate git directory git
# records the git directory itself as the main worktree, so its checkout is known only when the launch runs in it
# (its git directory is the common directory); from another worktree of it the launch is refused.
worktree_records
common_parent=$(physical_path "${common}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common}"
common_parent=${common_parent%/*}
common_parent=${common_parent:-/}
if [[ -d ${common_parent}/.git && ! -L ${common_parent}/.git && ${common_parent}/.git -ef ${common} ]]; then
    checkout=${common_parent}
elif ((main_bare)); then
    checkout=$(physical_path "${repo}") || refuse "cannot resolve the checkout ${repo}"
elif [[ ${worktree_paths[0]} -ef ${common} ]]; then
    [[ ${launch_gitdir} -ef ${common} ]] ||
        refuse "git records no main checkout for the separate git directory ${common}; launch from that checkout"
    checkout=$(physical_path "${repo}") || refuse "cannot resolve the checkout ${repo}"
else
    checkout=$(physical_path "${worktree_paths[0]}") || refuse "cannot resolve the main checkout ${worktree_paths[0]}"
fi

# OS containment (regime-cutover U85): the seat's omp runs under Anthropic's sandbox-runtime (`srt`, sandbox-exec on
# macOS, bubblewrap on Linux). hcom pins the `omp` it finds first on this process's PATH as the runner's
# --hcom-tool-path, so a per-seat shim placed first on PATH is what the pane runs; the shim never falls back to an
# uncontained omp. Every prerequisite is checked here, before anything is created or started.
sandbox=${seats_root%/}/.sandbox/${name}
# Every seat's sandbox denies reads of <seats-root>/.sandbox (refuse_inside_a_seat).
refuse_inside_a_seat "${seats_root%/}/.sandbox"

# @description Print the srt write roots of one seat, one per line in physical form: the list the seat's settings
#   carry as `allowWrite` (seat_sandbox_write writes exactly this list), followed by the paths srt 0.0.81 makes
#   writable without a listing (`srt_tmp_roots`: `/tmp/claude`, and `/private/tmp/claude` on macOS; `~/.npm/_logs`,
#   `~/.claude/debug`).
# @arg $1 string The role.
# @arg $2 string The seat name.
# @arg $3 string The seat directory (the worktree, or the checkout for the orchestrator).
# @stdout The roots.
# @exitcode 1 A path could not be resolved.
seat_write_roots() {
    local path claude=${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-${HOME}/.claude}
    # The seat's own slots come first (seat_overlap_check relies on it): its directory, then its state directory.
    for path in "$3" "${seats_root%/}/.state/$2" "${common}" "${HCOM_DIR}" "${HOME}/.omp/profiles/$1" "${HOME}/.omp/run" \
        "${claude}" "${HOME}/.claude.json" "${srt_tmp_roots[@]}" "${HOME}/.npm/_logs" "${HOME}/.claude/debug"; do
        physical_path "${path}" || return 1
    done
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless a seat's own slots under the seats root are what the overlap check's exemption
#   takes them for (regime-cutover U85): `<seats-root>/.state`, `<seats-root>/.state/<name>` and, for a worker,
#   `<seats-root>/<name>` are each no symbolic link, a directory when they exist, and, when they exist, their physical
#   parent has the identity of the physical seats root (resp. `.state`) and their physical basename is the name they
#   are spelled with. A `.state/<name> -> ..` or `<name> -> /` would otherwise resolve the slot to a wider root that
#   the exemption skips. It runs before anything resolves those paths (lstat first, then physical_path), so a slot
#   that is a link is refused before any link is followed. Missing slots are created later, one component at a time
#   (seat_sandbox_write).
# @arg $1 string The role.
# @arg $2 string The seat name.
own_slots_check() {
    local slot parent real seats_phys slots=("${seats_root}/.state" "${seats_root}/.state/$2")
    [[ $1 == orchestrator ]] || slots+=("${seats_root}/$2")
    seats_phys=$(physical_path "${seats_root}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${seats_root}"
    for slot in "${slots[@]}"; do
        [[ ! -L ${slot} ]] || refuse "the seat slot ${slot} is a symbolic link; a seat's own slots must be real directories"
        [[ -e ${slot} ]] || continue
        [[ -d ${slot} ]] || refuse "the seat slot ${slot} is not a directory"
        real=$(physical_path "${slot}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seat slot ${slot}"
        parent=${slot%/*}
        [[ ${real%/*} -ef ${parent} && ${parent} -ef ${seats_phys}${parent#"${seats_root}"} ]] ||
            refuse "the seat slot ${slot} does not sit in ${parent}"
        [[ ${real##*/} == "${slot##*/}" ]] || refuse "the seat slot ${slot} resolves to ${real}" # lint-comparisons: allow a basename test, the parent by identity
    done
}
own_slots_check "${role}" "${name}"
own_slots_check orchestrator orchestrator

# The exact roots (regime-cutover U85): this seat's `allowWrite` list, from the same function that writes the
# settings, so the check and the sandbox cannot drift, and the other role's; the derived seats root and hcom store;
# and every settings file under the derived seats root. Their identities join the set computed before any tool ran
# (which already covers them by their parents); every link, mise included, is then checked again.
seat_write=()
seat_roots_out=$(seat_write_roots "${role}" "${name}" "${dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the write roots of ${name}"
while IFS= read -r root; do seat_write+=("${root}"); done <<< "${seat_roots_out}"
other_roots=$(seat_write_roots orchestrator orchestrator "${repo}") || refuse 'cannot resolve the orchestrator write roots'

# Every linked worktree git records, resolved once for both overlap checks (the first record is the main worktree).
worktree_phys=()
if ((${#worktree_paths[@]} > 1)); then
    physical_paths "${worktree_paths[@]:1}"
    worktree_phys=("${phys_list[@]}")
fi

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless the admin directories in `<common>/worktrees` (dir_entries, dot names included)
#   are, one to one, the git directories of the linked worktrees git lists (regime-cutover U95): each admin directory's
#   `gitdir` names, the way git reads it (worktree.c get_linked_worktree: trailing `/.git` stripped, a relative path
#   resolved against the admin directory), a worktree git lists, no two name the same one, and their number is the
#   number git lists. So every consumer (the git-state denies, the shape check, the overlap check) sees the same set:
#   an admin directory no listed worktree owns, or one the scan missed, refuses. Sameness is identity, never text:
#   `cd -P` keeps a spelling's case, so on a case-insensitive volume `trees/a` and `TREES/A` are one directory under
#   two texts. Each path's key is its identity_table entry, the (device, inode) of its deepest existing ancestor
#   followed by the case-folded absent rest (`/` for an existing path), the same rule within_ix decides by. One read,
#   one resolving batch and one identity table.
# @arg $1 string The physical git common directory.
admin_dirs_match() {
    local a v key listed=$'\n' seen=$'\n' i n derived=() gitdirs=()
    dir_entries "$1/worktrees"
    ((${#dir_list[@]} == ${#admin_dirs[@]})) ||
        refuse "the worktree git directories of $1 changed while hcom-seat ran (${#dir_list[@]} now, ${#admin_dirs[@]} checked)"
    ((${#admin_dirs[@]} == ${#worktree_phys[@]})) ||
        refuse "$1/worktrees holds ${#admin_dirs[@]} worktree git directories but git lists ${#worktree_phys[@]} linked worktrees; an entry no listed worktree owns cannot be checked${git_fix_hint}"
    n=${#worktree_phys[@]}
    ((n)) || return 0
    for a in "${admin_dirs[@]}"; do
        [[ -f ${a}/gitdir && ! -L ${a}/gitdir ]] ||
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${a} has no regular gitdir file, so git lists no worktree for it${git_fix_hint}"
        gitdirs+=("${a}/gitdir")
    done
    pointer_values "${gitdirs[@]}"
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        git_form_path "${pointer_list[i]}" ||
            refuse "${gitdirs[i]} holds '${pointer_list[i]}', not a path in git's own form (no trailing /, no . component, .. only leading a relative path)${git_fix_hint}"
        v=${pointer_list[i]%/.git}
        case ${v} in # lint-comparisons: allow a relative operand is made absolute, no path compare
        /*) derived+=("${v}") ;;
        *) derived+=("${admin_dirs[i]}/${v}") ;;
        esac
    done
    physical_paths "${derived[@]}"
    ((${#phys_list[@]} == n)) || refuse "the worktrees the git directories of $1 record were not all resolved"
    # Listed worktrees at indices 0..n-1, recorded ones at n..2n-1.
    identity_table "${worktree_phys[@]}" "${phys_list[@]}"
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do listed+=${tbl_first[i]}${tbl_rest[i]}$'\n'; done
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        v=${phys_list[i]}
        key=${tbl_first[n + i]}${tbl_rest[n + i]}
        [[ ${listed} == *$'\n'"${key}"$'\n'* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities with case-folded absent rests, not paths
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${admin_dirs[i]} records ${v}, which git does not list as a worktree${git_fix_hint}"
        [[ ${seen} != *$'\n'"${key}"$'\n'* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities with case-folded absent rests, not paths
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${admin_dirs[i]} records ${v}, which another worktree git directory records too (the same directory by identity)${git_fix_hint}"
        seen+=${key}$'\n'
    done
}
if ((${#worktree_paths[@]} > 1 || ${#admin_dirs[@]} > 0)); then admin_dirs_match "${early_common}"; fi

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless the final `allowWrite` list of one seat keeps clear of every protected path
#   (regime-cutover U85), one invariant instead of a list of cases: for every granted root R and every protected
#   path P, R must not be or contain P, and R must not lie inside P. The protected paths are defined once: the main
#   checkout, the seats root, its `.sandbox`, every other seat directory under the seats root and every other
#   worktree of this repository; the seat's own directory (same identity) is not protected for it. Exempt by
#   construction, not by comparing text: the seat's own slots under the seats root (the first two roots: a worker's
#   `<seats-root>/<name>`, and `<seats-root>/.state/<name>`) against the seats root and its `.sandbox`, and the git
#   common directory named `.git` whose parent is the main checkout (identity). A linked worktree inside R (Claude
#   Code keeps its worktrees under `<checkout>/.claude/worktrees`) refuses, present or absent, naming the worktree
#   and `git worktree move`, `remove` or `prune` (regime-cutover U95, operator decision U95-nested-refuse-decided:
#   a seat could rewrite its `.git` file and tracked files, which host git and host tools read). Containment is
#   decided by identity for everything that exists, and below one shared deepest existing ancestor by the absent
#   components (identity_table, within_ix), one table for every pair. Every path must be clean (clean_path) before
#   anything is created, so this runs in a dry run too.
# @arg $1 string The role.
# @arg $2 string The seat directory, physical.
# @arg $@ string The seat's allowWrite roots after them, physical, its own slots first (seat_write_roots).
seat_overlap_check() {
    local own_role=$1 own_dir=$2 r p i j k nroots seats_phys labels=() protected=() own=() roots=() seat_dirs=()
    shift 2
    roots=("$@")
    nroots=$#
    seats_phys=$(physical_path "${seats_root}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${seats_root}"
    labels+=("the main checkout" "the seats root" "the seats' sandbox directory")
    protected+=("${checkout}" "${seats_phys}" "${seats_phys}/.sandbox")
    # Every directory in the seats root, dot names included (dir_entries); `.state` and `.sandbox` are protected or
    # exempt by their own rules above. All resolved in one batch (physical_paths), so more seats start no process.
    dir_entries "${seats_phys}"
    seat_dirs=()
    for p in ${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"}; do
        [[ -d ${p} ]] || continue
        case ${p##*/} in .state | .sandbox) continue ;; esac
        seat_dirs+=("${p}")
    done
    physical_paths ${seat_dirs[@]+"${seat_dirs[@]}"}
    ((${#phys_list[@]} == ${#seat_dirs[@]})) ||
        refuse "the seat directories in ${seats_phys} were not all resolved (${#phys_list[@]} of ${#seat_dirs[@]})"
    for p in ${phys_list[@]+"${phys_list[@]}"}; do
        labels+=("the seat directory")
        protected+=("${p}")
    done
    # One resolved path per linked worktree git records (physical_paths), or the check below could miss one.
    ((${#worktree_phys[@]} == ${#worktree_paths[@]} - 1)) ||
        refuse "the worktrees of ${repo} were not all resolved (${#worktree_phys[@]} of $((${#worktree_paths[@]} - 1)))"
    for p in ${worktree_phys[@]+"${worktree_phys[@]}"}; do
        labels+=("the worktree")
        protected+=("${p}")
    done
    for p in "${protected[@]}"; do
        require_clean_path 'a protected seat path' "${p}"
        # The seat's own directory is its to write.
        if [[ -e ${p} && ${p} -ef ${own_dir} ]]; then own+=(1); else own+=(0); fi
    done
    ((${#own[@]} == ${#protected[@]})) || refuse "the overlap table of the ${own_role} seat does not hold one entry per protected path"
    for r in "${roots[@]}"; do
        require_clean_path "a write root of the ${own_role} seat" "${r}"
    done
    identity_table "${roots[@]}" "${protected[@]}"
    for ((k = 0; k < nroots; k++)); do
        r=${roots[k]}
        for ((i = 0; i < ${#protected[@]}; i++)); do
            ((! own[i])) || continue
            # Its own slots under the seats root sit there by construction, as siblings of `.sandbox`: the state
            # directory of every seat, and a worker's directory (the orchestrator's is the launch checkout, checked).
            # own_slots_check has proved, before this runs, that they are what they claim (no link, right parent).
            if [[ (${k} == 1 || (${k} == 0 && ${own_role} != orchestrator)) && (${i} == 1 || ${i} == 2) ]]; then continue; fi
            p=${protected[i]}
            j=$((nroots + i))
            if within_ix "${k}" "${j}"; then
                if [[ ${labels[i]} == 'the worktree' ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a fixed label, no path compare
                    refuse "the worktree ${p} lies inside the ${own_role} seat's write root ${r}, where the seat could rewrite its .git file and tracked files; move it out (\`git worktree move ${p} <a path outside>\`), remove it (\`git worktree remove ${p}\`), or prune it if its directory is gone (\`git worktree prune\`)"
                fi
                refuse "the ${own_role} seat's write root ${r} contains ${labels[i]} ${p}; seat write roots must not overlap (choose another --seats-root, HCOM_DIR or git directory)"
            fi
            if within_ix "${j}" "${k}"; then
                # The main checkout's own `.git`, by identity of the common directory and its parent.
                if ((i == 0)) && [[ -e ${r} && ${r} -ef ${common} && -d ${checkout}/.git && ! -L ${checkout}/.git && ${checkout}/.git -ef ${r} ]]; then continue; fi
                refuse "the ${own_role} seat's write root ${r} lies inside ${labels[i]} ${p}; seat write roots must not overlap (choose another --seats-root, HCOM_DIR or git directory)"
            fi
        done
    done
}

dir_phys=$(physical_path "${dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seat directory ${dir}"
seat_overlap_check "${role}" "${dir_phys}" "${seat_write[@]}"
orchestrator_write=()
while IFS= read -r root; do orchestrator_write+=("${root}"); done <<< "${other_roots}"
# The orchestrator's own directory is the launch checkout (`${repo}`, a linked worktree or the main checkout), the
# directory its write list holds; the main checkout stays protected for it only when it is not that checkout.
repo_phys=$(physical_path "${repo}") || refuse "cannot resolve the launch checkout ${repo}"
seat_overlap_check orchestrator "${repo_phys}" "${orchestrator_write[@]}"
roots=("${seat_write[@]}" "${seats_root}" "${HCOM_DIR}" "${common}")
while IFS= read -r root; do roots+=("${root}"); done <<< "${other_roots}"
seat_settings_files "${seats_root}"
for settings_file in ${settings_files[@]+"${settings_files[@]}"}; do
    [[ -e ${settings_file} ]] || continue
    listed=$(allow_write_list "${os}" "${settings_file}") ||
        refuse "cannot read a clean allowWrite list from ${settings_file}"
    while IFS= read -r root; do
        if [[ -n ${root} ]]; then roots+=("${root}"); fi
    done <<< "${listed}"
done
add_roots "${roots[@]}"
if [[ -n ${mise_real} ]]; then PATH=${system_path} pin_exec mise "${mise_real}"; fi

# Every link in the private tool directory, with its interpreter chain, is re-checked against the exact set, and PATH
# is that directory and the system directories, so hcom's own lookups (`herdr`, `node`) and srt's (`env`, the shell)
# find nothing a seat writes.
for link in "${tools_dir}"/*; do
    [[ -e ${link} || -L ${link} ]] || continue
    pin_exec "${link##*/}" "${link}"
    for tool in "${optional_tools[@]}"; do
        if [[ ${tool} == "${link##*/}" ]]; then trusted_interpreter_check "${tool}"; fi
    done
done
pin_exec git "${git_path}"
git_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
IFS=: read -r -a path_dirs <<< "${PATH}"
for path_dir in "${path_dirs[@]}"; do
    path_real=$(physical_path "${path_dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the PATH entry ${path_dir}"
    refuse_if_seat_writable 'the PATH entry' "${path_real}"
done
pinned=()
omp_path=$(find_on_path omp) || refuse 'omp not found in the private tool directory'
pin_exec omp "${omp_path}"
omp_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
srt_path=$(find_on_path srt) || refuse 'srt (@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime) not found in the private tool directory'
pin_exec srt "${srt_path}"
srt_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
# hcom and the herdr it drives run outside every sandbox: the launch execs hcom by its physical argv, and hcom finds
# `hcom` and `herdr` through the shim directory first on PATH, as wrappers around their physical argv.
hcom_path=$(find_on_path hcom) || refuse 'hcom not found on PATH'
pin_exec hcom "${hcom_path}"
hcom_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
herdr_path=$(find_on_path herdr) || refuse 'herdr not found on PATH'
pin_exec herdr "${herdr_path}"
herdr_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
os=$(uname -s) || refuse 'cannot read the operating system name (uname -s)'
linux_tools=''
case ${os} in
Darwin) [[ -x /usr/bin/sandbox-exec ]] || refuse 'sandbox-exec absent: /usr/bin/sandbox-exec' ;;
Linux)
    # srt looks bwrap, socat and rg up on PATH unless its settings name them; they name the checked physical files.
    # srt runs them by these paths, so a script among them (whose interpreter the kernel would look up) is refused.
    bwrap_real='' socat_real='' rg_real=''
    for tool in bwrap socat rg; do
        pin_exec "${tool}" "${tools_dir}/${tool}"
        ((${#pinned[@]} == 1)) || refuse "${tool} ${pinned[1]} is a script; srt runs it by path, so it must be a binary"
        case ${tool} in
        bwrap) bwrap_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        socat) socat_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        rg) rg_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        esac
    done
    require_clean_path bwrap "${bwrap_real}"
    require_clean_path socat "${socat_real}"
    require_clean_path rg "${rg_real}"
    linux_tools=",\"bwrapPath\":\"${bwrap_real}\",\"socatPath\":\"${socat_real}\",\"ripgrep\":{\"command\":\"${rg_real}\"}"
    ;;
*) refuse "no seat sandbox for ${os}; srt supports macOS and Linux" ;;
esac
# @description Write the seat's srt settings and its `omp` shim under `<seats-root>/.sandbox/<name>` (regime-cutover
#   U85), afresh on every launch, after the seat directory exists. The settings name what the seat may write (its
#   directory, the repository's git common directory, the program's hcom store, its own omp profile and the omp
#   session leases, the Claude Code state the bridge child writes, a per-seat cache root; the same for both roles, so
#   no seat writes the seats root or reaches the herdr socket, and none can start a seat), what it may not change
#   inside those roots (git config and hooks, the hcom store's launch scripts and configuration, agent configuration
#   that runs outside the seat), what it may not read (SSH, GPG, cloud and codex credentials, the chezmoi sources,
#   `~/Workspace` but its own repository, other omp profiles, other hcom stores, every seat's sandbox directory, and
#   for a worker the other seats) and the hosts it may reach. The shim runs a canary under those settings first, a
#   write into the sandbox directory and reads of the settings file and `~/.ssh`, and refuses (exit 2) unless all
#   three fail inside; only then does it run omp under srt, both by the physical argv `pin_exec` checked.
# @noargs
seat_sandbox_write() {
    local h claude dir_real common_real hcom_real seats_real sandbox_real
    local root path settings shim json base sandbox_state origin_url push_url srt_q omp_q
    local write_json deny_write_json deny_read_json allow_read_json
    local write=() deny_write=() deny_read=() allow_read=()
    # srt on Linux grants writes only to paths that exist, so omp's own state directories are made first. The seat's
    # slots under the seats root were proved free of links (own_slots_check); they are made one component at a time,
    # and each is checked again to be a real directory.
    (umask 077 && mkdir -p "${seats_root}" "${HOME}/.omp/profiles/${role}" "${HOME}/.omp/run") ||
        refuse "cannot create the seats root ${seats_root} or omp's state directories"
    for path in "${seats_root}/.state" "${seats_root}/.state/${name}" "${seats_root}/.sandbox" "${sandbox}" \
        "${sandbox}/bin"; do
        if [[ ! -e ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]]; then
            (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${path}") || refuse "cannot create ${path}"
        fi
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "${path} is not a real directory"
    done
    h=$(physical_path "${HOME}") || refuse "cannot resolve HOME ${HOME}"
    claude=${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-${h}/.claude}
    dir_real=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the seat directory ${dir}"
    common_real=$(cd "${common}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common}"
    hcom_real=$(cd "${HCOM_DIR}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR}"
    seats_real=$(cd "${seats_root}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${seats_root}"
    sandbox_real=$(cd "${sandbox}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the seat sandbox directory ${sandbox}"
    sandbox_state=${seats_real}/.state/${name}
    # Exactly the list the protected set was built from (seat_write_roots), so the check and the sandbox cannot drift.
    write=("${seat_write[@]}")
    deny_write=("${seats_real}/.sandbox")
    for base in "${dir_real}" "${checkout}"; do
        deny_write+=("${base}/.claude/settings.json" "${base}/.claude/settings.local.json" "${base}/.claude/hooks"
            "${base}/.omp" "${base}/.codex" "${base}/.envrc" "${base}/.mcp.json")
    done
    # The git state host git reads for any worktree of this repository (regime-cutover U85): a seat that could write
    # it could make a later host git command run a program of its choosing (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`,
    # filter and textconv drivers, includes). git_state_check refuses a launch over such state and creates the files
    # that are absent, so each deny below names an existing path (srt on Linux binds only existing paths).
    git_state_check "${common_real}" "${dir_real}"
    deny_write+=("${git_state[@]}")
    # A worktree created after this launch gets its files denied on macOS by pattern; on Linux srt takes literal
    # write denies only, and the next launch's git_state_check covers it.
    # The patterns are the one place a settings entry is not a clean path: a clean prefix and a fixed suffix.
    deny_write_patterns=''
    if [[ ${os} == Darwin ]]; then
        require_clean_path 'the git common directory' "${common_real}"
        for path in config.worktree info commondir gitdir; do
            # srt reads `*` as `[^/]*` (glob-pattern.js:179-180, globToRegex :208-209), so dot-named ids match too.
            deny_write_patterns+=",\"${common_real}/worktrees/*/${path}\""
        done
    fi
    for path in config.toml env config.env .tmp/launch scripts integrations shell_env.json; do
        deny_write+=("${hcom_real}/${path}")
    done
    for path in settings.json settings.local.json hooks plugins commands agents skills CLAUDE.md; do
        deny_write+=("${claude}/${path}")
    done
    deny_read=("${h}/.ssh" "${h}/.gnupg" "${h}/.aws" "${h}/.netrc" "${h}/.docker" "${h}/.kube" "${h}/.config/gcloud"
        "${h}/.codex" "${h}/.omp/agent" "${h}/.omp/profiles" "${h}/.hcom" "${h}/.local/state/hcom"
        "${h}/.local/share/chezmoi" "${h}/.local/share/chezmoi-private" "${h}/.config/chezmoi"
        "${h}/.config/chezmoi-private" "${h}/Workspace" "${seats_real}/.sandbox")
    # Every program's seats root is unreadable but this seat's own paths: the whole ~/.local/state/omp-seats tree
    # and every configured seats root. srt keeps a deeper deny under an allow (measured, 0.0.81), so each
    # `.sandbox` stays unreadable inside an allowed root.
    deny_read+=("${h}/.local/state/omp-seats" "${seats_real}")
    if [[ -n ${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:-} ]]; then
        root=$(physical_path "${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT}"
        deny_read+=("${root}")
    fi
    allow_read=("${dir_real}" "${common_real}" "${hcom_real}" "${h}/.omp/profiles/${role}" "${sandbox_state}")
    # The main checkout is unreadable to a worker wherever it lives, but for its git directory (the worktree's objects
    # and refs) and the coordinator's records (briefs, verdict files), read by absolute path.
    if [[ ${role} != orchestrator ]]; then deny_read+=("${checkout}"); fi
    allow_read+=("${checkout}/.orchestration/orchestrate")
    # The orchestrator reads the worker clones of its own program, which it reviews; a worker reads no other seat.
    if [[ ${role} == orchestrator ]]; then allow_read+=("${seats_real}"); fi
    settings=${sandbox_real}/srt-settings.json
    write_json=$(json_paths 'a seat write root' "${write[@]}") || exit 2
    deny_write_json=$(json_paths 'a seat write deny' "${deny_write[@]}") || exit 2
    deny_write_json=${deny_write_json%]}${deny_write_patterns}]
    deny_read_json=$(json_paths 'a seat read deny' "${deny_read[@]}") || exit 2
    allow_read_json=$(json_paths 'a seat read root' "${allow_read[@]}") || exit 2
    # No unix socket for any seat: the herdr socket would let a seat open a pane outside every sandbox. No local
    # binding either: srt 0.0.81 grants it as bind and inbound on `*:*` (every interface); the one listener a seat
    # runs, the hcom plugin's notify server, falls back to polling every 5 s when its bind fails (hcom.ts
    # `startNotifyServer`, `FALLBACK_PENDING_POLL_MS`). The settings are written by the shell from clean paths only
    # (json_paths), so no JSON tool runs and none is needed on macOS.
    domains='"github.com","api.github.com","uploads.github.com","codeload.github.com","objects.githubusercontent.com"'
    domains+=',"raw.githubusercontent.com","release-assets.githubusercontent.com","pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org"'
    domains+=',"api.anthropic.com","claude.ai","platform.claude.com","console.anthropic.com"'
    domains+=',"chatgpt.com","auth.openai.com","api.openai.com"'
    json="{\"network\":{\"allowedDomains\":[${domains}],\"deniedDomains\":[],\"allowUnixSockets\":[]"
    json+=",\"allowMachLookup\":[\"com.apple.trustd.agent\"],\"allowLocalBinding\":false}"
    json+=",\"filesystem\":{\"denyRead\":${deny_read_json},\"allowRead\":${allow_read_json}"
    json+=",\"allowWrite\":${write_json},\"denyWrite\":${deny_write_json}},\"allowPty\":true${linux_tools}}"
    if ! printf '%s\n' "${json}" > "${settings}.tmp" || ! mv -f "${settings}.tmp" "${settings}"; then
        refuse "cannot write ${settings}"
    fi
    # ~/.ssh is unreadable inside, so the seat pushes over HTTPS through the gh credential helper: an explicit
    # pushurl wins over a global `url.<ssh>.pushInsteadOf` rewrite. An origin that is neither HTTPS nor
    # git@github.com gets no override, and an SSH push from the seat fails.
    origin_url=$(git -C "${repo}" config --get remote.origin.url) || {
        (($? == 1)) || refuse "cannot read remote.origin.url in ${repo}"
        origin_url=''
    }
    case ${origin_url} in # lint-comparisons: allow a URL scheme prefix is the classification, no path compare
    https://*) push_url=${origin_url} ;;
    git@github.com:*) push_url=https://github.com/${origin_url#git@github.com:} ;;
    *) push_url='' ;;
    esac
    shim=${sandbox_real}/bin/omp
    {
        echo '#!/bin/bash'
        echo "# Generated by hcom-seat for the ${role} seat ${name} (regime-cutover U85); rewritten on every launch."
        echo '# A canary proves the sandbox holds before omp starts; there is no uncontained fallback.'
        echo 'set -u'
        printf -v srt_q '%q ' "${srt_cmd[@]}"
        printf -v omp_q '%q ' "${omp_cmd[@]}"
        echo "srt_cmd=(${srt_q}) omp_cmd=(${omp_q})"
        printf 'settings=%q canary=%q state=%q push_url=%q sandbox=%q\n' "${settings}" "${sandbox_real}/canary" \
            "${sandbox_state}" "${push_url}" "${sandbox_real}"
        # Outside the sandbox the shim and srt look up only in the private tool directory and the system directories;
        # inside it omp gets the seat's working PATH, applied by /usr/bin/env under srt.
        printf 'outer_path=%q seat_path=%q\n' "${sandbox_real}/bin:${PATH}" "${seat_path}"
        cat << 'SHIM'
export PATH=${outer_path}
/bin/rm -f "${canary}" || { echo "hcom-seat shim: cannot clear ${canary}" >&2; exit 2; }
# `true`, not `:`: a failed redirection on a special builtin ends a POSIX shell (dash, Ubuntu's /bin/sh).
probe=$("${srt_cmd[@]}" --settings "${settings}" -- /bin/sh -c 'if true 2> /dev/null > "$1"; then w=write-open; else w=write-denied; fi
if cat "$2" > /dev/null 2>&1; then r=read-open; else r=read-denied; fi
if ls "$3" > /dev/null 2>&1; then s=ssh-open; else s=ssh-denied; fi
echo "$w $r $s"' canary "${canary}" "${settings}" "${HOME}/.ssh") || {
    echo "hcom-seat shim: the sandbox canary did not run under ${srt_cmd[*]}; omp not started" >&2
    exit 2
}
if [[ ${probe} != 'write-denied read-denied ssh-denied' || -e ${canary} ]]; then
    echo "hcom-seat shim: the sandbox does not hold (canary: ${probe}); omp not started" >&2
    exit 2
fi
export UV_CACHE_DIR=${state}/uv-cache
# omp's Bedrock discovery stats ~/.aws/{credentials,config} unless these name the files, and an EPERM from the read
# deny ends omp at start (measured, omp 18.11.3 and 18.12.6); /dev/null reads as no AWS profile.
export AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/dev/null AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null
unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK
# Seat commits and tags are unsigned (standing order 29): the signing key under ~/.ssh is unreadable inside, so a
# host config with commit.gpgsign or tag.gpgsign true would fail every commit. GIT_CONFIG_* outranks every file.
export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false \
    GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=tag.gpgsign GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=false
if [[ -n ${push_url} ]]; then
    export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=remote.origin.pushurl GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=${push_url}
fi
# hcom-seat refuses to launch a seat where this is set.
export HCOM_SEAT_SANDBOX=${sandbox}
exec "${srt_cmd[@]}" --settings "${settings}" -- /usr/bin/env PATH="${seat_path}" "${omp_cmd[@]}" --no-extensions "$@"
SHIM
    } > "${shim}.tmp" || refuse "cannot write ${shim}.tmp"
    if ! chmod 700 "${shim}.tmp" || ! mv -f "${shim}.tmp" "${shim}"; then
        refuse "cannot install ${shim}"
    fi
    # hcom resolves `hcom` (for the runner script) and `herdr` (the terminal preset) from PATH; both find these
    # wrappers first, each of which runs exactly the physical argv pin_exec checked.
    seat_wrapper_write hcom "${hcom_cmd[@]}"
    seat_wrapper_write herdr "${herdr_cmd[@]}"
}

# @description Write `<sandbox>/bin/$1`, a wrapper that execs the given physical argv with its own arguments.
# @arg $1 string The command name.
# @arg $@ string The physical argv after the name.
seat_wrapper_write() {
    local tool=$1 argv_q
    shift
    printf -v argv_q '%q ' "$@"
    printf '#!/bin/bash\n# Generated by hcom-seat (regime-cutover U85): %s by its checked physical argv.\nexec %s"$@"\n' \
        "${tool}" "${argv_q}" > "${sandbox}/bin/${tool}.tmp" || refuse "cannot write ${sandbox}/bin/${tool}.tmp"
    if ! chmod 700 "${sandbox}/bin/${tool}.tmp" || ! mv -f "${sandbox}/bin/${tool}.tmp" "${sandbox}/bin/${tool}"; then
        refuse "cannot install ${sandbox}/bin/${tool}"
    fi
}

argv=(hcom omp --tag "${name}" --dir "${dir}" --terminal herdr --go -- --profile "${role}" --config "${policy}" --config "${profile}" --append-system-prompt "${rules}")
for ext in "${exts[@]}"; do
    argv+=(-e "${ext}")
done
argv+=(--hcom-team "${HCOM_TEAM}")
# @description Make sure the hcom store `HCOM_DIR` is a real directory before anything else is created (regime-cutover
#   U85): it is already clean (require_clean_path) and clear of every protected root by the identity of its deepest
#   existing ancestor (seat_overlap_check, a write root of every seat). An existing store must be a directory and no
#   symbolic link. A missing one is made 0700 one component at a time below its deepest existing ancestor, which must
#   be a real directory, not a symbolic link; each made component is checked again. A dry run creates nothing and
#   says what it would make.
# @arg $1 int 1 for a dry run.
hcom_store_ensure() {
    local top=${HCOM_DIR} rest=() path part
    if [[ -e ${HCOM_DIR} || -L ${HCOM_DIR} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${HCOM_DIR} && ! -L ${HCOM_DIR} ]] || refuse "the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR} is not a real directory"
        return 0
    fi
    while [[ ! -e ${top} && ! -L ${top} ]]; do
        # bash 3.2 reads an empty array as unset under `set -u`, so the expansion is guarded.
        rest=("${top##*/}" ${rest[@]+"${rest[@]}"})
        top=${top%/*}
        [[ -n ${top} ]] || top=/
    done
    [[ -d ${top} && ! -L ${top} ]] ||
        refuse "the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR} would be made under ${top}, which is not a real directory (a symbolic link or a file)"
    if (($1)); then
        echo "hcom-seat: the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR} does not exist; a launch creates it (0700)" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    path=${top%/}
    for part in "${rest[@]}"; do
        path=${path}/${part}
        (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${path}") || refuse "cannot create the hcom store ${path}"
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "${path} is not a real directory"
    done
}

hcom_store_ensure "${dry_run}"
if ((dry_run)); then
    printf '%q ' "${argv[@]}"
    echo
    echo "hcom-seat: environment HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR} HCOM_TEAM=${HCOM_TEAM:-}" >&2
    echo "hcom-seat: sandbox ${sandbox} (srt ${srt_cmd[*]}, omp ${omp_cmd[*]}, hcom ${hcom_cmd[*]}, herdr ${herdr_cmd[*]})" >&2
    exit 0
fi
# U37: a remote seat host needs this host's own login first (seat-login-preflight beside this file).
/bin/bash "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/seat-login-preflight" "${role}" || exit $?
if [[ ! -e ${dir} ]]; then
    # A repository without a remote (a fresh project) seats its worktrees at HEAD instead of origin/main. Only a
    # genuinely absent ref means that: a ref that is broken or names no commit, or a failed git, is a refusal.
    origin_main=$(git -C "${repo}" for-each-ref --format='%(objecttype)' refs/remotes/origin/main 2>&1) ||
        refuse "cannot inspect refs/remotes/origin/main in ${repo}: ${origin_main}"
    case ${origin_main} in
    commit) base=origin/main ;;
    '')
        base=HEAD
        echo "hcom-seat: origin/main is absent in ${repo}; the seat worktree starts at HEAD" >&2
        ;;
    *) refuse "refs/remotes/origin/main in ${repo} does not resolve to a commit: ${origin_main}" ;;
    esac
    git -C "${repo}" worktree add --detach "${dir}" "${base}"
else
    # A stale or foreign directory at the seat path would seat omp in the wrong tree. Each step's status is checked
    # on its own: the git state first (before git runs in the directory), then the directory's common directory.
    [[ -d ${dir} ]] || refuse "seat directory exists and is not a worktree of ${repo}: ${dir}"
    dir_phys=$(physical_path "${dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seat directory ${dir}"
    common_phys=$(physical_path "${common}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common}"
    git_state_check "${common_phys}" "${dir_phys}"
    seat_common=$(git -C "${dir}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2> /dev/null) ||
        refuse "seat directory exists and is not a worktree of ${repo}: ${dir}"
    [[ ${seat_common} -ef ${common} ]] || refuse "seat directory exists and is not a worktree of ${repo}: ${dir}"
fi
# U66 (F005): omp 18.11.3 merges the cwd's .omp/config.yml and .omp/settings.json at start whatever disabledProviders
# says (the list binds only after settings load; measured under a scratch HOME; 18.12.6 loads settings the same way), so a seat never starts in a directory
# that holds .omp. The profile overlay's disabledProviders (native and the other project-code providers) keeps the
# cwd's .omp tools, MCP servers, rules and skills out of the running seat (measured the same way).
[[ ! -e ${dir}/.omp && ! -L ${dir}/.omp ]] ||
    refuse "seat directory holds .omp, whose project settings omp would apply to the seat: ${dir}/.omp"
seat_sandbox_write
# hcom resolves `omp`, `hcom` and `herdr` from this PATH and pins the shim as the runner's tool path (U85); hcom
# itself runs by the physical argv checked above, with no second lookup.
export PATH="${sandbox}/bin:${PATH}"
exec "${hcom_cmd[@]}" "${argv[@]:1}"

The profile name equals the role and the two overlays are the ones hcom-seat passes every role: a named profile reads its own ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml, so the manifest's modelRoles.default for the role reaches the run only through the profile overlay (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, hcom-seat), unless --model overrides it. The role's policy overlay owns the approval mode (home/dot_agents/omp/policies/README.md), so --approval-mode is never passed. Extensions default to the bridge ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge and the SIWC ~/.agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc; --ext replaces that list. --no-extensions is passed for every role (regime-cutover U66, F005): the -e directories still load, and no ambient module does (the cwd's .omp/extensions, .omp/hooks, .omp/plugins, a settings extensions entry, the profile's plugin store; docs/extension-loading.md "Disable discovery", measured under a scratch HOME). Installed as the lever ~/.local/bin/common/omp-run.sh with its claude.levers.sha256 pin, it refuses to run when its own bytes differ (U31). omp is the first omp on PATH whose physical directory lies outside every .sandbox directory: a seat's PATH starts with the seat shim <seats-root>/.sandbox/<name>/bin/omp (U85), and the package beside the real executable holds the discovery registry the audit reads. Every input is checked before omp starts: an unknown role, an absent or empty prompt file, an absent overlay, extension directory or cwd is exit 2 with the path. omp's stderr is held and replayed after the run; a Failed to load extension <path>: <error> line in it (src/extensibility/extensions/load-errors.ts:5-13) is exit 2 as well, because a seat whose bridge or policy did not load must never be read as that seat (U1 report F5). Otherwise omp's exit status is returned. --mode text passes omp's own print-mode text through and --mode json its event stream, one JSON object per line, unchanged. HOME is the caller's: seats run as the operator. --role audit is the audit path (hcom-orchestration SKILL, step 4) and treats --cwd, a worktree at the audited head, as data only. Its rules are the whole AGENTS.md of refs/remotes/origin/main in that repository (the full ref, so a tag or a local branch named origin/main cannot stand in for it), read with git show and put before the prompt, never the head's copy (Claude Code Review reads its rules from the base branch, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review). omp reads project context (context files, rules, skills, settings, hooks, tools, MCP servers, ...) from its cwd and the cwd's ancestors through the discovery providers its capability registry holds (src/discovery/index.ts), and its disabledProviders setting switches a provider off for user and project scope alike (src/capability/index.ts filterProviders). So the audit lists every provider that registry holds, read with bun from the src/discovery/index.ts of the package omp resolves to (getAllProvidersInfo), adds the entries the two overlays already disable (an overlay's list replaces an earlier one), and passes that disabledProviders as the last --config. The model, the policy and the -e extensions do not come from discovery and stay. The task tool's agent list (src/task/discovery.ts, .omp/agents/*.md in the cwd's ancestors) is read by no provider, so the audit also passes --tools=read,grep,glob,bash, the read tools its policy lets run: a tool absent from that list is never built, and the task tool is the one that assembles the agent descriptions into its schema. omp runs in a fresh directory <scratch>/cwd, <scratch> made directly in TMPDIR (default /tmp, made absolute and exported so), with GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE naming the worktree; omp's plugin registry walk, which no provider gates, never reaches TMPDIR or above it (src/discovery/helpers.ts getProjectDiscoveryCeilings, the inherited TMPDIR being omp's os.tmpdir()). bun is called by its PATH name, not dereferenced, so a mise shim stays bun. The scratch directory is removed on exit.
