# @file worktree-gc.sh
# @brief List the clean agent worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ whose work landed; quarantine them with --apply, delete old quarantined ones with --purge.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U16, a coordinator lever pre-authorized by
#   `Bash(scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh *)` (scripts/orchestrator/README.md,
#   "Pre-authorized levers"). The candidates are the worktrees of this checkout
#   (`git worktree list --porcelain -z`) under `<toplevel>/.claude/worktrees/`,
#   except the quarantine `<toplevel>/.claude/worktrees/.gc-quarantine/`; every
#   other worktree, the main one and the omp seats included, is never listed.
#   A candidate qualifies when its tree is clean (`git status --porcelain
#   --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all` prints nothing: `git worktree
#   remove` deletes ignored files without asking, so a tree holding one, an
#   `.env` say, is kept; and no index entry carries the `assume-unchanged` or
#   `skip-worktree` flag, `git ls-files -v` tag lowercase or `S`, since an edit
#   to such a file is invisible to `git status` and to the removal's own check)
#   and its work landed, the first of: its head is
#   reachable from `origin/main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`); it landed by
#   content (every path `git diff --no-renames --name-only -z <merge-base>
#   <head>` names holds in `origin/main` the entry it holds in the head, mode
#   and object, or is absent from both: the case of a squash merge with no
#   later commit; no merge runs, so no configured merge driver or `merge=`
#   attribute can answer, and a git failure is an `error` row); or its head is
#   the `headRefOid` of a merged pull request of this repository (`gh pr list
#   --state merged --head <branch> --json number,headRefOid --limit 100`,
#   detached `--search <sha>`). A branch name
#   alone never counts: a commit pushed after a squash merge is not in main,
#   and `--head` also matches a fork's branch of the same name. A locked or
#   missing worktree is kept. The listing is read field by field on its NUL
#   separators, so a path cannot forge a record; a candidate whose path
#   contains a newline is an `error` row. Each candidate prints one row
#   `<verdict>\t<path>\t<ref>\t<reason>` (a newline in the path printed as
#   `\n`), verdict `gc` (qualifies), `keep` or `error`, then each quarantined
#   worktree a `quarantine` row with its age, then one `summary` row.
#
#   No check can be made atomic with a deletion, so taking a tree out of use
#   and deleting it are two runs. `--apply` deletes nothing: it renames each
#   qualifying tree with `git worktree move <path>
#   .gc-quarantine/<random>/<name>` (one rename on the same filesystem; git
#   refuses a locked tree), writes `<epoch> <classified head>` to
#   `gc-quarantined-at` in the tree's admin directory (`git rev-parse
#   --absolute-git-dir`, refused unless a plain directory directly under
#   `<common dir>/worktrees/`; the marker goes to a `mktemp` file there,
#   renamed onto its name, so a symlink planted at the name is replaced, never
#   written through), then checks the moved tree clean again (index flags
#   included) and its HEAD equal to the classified one. Both hold: a
#   `quarantined` row. Either fails (a file or commit made after the
#   classification moved with the tree), or the marker cannot be written: a
#   `held` row with the reason; the tree stays in the quarantine, is never
#   moved back and never deleted by this run. A refused move is a `failed`
#   row, exit 1. `--purge <days>` lists only the quarantine: each entry whose
#   marker is at least <days> days old (0: any age) is classified again by the
#   same rules (clean, ignored files included; HEAD read again and landed by
#   ancestry, content or a merged PR's exact head) and then removed with `git
#   worktree remove <path>`; an entry without a marker, younger, locked, or
#   no longer qualifying is kept, a refused removal is a `failed` row, exit 1.
#   Residual: purge, too, cannot check and remove atomically, so a file
#   written into the quarantined tree between its re-check and the removal is
#   lost; nothing has the quarantine path as its own, so that takes a process
#   still writing through its old working directory into the renamed tree
#   <days> days after the move. Nothing ever passes `--force`, and branch refs
#   stay. `git worktree prune` is never run: it would drop the admin data of
#   every worktree whose directory is missing, an unlocked omp seat included.
#   A `gh` error fails closed: the run moves and removes nothing and exits 1.
#   `origin/main` is read as it is; run `git fetch origin` first for a current
#   answer. Every `gh` call is bounded by WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl
#   `alarm`, because `timeout` is not on every host). A path argument narrows
#   the listing and `--apply` to those worktrees and is refused unless it is
#   one of the candidates; `--purge` takes none.
# @arg $@ path Optional worktree paths under .claude/worktrees/ (not in the quarantine); default: all of them.
# @option --apply Move the qualifying worktrees into the quarantine (default: list only).
# @option --purge <days> Remove the quarantined worktrees quarantined at least <days> days ago that still qualify.
# @env WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One TSV row per candidate and quarantined worktree, the move or removal rows, then `summary`.
# @exitcode 0 Listed (and quarantined or purged), including when nothing qualifies or a moved tree is held.
# @exitcode 1 A git or gh query failed, a path holds a newline, or a move or removal failed.
# @exitcode 2 Usage error, not in a git checkout, a path outside .claude/worktrees/ or in the quarantine, or a quarantine that is a symlink.
# @example
#   scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh
#   scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh --apply
#   scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh --purge 7
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

usage='usage: worktree-gc.sh [--apply] [<path>...] | --purge <days>'
apply=0 purge=''
paths=()
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --apply) apply=1 ;;
    --purge)
        if (($# < 2)) || [[ ! $2 =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,4})$ ]]; then
            echo "${usage}" >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        purge=$2
        shift
        ;;
    --) ;;
    -*)
        echo "${usage}" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
    *) paths+=("$1") ;;
    esac
    shift
done
if [[ -n ${purge} ]] && ((apply || ${#paths[@]})); then
    echo "${usage}" >&2
    exit 2
fi
gh_timeout=${WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || {
    echo 'worktree-gc: WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer' >&2
    exit 2
}

toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || {
    echo 'worktree-gc: not in a git checkout' >&2
    exit 2
}
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P)
base=${toplevel}/.claude/worktrees
quarantine=${base}/.gc-quarantine
if ! common_dir=$(git -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) ||
    ! common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P); then
    echo 'worktree-gc: cannot resolve the git common directory' >&2
    exit 1
fi
git -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --verify --quiet 'origin/main^{commit}' > /dev/null || {
    echo 'worktree-gc: origin/main is absent; run git fetch origin' >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Print the physical form of a path, or the path itself when it no longer exists.
# @arg $1 path A path.
physical() {
    if [[ -d $1 ]]; then (cd "$1" && pwd -P); else printf '%s\n' "$1"; fi
}

# @description Succeed when a physical path lies strictly under .claude/worktrees/ of this checkout.
# @arg $1 path A physical path.
under_base() {
    [[ $1 == "${base}/"?* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
}

# @description Succeed when a physical path is the quarantine or lies under it.
# @arg $1 path A physical path.
in_quarantine() {
    [[ $1 == "${quarantine}" || $1 == "${quarantine}/"* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
}

# @description Print the admin directory of a worktree, refusing one outside `<common dir>/worktrees/`.
# @arg $1 path The worktree.
# @exitcode 1 git failed or the admin directory is elsewhere.
admin_dir() {
    local raw dir
    raw=$(git -C "$1" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) && [[ ! -L ${raw} ]] && dir=$(cd "${raw}" && pwd -P) || return 1
    [[ ${dir} == "${common_dir}/worktrees/"?* && ${dir} != "${common_dir}/worktrees/"*/* ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    printf '%s\n' "${dir}"
}

# @description Write the quarantine marker into an admin directory without following a link at its name: the content
#   goes to a fresh `mktemp` file beside it, which is renamed onto the name (a rename replaces a symlink there). A
#   directory at the name, or one a symlink there points at, is refused, since `mv` would move the file into it.
# @arg $1 path The admin directory, from admin_dir.
# @arg $2 string The marker line.
# @exitcode 1 The marker was not written.
write_marker() {
    local tmp
    [[ ! -d $1/${marker} ]] || return 1
    tmp=$(mktemp "$1/${marker}.XXXXXX") || return 1
    if printf '%s\n' "$2" > "${tmp}" && mv -f "${tmp}" "$1/${marker}"; then return 0; fi
    rm -f "${tmp}"
    return 1
}

# @description Run gh in the checkout, killed after WORKTREE_GC_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string gh arguments.
bounded_gh() {
    (cd "${toplevel}" && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@")
}

selected=()
for path in "${paths[@]+"${paths[@]}"}"; do
    resolved=$(physical "${path}")
    under_base "${resolved}" || {
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is outside ${base}/" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    ! in_quarantine "${resolved}" || {
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is in the quarantine ${quarantine}/; --purge handles it" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    selected+=("${resolved}")
done

# Candidates and quarantined worktrees as parallel arrays: path, head, branch (empty when detached), state (`locked`,
# `missing`, `newline` or empty).
cand_path=() cand_head=() cand_branch=() cand_state=()
q_path=() q_head=() q_branch=() q_state=()
record() {
    [[ -n ${wt_path} ]] || return 0
    local resolved state=${wt_state}
    resolved=$(physical "${wt_path}")
    under_base "${resolved}" || return 0
    if [[ ${wt_path} == *$'\n'* ]]; then state=newline; fi # lint-comparisons: allow a newline-content test, not a path comparison
    if in_quarantine "${resolved}"; then
        ((${#selected[@]})) && return 0
        q_path+=("${resolved}") q_head+=("${wt_head}") q_branch+=("${wt_branch}") q_state+=("${state}")
        return 0
    fi
    if ((${#selected[@]})); then
        local wanted='' item
        for item in "${selected[@]}"; do [[ ${item} == "${resolved}" ]] && wanted=1; done # lint-comparisons: allow both operands are pwd -P forms from physical()
        [[ -n ${wanted} ]] || return 0
    fi
    cand_path+=("${resolved}") cand_head+=("${wt_head}") cand_branch+=("${wt_branch}") cand_state+=("${state}")
}
# The producer writes to a file, not a pipe or a process substitution, so its exit status is checked; the NUL-separated
# fields are read as they are (`read -d ''`), never turned into lines, so a newline inside a path stays in its field.
listing=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/worktree-gc.XXXXXX")
changed=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/worktree-gc.XXXXXX")
entries=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/worktree-gc.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "${listing}" "${changed}" "${entries}"' EXIT
git -C "${toplevel}" worktree list --porcelain -z > "${listing}" || {
    echo 'worktree-gc: git worktree list failed' >&2
    exit 1
}
wt_path='' wt_head='' wt_branch='' wt_state=''
while IFS= read -r -d '' field; do
    case ${field} in
    'worktree '*)
        record
        wt_path=${field#worktree } wt_head='' wt_branch='' wt_state=''
        ;;
    'HEAD '*) wt_head=${field#HEAD } ;;
    'branch refs/heads/'*) wt_branch=${field#branch refs/heads/} ;;
    locked | 'locked '*) wt_state=locked ;;
    prunable | 'prunable '*) [[ -n ${wt_state} ]] || wt_state=missing ;;
    esac
done < "${listing}"
record

for path in "${selected[@]+"${selected[@]}"}"; do
    found=''
    for item in "${cand_path[@]+"${cand_path[@]}"}"; do [[ ${item} == "${path}" ]] && found=1; done # lint-comparisons: allow both operands are pwd -P forms from physical()
    [[ -n ${found} ]] || {
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is not a worktree of ${toplevel}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
done

# @description Succeed when the head landed in origin/main by content: every path `git diff` names between the merge
#   base and the head holds in origin/main the `git ls-tree -r` entry (mode, type, object) it holds in the head, or is
#   absent from both. Nothing here merges, so no merge driver, `merge=` attribute or `merge.*` setting takes part; the
#   diff is name-only and NUL-separated, renames off and submodules shown, and every pathspec literal.
# @arg $1 string The head sha.
# @exitcode 0 Landed by content (an empty change set included).
# @exitcode 1 Not landed, or the head shares no history with origin/main.
# @exitcode 2 A git call failed.
landed_by_content() {
    local head=$1 mb rc field in_head in_main
    local -a changed_paths=()
    mb=$(git -C "${toplevel}" merge-base origin/main "${head}") && rc=0 || rc=$?
    ((rc != 1)) || return 1
    if ((rc)) || [[ ! ${mb} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$ ]]; then return 2; fi
    git -C "${toplevel}" diff --no-renames --no-relative --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color \
        --ignore-submodules=none --name-only -z "${mb}" "${head}" -- > "${changed}" || return 2
    while IFS= read -r -d '' field; do changed_paths+=("${field}"); done < "${changed}"
    ((${#changed_paths[@]})) || return 0
    # Without -z the quoted listing has one line per entry, so it survives a command substitution; both sides are quoted alike.
    in_head=$(git -C "${toplevel}" -c core.quotePath=true --literal-pathspecs ls-tree -r --full-tree "${head}" \
        -- "${changed_paths[@]}") || return 2
    in_main=$(git -C "${toplevel}" -c core.quotePath=true --literal-pathspecs ls-tree -r --full-tree origin/main \
        -- "${changed_paths[@]}") || return 2
    [[ ${in_head} == "${in_main}" ]] || return 1
}

# @description Set `status` to the `git status --porcelain --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all` of a worktree,
#   and `flagged` to the number of its index entries marked `assume-unchanged` (`git ls-files -v` tag lowercase) or
#   `skip-worktree` (tag `S`), whose edits neither `git status` nor `git worktree remove` sees.
# @arg $1 path The worktree.
# @exitcode 1 git status or git ls-files failed.
tree_status() {
    local entry
    flagged=0
    status=$(git -C "$1" status --porcelain --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all) || return 1
    git -C "$1" ls-files -v -z > "${entries}" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
        if [[ ${entry} == [[:lower:]S]' '* ]]; then flagged=$((flagged + 1)); fi
    done < "${entries}"
}

# @description Set `verdict` and `reason` for one candidate.
# @arg $1 path The worktree.
# @arg $2 string Its head sha.
# @arg $3 string Its branch, empty when detached.
# @arg $4 string Its state: `locked`, `missing`, `newline` or empty.
classify() {
    local path=$1 head=$2 branch=$3 state=$4 rc query prs number
    verdict=keep
    if [[ ${state} == newline ]]; then
        verdict=error reason='path contains a newline'
        return
    fi
    if [[ ${state} == locked ]]; then
        reason='locked'
        return
    fi
    if [[ ${state} == missing || ! -d ${path} ]]; then
        reason='missing (its admin data is left for the operator)'
        return
    fi
    if ! tree_status "${path}"; then
        verdict=error reason='git status failed'
        return
    fi
    if [[ -n ${status} ]] && grep -qv '^!! ' <<< "${status}"; then
        reason='dirty or untracked files'
        return
    fi
    if ((flagged)); then
        reason="${flagged} index entries marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree (git status cannot see their edits)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ -n ${status} ]]; then
        reason='ignored files (git worktree remove would delete them)'
        return
    fi
    if [[ ! ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$ ]]; then
        verdict=error reason="unreadable head '${head}'"
        return
    fi
    if git -C "${toplevel}" merge-base --is-ancestor "${head}" origin/main 2> /dev/null; then
        verdict=gc reason="head ${head:0:12} is in origin/main"
        return
    fi
    landed_by_content "${head}" && rc=0 || rc=$?
    if ((rc > 1)); then
        verdict=error reason="comparing head ${head:0:12} with origin/main failed"
        return
    fi
    if ((rc == 0)); then
        verdict=gc reason="every path head ${head:0:12} changed holds the same entry in origin/main"
        return
    fi
    if [[ -n ${branch} ]]; then
        query=(--head "${branch}" --json 'number,headRefOid' --limit 100)
    else
        query=(--search "${head}" --json 'number,headRefOid')
    fi
    if ! prs=$(bounded_gh pr list --state merged "${query[@]}") ||
        ! number=$(jq -r --arg sha "${head}" 'map(select(.headRefOid == $sha))[0].number // empty' <<< "${prs}"); then
        verdict=error reason="gh pr list ${query[0]} ${query[1]:0:12} failed"
        return
    fi
    if [[ -n ${number} ]]; then
        verdict=gc reason="head ${head:0:12} is the head of merged PR #${number}"
    else
        reason="head ${head:0:12} is neither in origin/main nor the head of a merged PR"
    fi
}

marker='gc-quarantined-at'
now=$(date +%s)

# @description Set `quarantined_at` to the epoch the quarantine marker of a worktree records, empty without a readable one.
# @arg $1 path The quarantined worktree.
read_marker() {
    local dir line=''
    quarantined_at=''
    dir=$(admin_dir "$1") || return 0
    [[ -f ${dir}/${marker} && ! -L ${dir}/${marker} ]] || return 0
    IFS= read -r line < "${dir}/${marker}" || [[ -n ${line} ]] || return 0
    if [[ ${line} =~ ^([0-9]{1,12})\ [0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$ ]]; then quarantined_at=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}; fi
}

# @description Print an age in seconds as `<d>d <h>h`.
# @arg $1 number Seconds.
age() {
    printf '%dd %dh' $(($1 / 86400)) $(($1 % 86400 / 3600))
}

if [[ -n ${purge} ]]; then
    doomed=() errors=0 kept=0
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#q_path[@]}; i++)); do
        path=${q_path[i]} state=${q_state[i]} verdict=keep
        if [[ ${state} == newline ]]; then
            verdict=error reason='path contains a newline'
        elif [[ ${state} == locked ]]; then
            reason='locked'
        elif [[ ${state} == missing || ! -d ${path} ]]; then
            reason='missing (its admin data is left for the operator)'
        else
            read_marker "${path}"
            if [[ -z ${quarantined_at} ]]; then
                reason="no ${marker} marker in its admin directory"
            elif ((now - quarantined_at < purge * 86400)); then
                reason="quarantined $(age $((now - quarantined_at))) ago, younger than ${purge} days"
            elif ! head=$(git -C "${path}" rev-parse --verify --quiet 'HEAD^{commit}'); then
                verdict=error reason='cannot read HEAD'
            elif [[ ${head} != "${q_head[i]}" ]]; then
                reason="head moved to ${head:0:12} during the run"
            else
                # The same rules as a candidate's: clean (ignored files included) and landed by ancestry, content or a
                # merged PR's exact head.
                classify "${path}" "${head}" "${q_branch[i]}" "${state}"
            fi
        fi
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${verdict}" "${path//$'\n'/\\n}" "${q_branch[i]:-(detached ${q_head[i]:0:12})}" "${reason}"
        case ${verdict} in
        gc) doomed+=("${path}") ;;
        error) errors=$((errors + 1)) ;;
        *) kept=$((kept + 1)) ;;
        esac
    done
    if ((errors)); then
        printf 'summary\t%d qualify, %d kept, %d errors; nothing removed\n' "${#doomed[@]}" "${kept}" "${errors}"
        exit 1
    fi
    removed=0 failed=0
    for path in "${doomed[@]+"${doomed[@]}"}"; do
        in_quarantine "${path}" || {
            echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is outside ${quarantine}/" >&2
            exit 2
        }
        # Residual: no check is atomic with the removal; the tree has sat renamed for at least the purge age.
        if git -C "${toplevel}" worktree remove "${path}"; then
            printf 'removed\t%s\n' "${path}"
            removed=$((removed + 1))
            slot=${path%/*}
            if [[ ${slot} != "${quarantine}" ]] && in_quarantine "${slot}"; then rmdir "${slot}" 2> /dev/null || true; fi # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        else
            printf 'failed\t%s\tgit worktree remove refused\n' "${path}"
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
    printf 'summary\t%d removed, %d failed, %d kept\n' "${removed}" "${failed}" "${kept}"
    ((! failed)) || exit 1
    exit 0
fi

gc=() errors=0 kept=0
for ((i = 0; i < ${#cand_path[@]}; i++)); do
    classify "${cand_path[i]}" "${cand_head[i]}" "${cand_branch[i]}" "${cand_state[i]}"
    shown=${cand_path[i]//$'\n'/\\n}
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${verdict}" "${shown}" "${cand_branch[i]:-(detached ${cand_head[i]:0:12})}" "${reason}"
    case ${verdict} in
    gc) gc+=("${i}") ;;
    error) errors=$((errors + 1)) ;;
    *) kept=$((kept + 1)) ;;
    esac
done
for ((i = 0; i < ${#q_path[@]}; i++)); do
    read_marker "${q_path[i]}"
    if [[ -n ${quarantined_at} ]]; then
        reason="quarantined $(age $((now - quarantined_at))) ago"
    else
        reason="no ${marker} marker in its admin directory (--purge keeps it)"
    fi
    printf 'quarantine\t%s\t%s\t%s%s\n' "${q_path[i]//$'\n'/\\n}" "${q_branch[i]:-(detached ${q_head[i]:0:12})}" "${reason}" "${q_state[i]:+, ${q_state[i]}}"
done

if ((errors)); then
    printf 'summary\t%d qualify, %d kept, %d errors; nothing moved\n' "${#gc[@]}" "${kept}" "${errors}"
    exit 1
fi
if ((! apply)); then
    printf 'summary\t%d qualify, %d kept, %d in quarantine; dry run, rerun with --apply to quarantine\n' "${#gc[@]}" "${kept}" "${#q_path[@]}"
    exit 0
fi

if ((${#gc[@]})); then
    resolved=''
    if mkdir -p "${quarantine}" && [[ ! -L ${quarantine} ]]; then resolved=$(physical "${quarantine}"); fi
    [[ ${resolved} == "${quarantine}" ]] || { # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: the quarantine ${quarantine} is not a plain directory" >&2
        exit 2
    }
fi
quarantined=0 held=0 failed=0
for i in "${gc[@]+"${gc[@]}"}"; do
    path=${cand_path[i]} head=${cand_head[i]}
    if ! under_base "${path}" || in_quarantine "${path}"; then
        echo "worktree-gc: refused: ${path} is outside ${base}/ or in the quarantine" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    # A fresh directory per tree, so the destination never exists (git moves into an existing directory) and two trees
    # of the same name never meet.
    if ! slot=$(mktemp -d "${quarantine}/XXXXXXXX"); then
        printf 'failed\t%s\tcannot create a directory in the quarantine\n' "${path}"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
    fi
    dest=${slot}/${path##*/}
    # One rename: a process inside the tree keeps its working directory, now in the quarantine; nothing is deleted.
    if ! git -C "${toplevel}" worktree move "${path}" "${dest}"; then
        rmdir "${slot}" 2> /dev/null || true
        printf 'failed\t%s\tgit worktree move refused\n' "${path}"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
    fi
    # The classification may be minutes old (gh calls); whatever changed since moved with the tree and holds it.
    reason=''
    if ! dir=$(admin_dir "${dest}") || ! write_marker "${dir}" "${now} ${head}"; then
        reason="cannot write ${marker} in its admin directory"
    elif ! tree_status "${dest}"; then
        reason='git status failed after the move'
    elif [[ -n ${status} ]]; then
        reason='changed since the check: dirty, untracked or ignored files'
    elif ((flagged)); then
        reason="${flagged} index entries marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree since the check"
    elif ! moved_head=$(git -C "${dest}" rev-parse --verify --quiet 'HEAD^{commit}'); then
        reason='cannot read HEAD after the move'
    elif [[ ${moved_head} != "${head}" ]]; then
        reason="head moved from ${head:0:12} to ${moved_head:0:12} since the check"
    fi
    if [[ -n ${reason} ]]; then
        printf 'held\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${path}" "${dest}" "${reason}"
        held=$((held + 1))
    else
        printf 'quarantined\t%s\t%s\n' "${path}" "${dest}"
        quarantined=$((quarantined + 1))
    fi
done
printf 'summary\t%d quarantined, %d held, %d failed, %d kept\n' "${quarantined}" "${held}" "${failed}" "${kept}"
((! failed)) || exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env zsh

# @file home/dot_local/bin/server/cuda.sh
# @brief Export CUDA paths for server shells.
# @description
#   Sets `CUDA_HOME`, prepends the CUDA binaries to the shell path, and extends
#   `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for CUDA libraries.
# @example
#   source ~/.local/bin/server/cuda.sh

export CUDA_HOME="/usr/local/cuda"

typeset -gU path
path=(
    $path
    ${CUDA_HOME}/bin(N-/)
)

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:$CUDA_HOME/lib64"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/server/ssh_agent.sh
# @brief Start `ssh-agent` and load the default SSH key when present.
# @description
#   Starts a new `ssh-agent` process and adds the default ed25519 private key
#   for the current user when the key exists. This file is sourced by sheldon,
#   so it must not enable strict shell options in the parent interactive shell.
#   Private keys are intentionally not stored in the public chezmoi source state.
# @example
#   source ~/.local/bin/server/ssh_agent.sh

# @description Start ssh-agent and add the default ed25519 key when available.
function _dotfiles_start_ssh_agent() {
    local default_ssh_key="${HOME}/.ssh/id_ed25519"

    eval "$(ssh-agent)" > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

    if [[ -r "${default_ssh_key}" ]]; then
        ssh-add "${default_ssh_key}" > /dev/null 2>&1 ||
            printf 'Failed to add default SSH key: %s\n' "${default_ssh_key}" >&2
    else
        printf 'Default SSH key not found: %s\n' "${default_ssh_key}" >&2
        printf 'Skipping ssh-add; restore the key from private state or create one with ssh-keygen.\n' >&2
    fi
}

_dotfiles_start_ssh_agent
unset -f _dotfiles_start_ssh_agent

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/common/aws_cli.sh
# @brief Install the current AWS CLI from AWS's official distribution, verified with AWS's GPG signature.
# @description
#   On Linux the archive is verified and installed. On macOS AWS's install.sh is verified, then run under the
#   XDG roots; it downloads the pkg and checks its Apple Developer team id before Apple's installer runs.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

# Rendered from assets.aws-cli in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml; change it there.
readonly AWS_CLI_FINGERPRINT="FB5DB77FD5C118B80511ADA8A6310ACC4672475C"
readonly AWS_CLI_KEY_PATH="${AWS_CLI_KEY_PATH:-${HOME}/.local/share/aws-cli-keys/aws-cli-public-key.asc}"
readonly AWS_CLI_INSTALL_DIR="${HOME}/.local/share/aws-cli"
readonly AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR="${HOME}/.local/bin"
# The ETag of the archive the last verified install came from; a changed ETag means a new release.
readonly AWS_CLI_ETAG_FILE="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/state}/dotfiles/aws-cli-archive.etag"

#
# @description Print the URL of AWS's current release: the archive for the current supported architecture
#   on Linux, whose .sig is checked against the pinned key, and on macOS v2/version.txt, the release marker
#   that v2/install.sh installs, whose ETag main reads.
# @stdout The official x86_64 or aarch64 archive URL, or the macOS v2/version.txt URL.
#
function aws_cli_url() {
    local architecture kernel

    kernel="$(uname -s)" || {
        printf 'uname -s failed; no AWS CLI archive was chosen.\n' >&2
        return 1
    }
    # macOS installs through v2/install.sh, which installs the release v2/version.txt names.
    if [ "${kernel}" = Darwin ]; then
        printf 'https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/version.txt\n'
        return
    fi
    architecture="$(uname -m)"
    case "${architecture}" in
    x86_64 | aarch64)
        printf 'https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-%s.zip\n' "${architecture}"
        ;;
    *)
        printf 'Unsupported AWS CLI architecture: %s\n' "${architecture}" >&2
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
}

#
# @description Verify that an executable runs as the AWS CLI and print the version it reports.
# @arg $1 executable AWS CLI executable path.
# @arg $2 error_prefix Error message prefix.
# @stdout The version token, for example aws-cli/2.37.6.
#
function verify_aws_cli_version() {
    local executable="$1"
    local error_prefix="$2"
    local version_output
    local version_token

    if [[ ! -x "${executable}" ]]; then
        printf '%s: %s is not executable.\n' "${error_prefix}" "${executable}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    version_output="$("${executable}" --version)" || return
    read -r version_token _ <<< "${version_output}"
    if [[ "${version_token}" != aws-cli/* ]]; then
        printf '%s: expected an aws-cli/<version> banner, got %s.\n' "${error_prefix}" "${version_token}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${version_token}"
}

#
# @description Verify that the installer left the staged release as the working AWS CLI and report it.
# @arg $1 string The staged version, for example 2.37.6.
#
function verify_aws_cli_install() {
    local version
    version="$(verify_aws_cli_version "${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}/aws" "AWS CLI postcondition failed")" || return
    # An installer that skipped (an existing version directory) can leave an older CLI active.
    if [ "${version}" != "aws-cli/$1" ]; then
        printf 'AWS CLI postcondition failed: %s is active, not the staged aws-cli/%s.\n' "${version}" "$1" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf 'Installed %s.\n' "${version}"
}

#
# @description Verify and install the current AWS CLI without modifying a working install on verification failure.
#   On macOS the verified file is install.sh, and version.txt names the release the postcondition expects.
# @exitcode 3 A download failed, so nothing was installed.
#
function install_aws_cli() (
    local archive_url
    local archive_path
    local signature_path
    local current_time
    local expiration
    local key_data
    local keyring_path
    local fingerprint
    local inspection_home
    local validity
    local temporary_dir
    local staged_version
    local same_version_dir
    local active_version
    local kernel
    local macos=""

    kernel="$(uname -s)" || {
        printf 'uname -s failed; the AWS CLI was not installed.\n' >&2
        return 1
    }
    if [ "${kernel}" = Darwin ]; then
        macos=1
        archive_url="https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/install.sh"
    else
        archive_url="$(aws_cli_url)" || return
    fi
    temporary_dir="$(mktemp -d)" || return
    trap 'rm -rf "${temporary_dir}"' EXIT

    archive_path="${temporary_dir}/awscliv2.zip"
    [ -z "${macos}" ] || archive_path="${temporary_dir}/install.sh"
    signature_path="${archive_path}.sig"
    inspection_home="${temporary_dir}/gnupg-inspection"
    keyring_path="${temporary_dir}/aws-cli-keyring.gpg"

    # curl gets 30 s to connect and fails a transfer under 1 KB/s for 60 s, so a stalled download ends.
    curl --fail --location --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 \
        "${archive_url}" --output "${archive_path}" || return 3
    curl --fail --location --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 \
        "${archive_url}.sig" --output "${signature_path}" || return 3
    if [ -n "${macos}" ]; then
        # install.sh installs the release version.txt names, so the postcondition expects that one.
        staged_version="$(curl --fail --location --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 \
            https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/version.txt)" || return 3
        staged_version="${staged_version//[[:space:]]/}"
    fi

    mkdir -m 700 "${inspection_home}" || return
    key_data="$(gpg --homedir "${inspection_home}" --batch --with-colons --import-options show-only --import "${AWS_CLI_KEY_PATH}")" || return
    fingerprint="$(awk -F: '$1 == "fpr" { print $10 }' <<< "${key_data}")"
    validity="$(awk -F: '$1 == "pub" { print $2 }' <<< "${key_data}")"
    expiration="$(awk -F: '$1 == "pub" { print $7 }' <<< "${key_data}")"
    current_time="$(date +%s)"
    if [[ "${fingerprint}" != "${AWS_CLI_FINGERPRINT}" || "${validity}" != "-" || ! "${expiration}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] ||
        ((expiration <= current_time)); then
        printf 'AWS CLI signing key validation failed.\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    gpg --batch --yes --dearmor --output "${keyring_path}" "${AWS_CLI_KEY_PATH}" || return
    gpgv --keyring "${keyring_path}" "${signature_path}" "${archive_path}" || return

    if [ -n "${macos}" ]; then
        mkdir -p "${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}" "$(dirname "${AWS_CLI_INSTALL_DIR}")" || return
        XDG_DATA_HOME="$(dirname "${AWS_CLI_INSTALL_DIR}")" XDG_BIN_HOME="${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}" bash "${archive_path}" || return
        verify_aws_cli_install "${staged_version}"
        return
    fi
    unzip -q "${archive_path}" -d "${temporary_dir}" || return
    staged_version="$(verify_aws_cli_version "${temporary_dir}/aws/dist/aws" "AWS CLI staged artifact verification failed")" || return
    staged_version="${staged_version#aws-cli/}"
    # The upstream installer's --update skips a version directory that already exists, so a broken
    # install of the same version, or an interrupted update that left it beside an older active CLI,
    # would never be repaired. Remove that directory first, after the signature and the staged CLI
    # passed and only when the active CLI does not run as the staged release.
    same_version_dir="${AWS_CLI_INSTALL_DIR}/v2/${staged_version}"
    if [[ "${staged_version}" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$ && -d "${same_version_dir}" ]]; then
        # An active CLI that does not run is not the staged release either, so its failure is the answer.
        active_version="$(verify_aws_cli_version "${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}/aws" "AWS CLI check" 2> /dev/null)" || active_version=""
        if [ "${active_version}" != "aws-cli/${staged_version}" ]; then
            rm -rf "${same_version_dir}" || return
        fi
    fi
    mkdir -p "${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}" "$(dirname "${AWS_CLI_INSTALL_DIR}")" || return
    "${temporary_dir}/aws/install" \
        --install-dir "${AWS_CLI_INSTALL_DIR}" \
        --bin-dir "${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}" \
        --update || return
    verify_aws_cli_install "${staged_version}"
)

#
# @description Print the ETag AWS serves for the current archive.
#
function aws_cli_archive_etag() {
    local url
    url="$(aws_cli_url)" || return
    curl --fail --location --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 \
        --head "${url}" |
        awk 'tolower($1) == "etag:" { etag = $2 } END { sub(/\r$/, "", etag); if (etag == "") exit 1; print etag }'
}

#
# @description Install or update the AWS CLI. Runs on every chezmoi apply and skips when the
#   archive's ETag still matches the one recorded after the last verified install and that
#   AWS CLI still runs.
#
function main() {
    local etag recorded status=0
    if ! etag="$(aws_cli_archive_etag)"; then
        # Only a CLI that still runs stays; a broken one fails the offline apply instead of passing.
        verify_aws_cli_version "${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}/aws" "AWS CLI check" > /dev/null 2>&1 || {
            printf 'Could not reach the AWS CLI archive, and no working AWS CLI is installed.\n' >&2
            return 1
        }
        printf 'warning: could not reach the AWS CLI archive; the installed AWS CLI stays.\n' >&2
        return 0
    fi
    # The recorded ETag counts only for an AWS CLI that still runs; a broken one is reinstalled. No
    # readable record is no match: the verified install runs again and records it.
    recorded="$(cat "${AWS_CLI_ETAG_FILE}" 2> /dev/null)" || recorded=""
    if [ "${recorded}" = "${etag}" ] &&
        verify_aws_cli_version "${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}/aws" "AWS CLI check" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0
    fi
    install_aws_cli || status=$?
    # A failed download keeps a working AWS CLI (its ETag stays unrecorded, so the next apply retries);
    # a failed signature or postcondition never does.
    if [ "${status}" -eq 3 ] && verify_aws_cli_version "${AWS_CLI_BIN_DIR}/aws" "AWS CLI check" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf 'warning: could not download the AWS CLI archive; the installed AWS CLI stays.\n' >&2
        return 0
    fi
    [ "${status}" -eq 0 ] || return "${status}"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "${AWS_CLI_ETAG_FILE}")" && printf '%s\n' "${etag}" > "${AWS_CLI_ETAG_FILE}" ||
        printf 'warning: could not record the AWS CLI archive ETag; the next apply reinstalls it.\n' >&2
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/common/chezmoi_private.sh
# @brief Initialize the private chezmoi repository.
# @description
#   Bootstraps `mryfmo/dotfiles-private` using the dedicated source and
#   config paths under the current user's home directory.

set -Eeuo pipefail

declare -r PRIVATE_DOTFILES_REPO_URL="https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles-private"
declare -r PRIVATE_DOTFILES_PATH="${HOME}/.local/share/chezmoi-private"
declare -r PRIVATE_DOTFILES_CONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.config/chezmoi-private/chezmoi.yaml"

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

#
# @description Initialize the private dotfiles repository if it is available.
#
function install_chezmoi_private() {
    if chezmoi init \
        --apply \
        --source "${PRIVATE_DOTFILES_PATH}" \
        --config "${PRIVATE_DOTFILES_CONFIG_PATH}" \
        "${PRIVATE_DOTFILES_REPO_URL}"; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "Warning: Failed to initialize dotfiles-private. Skipping private dotfiles setup." >&2
}

#
# @description Run the private chezmoi initialization flow.
#
function main() {
    install_chezmoi_private
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

docs.title: install/common/credential_dirs.sh
docs.text: Ubuntu's default umask 002 creates directories group-writable, so gh, age, the AWS CLI and chezmoi init leave their credential directories at 0775 or 0771. This script sets each existing directory to 0700. A missing directory is skipped. A directory that is a symlink, or that is reached through a symlinked component below $HOME (or below / for a directory outside $HOME), is warned about and left unchanged; trailing slashes are stripped first, so dir/ cannot hide a symlink. On macOS and the BSDs chmod runs with -h (never follows a link). A chmod that fails stops the apply with a message naming the directory. shortcut: GNU chmod has no no-follow flag, so a symlink swapped in between the check and the chmod is followed; that needs write access to $HOME.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/common/credential_dirs.sh
# @brief Keep the credential directories private (mode 0700) on every apply.
# @description
#   Ubuntu's default umask 002 creates directories group-writable, so gh, age,
#   the AWS CLI and `chezmoi init` leave their credential directories at 0775 or
#   0771. This script sets each existing directory to 0700. A missing directory
#   is skipped. A directory that is a symlink, or that is reached through a
#   symlinked component below `$HOME` (or below `/` for a directory outside
#   `$HOME`), is warned about and left unchanged; trailing slashes are stripped
#   first, so `dir/` cannot hide a symlink. On macOS and the BSDs chmod runs with
#   `-h` (never follows a link). A chmod that fails stops the apply with a
#   message naming the directory.
#   shortcut: GNU chmod has no no-follow flag, so a symlink swapped in between
#   the check and the chmod is followed; that needs write access to `$HOME`.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

#
# @description Strip trailing slashes from a path (a bare `/` stays `/`).
# @arg $1 string Path.
# @stdout The path without trailing slashes.
#
function strip_trailing_slashes() {
    local path="$1"
    while [[ ${#path} -gt 1 && ${path: -1} == / ]]; do # lint-comparisons: allow the last character, not a path identity
        path="${path%/}"
    done
    printf '%s\n' "${path}"
}

#
# @description Return success when no component of a path is a symlink, checked below `$HOME`
#   for a path inside it and below `/` otherwise; `.` and `..` components count as unsafe.
# @arg $1 string Absolute path without trailing slashes.
# @arg $2 string `$HOME` without trailing slashes.
# @exitcode 1 A component is a symlink, `.` or `..`, or the path is relative.
#
function path_has_no_symlink() {
    local path="$1" home="$2" current rest component
    [[ ${path:0:1} == / ]] || return 1                  # lint-comparisons: allow the first character, not a path identity
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${path} == "${home}"/* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a lexical prefix split, never an identity check
        current="${home}"
        rest="${path#"${home}"/}"
    else
        current=""
        rest="${path#/}"
    fi
    while [ -n "${rest}" ]; do
        component="${rest%%/*}"
        if [[ ${rest} == */* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a separator test, not a path identity
            rest="${rest#*/}"
        else
            rest=""
        fi
        [ -n "${component}" ] || continue
        case "${component}" in
        . | ..) return 1 ;;
        esac
        current="${current}/${component}"
        [ ! -L "${current}" ] || return 1
    done
}

#
# @description Set one directory to mode 0700, never following a link when the chmod supports it.
# @arg $1 string Directory.
# @arg $2 string Non-empty when chmod takes `-h` (macOS, BSD).
#
function chmod_private() {
    if [ -n "$2" ]; then
        chmod -h 700 "$1"
    else
        chmod 700 "$1"
    fi
}

#
# @description Set every existing credential directory to mode 0700.
# @exitcode 0 Every existing directory now has mode 0700.
# @exitcode 1 chmod failed on a directory, or uname failed.
#
function secure_credential_dirs() {
    local config_home="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-${HOME}/.config}" dir home kernel no_follow="" status=0
    # An array, not a here-string: bash 3.2 writes a here-string to a temporary file, and a failed
    # write there would skip every chmod while the loop still returned success.
    local -a dirs=(
        "${GH_CONFIG_DIR:-${config_home}/gh}"
        "${config_home}/age"
        "${HOME}/.aws"
        "${HOME}/.local/share/chezmoi-private"
    )
    home="$(strip_trailing_slashes "${HOME}")" || return 1
    kernel="$(uname -s)" || {
        printf 'credential_dirs: uname -s failed; no directory mode was changed\n' >&2
        return 1
    }
    case "${kernel}" in
    Darwin | *BSD) no_follow=1 ;;
    esac
    for dir in "${dirs[@]}"; do
        dir="$(strip_trailing_slashes "${dir}")" || return 1
        if [ -L "${dir}" ] || ! path_has_no_symlink "${dir}" "${home}"; then
            printf 'warning: credential_dirs: %s is a symlink or is reached through one; its mode is left unchanged\n' "${dir}" >&2
            continue
        fi
        [ -d "${dir}" ] || continue
        if ! chmod_private "${dir}" "${no_follow}"; then
            printf 'credential_dirs: cannot set %s to mode 0700\n' "${dir}" >&2
            status=1
        fi
    done
    return "${status}"
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    secure_credential_dirs
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/common/gh_extensions.sh
# @brief Install GitHub CLI extensions used by the dotfiles.
# @description
#   Activates `mise` when available and installs the configured `gh`
#   extensions at their reviewed tags, only when GitHub CLI is already
#   authenticated. An extension at another tag is reinstalled at the pin.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

readonly MISE_BIN="${HOME}/.local/bin/mise"

# Rendered from assets.gh-extensions in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml; change the pin there.
GH_POI_PIN_VERSION="v0.18.5"

readonly GH_EXTENSIONS=(
    "seachicken/gh-poi=${GH_POI_PIN_VERSION}"
)

#
# @description Activate `mise` so `gh` can resolve the expected toolchain.
#
function activate_mise() {
    local activation
    if [ -x "${MISE_BIN}" ]; then
        activation="$("${MISE_BIN}" activate bash)" || {
            printf '%s activate bash failed; gh extensions were not installed.\n' "${MISE_BIN}" >&2
            return 1
        }
        eval "${activation}"
    fi
}

#
# @description Print the path of scripts/pin_records.py, the strict reader of gh's extension manifest: from
#   the dotfiles checkout (update-agent-assets.sh), chezmoi's source directory (the run_once script), or this
#   file's own repository.
# @exitcode 1 When none of them holds it.
#
function pin_records_path() {
    local root
    for root in "${DOTFILES_REPO_SOURCE_DIR:-}" "${CHEZMOI_SOURCE_DIR:+${CHEZMOI_SOURCE_DIR}/..}" "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/../.."; do
        if [ -n "${root}" ] && [ -f "${root}/scripts/pin_records.py" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${root}/scripts/pin_records.py"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

#
# @description Print gh's record of an installed extension as `<tag> <pinned>`, or `absent`.
# @arg $1 string Extension repository, for example seachicken/gh-poi.
# @exitcode 2 When the record cannot be read, has an unknown shape, or names another owner (a fork):
#   such a copy cannot be verified, so the caller reinstalls it pinned.
#
function gh_extension_state() {
    local reader gh_dir

    if ! reader="$(pin_records_path)" || ! gh_dir="$(python3 -I "${reader}" agent-home gh)"; then
        printf 'Cannot find scripts/pin_records.py or the gh data directory; cannot verify %s.\n' "$1" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    python3 -I "${reader}" gh-extension "${gh_dir}" "$1"
}

#
# @description Install one extension pinned at its tag without losing the copy it replaces.
# @description
#   The installed copy (gh's directory for it) is moved aside under the gh extensions directory with a
#   dot name, which `gh extension list` does not read as an extension; the pinned copy is installed;
#   on success the old copy is deleted, on failure the partial install is removed and the old copy put
#   back, so a failed install never leaves the extension missing.
# @arg $1 string Extension repository, for example seachicken/gh-poi.
# @arg $2 string Pinned tag.
# @exitcode 1 When the pinned install fails (the previous copy is restored) or the old copy cannot be moved.
#
function replace_gh_extension() {
    local extension="$1" pin="$2"
    local reader gh_dir root current previous

    # Its name becomes a directory under gh's extensions directory that is moved and removed: one strict
    # component only (pin_records.py COMPONENT), never empty, `.`, `..` or another path.
    if ! [[ ${extension} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ ]]; then
        printf 'ERROR: %s is not <owner>/<repository>; nothing was changed.\n' "${extension}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # gh's extension directory, resolved as make doctor resolves it (pin_records.py agent-home gh).
    if ! reader="$(pin_records_path)" || ! gh_dir="$(python3 -I "${reader}" agent-home gh)"; then
        printf 'Cannot resolve the gh extension directory; %s was not changed.\n' "${extension}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    root="${gh_dir}/extensions"
    current="${root}/${1##*/}"
    previous="${root}/.${1##*/}.previous"

    if [ -e "${current}" ] || [ -L "${current}" ]; then
        if ! { rm -rf "${previous}" && mv "${current}" "${previous}"; }; then
            printf 'Cannot move %s aside; %s was not changed.\n' "${current}" "${extension}" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    if gh extension install "${extension}" --pin "${pin}"; then
        rm -rf "${previous}"
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'gh extension install %s --pin %s failed; restoring the previous copy.\n' "${extension}" "${pin}" >&2
    if [ -e "${previous}" ] || [ -L "${previous}" ]; then
        rm -rf "${current}" && mv "${previous}" "${current}"
    fi
    return 1
}

#
# @description Install every configured extension pinned at its tag, or skip when unauthenticated.
# @description
#   An extension at its tag and pinned is left alone; one at another tag, or installed unpinned (an earlier
#   plain install, which `gh extension upgrade` could move), is installed again with --pin, keeping the old
#   copy until the new one is in place (replace_gh_extension).
# @exitcode 1 When `gh extension list` fails (an unreadable list is never read as "not installed") or a
#   pinned install fails; every other extension is still processed.
#
function install_gh_extensions() {
    local entry extension pin listing installed state failed=0

    if ! gh auth status &> /dev/null; then
        printf '%s\n' 'Warning: GitHub CLI is not authenticated. Run setup-gh, then make update to install extensions.' >&2
        return 0
    fi

    if ! listing="$(gh extension list)"; then
        printf '%s\n' 'gh extension list failed; gh extensions were not changed.' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    for entry in "${GH_EXTENSIONS[@]}"; do
        extension="${entry%=*}"
        pin="${entry##*=}"
        installed="$(awk -F '\t' -v expected="${extension}" '$2 == expected { print $3; exit }' <<< "${listing}")"
        # gh's own record decides, read strictly; one it cannot verify (unreadable, foreign) is reinstalled.
        state="$(gh_extension_state "${extension}")" || state="unverifiable"
        if [ "${state}" = "${pin} true" ]; then
            continue
        fi
        if [ "${state}" != "absent" ]; then
            printf '%s is %s (listed at %s); reinstalling it pinned at %s.\n' "${extension}" "${state}" "${installed:-no tag}" "${pin}"
        fi
        replace_gh_extension "${extension}" "${pin}" || failed=1
    done
    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Run the `gh` extension installation workflow.
#
function main() {
    activate_mise
    install_gh_extensions
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/common/mise.sh
# @brief Install and bootstrap `mise`.
# @description
#   Nothing runs before a check independent of the release page passes. With gpg and gpgv
#   (the release key's signature on SHASUMS256.asc) or an authenticated gh (the GitHub release
#   attestation), it downloads the newest standalone `mise` release that is at least 72 hours old
#   and verifies it that way; without either, as on a fresh macOS, it installs the reviewed
#   fallback release pinned in the manifest. Then it runs `mise install` against the repository
#   tool definitions; `mise self-update` moves mise forward afterwards.

# set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

export MISE_INSTALL_PATH="${HOME}/.local/bin/mise"
readonly MISE_RELEASE_REPO="jdx/mise"
# Rendered from assets.mise in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml; change it there.
readonly MISE_GPG_FINGERPRINT="24853EC9F655CE80B48E6C3A8B81C9D17413A06D"
# mise publishes its release key on this keyserver; only the pinned fingerprint makes it trusted.
readonly MISE_GPG_KEY_URL="https://keys.openpgp.org/vks/v1/by-fingerprint/${MISE_GPG_FINGERPRINT}"
# The reviewed release a host without gh or gpg bootstraps, rendered from assets.mise.fallback;
# change them there. Assignments stay non-readonly so tests can override them after sourcing.
MISE_FALLBACK_VERSION="v2026.10.3"
MISE_FALLBACK_MACOS_X64_SHA256="791b92b446729c53e6501acd2b84ea207f541659ca9d0480c9c70c291919a321"
MISE_FALLBACK_MACOS_ARM64_SHA256="28ecc8640b0a28dab52817766f37fecfd898f1dff82e03f36fcb072e971f9246"
MISE_FALLBACK_LINUX_X64_SHA256="04147c68e946902f5226dfdcd54d19907aed3cf54d95b2f27d2b9c778bb26f9e"
MISE_FALLBACK_LINUX_ARM64_SHA256="e79866e32624b346f6854d93ca8a24294516cd7c0b48ce0e80af508fb7c3d8b8"

# The chezmoi script includes scripts/lib/github-release.sh before this file; a direct run sources it.
if ! declare -F github_release_tag > /dev/null; then
    # shellcheck source=scripts/lib/github-release.sh
    source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../scripts/lib/github-release.sh"
fi

# @description Print the mise release artifact name for the current platform.
# @arg $1 string The release tag.
function mise_artifact() {
    local os arch
    os="$(uname -s)"
    arch="$(uname -m)"
    case "${os}/${arch}" in # lint-comparisons: allow the uname OS/arch pair, not a path
    Darwin/x86_64) printf 'mise-%s-macos-x64.tar.gz\n' "$1" ;;
    Darwin/arm64) printf 'mise-%s-macos-arm64.tar.gz\n' "$1" ;;
    Linux/x86_64) printf 'mise-%s-linux-x64.tar.gz\n' "$1" ;;
    Linux/aarch64 | Linux/arm64) printf 'mise-%s-linux-arm64.tar.gz\n' "$1" ;;
    *)
        printf 'Unsupported mise platform: %s/%s\n' "${os}" "${arch}" >&2
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Verify a release archive against an upstream checksum manifest.
# @arg $1 archive Archive path.
# @arg $2 manifest Checksum manifest path.
# @arg $3 name Artifact name in the manifest.
function verify_mise_archive() {
    local archive="$1" manifest="$2" name="$3" expected actual sum
    expected="$(awk -v name="./${name}" '$2 == name { print $1 }' "${manifest}")"
    [ -n "${expected}" ] || {
        printf 'Missing checksum for %s\n' "${name}" >&2
        return 1
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        sum="$(sha256sum "${archive}")" || {
            printf 'sha256sum could not hash %s\n' "${archive}" >&2
            return 1
        }
    else
        sum="$(shasum -a 256 "${archive}")" || {
            printf 'shasum -a 256 could not hash %s\n' "${archive}" >&2
            return 1
        }
    fi
    actual="${sum%% *}"
    [ "${actual}" = "${expected}" ] || {
        printf 'Checksum mismatch for %s\n' "${name}" >&2
        return 1
    }
}

#
# @description Print the checksums SHASUMS256.asc signs, once gpgv has checked the signature
#   against mise's release key with the pinned fingerprint.
# @arg $1 path SHASUMS256.asc
# @arg $2 path A private scratch directory.
# @stdout The signed checksum lines.
# @exitcode 3 The release key could not be downloaded, so nothing was checked.
#
function verify_mise_shasums_signature() {
    local key="$2/mise-release-key.asc" key_data key_fields fingerprint validity expiration now
    curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 "${MISE_GPG_KEY_URL}" -o "${key}" || return 3
    mkdir -m 700 "$2/gnupg" || return
    key_data="$(gpg --homedir "$2/gnupg" --batch --with-colons --import-options show-only --import "${key}")" || return
    # Exactly one primary key, and the fingerprint line right after it is the primary's own.
    key_fields="$(awk -F: '
        $1 == "pub" { keys++; validity = $2; expiration = $7; primary = 1; next }
        $1 == "fpr" && primary { fingerprint = $10; primary = 0 }
        END { if (keys == 1) print fingerprint, validity, expiration }' <<< "${key_data}")" || {
        printf 'awk could not read the mise release key listing.\n' >&2
        return 1
    }
    read -r fingerprint validity expiration <<< "${key_fields}"
    now="$(date +%s)" || {
        printf 'date +%%s failed; the mise release key expiry was not checked.\n' >&2
        return 1
    }
    if [ "${fingerprint}" != "${MISE_GPG_FINGERPRINT}" ] || [ "${validity}" != "-" ] ||
        { [ -n "${expiration}" ] && ! [ "${expiration}" -gt "${now}" ] 2> /dev/null; }; then
        printf 'mise release key validation failed.\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    gpg --homedir "$2/gnupg" --batch --yes --dearmor --output "$2/mise-keyring.gpg" "${key}" || return
    gpgv --keyring "$2/mise-keyring.gpg" --output - "$1"
}

#
# @description Succeed when gpg and gpgv can check the release key's signature on SHASUMS256.asc.
#
function mise_gpg_ready() {
    command -v gpg > /dev/null 2>&1 && command -v gpgv > /dev/null 2>&1
}

#
# @description Print the version the installed mise reports, or nothing when it is absent or broken.
#
function mise_installed_version() {
    local output
    [ -x "${MISE_INSTALL_PATH}" ] || return 0
    # A binary that exits non-zero is broken whatever it printed, so it reports no version.
    output="$("${MISE_INSTALL_PATH}" --version 2> /dev/null)" || return 0
    printf '%s\n' "${output}" | awk 'NR == 1 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$/ { print $1 }'
}

#
# @description Succeed when version $1 is at or after version $2 (X.Y.Z, a leading v ignored).
#
function mise_version_at_least() {
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "${2#v}" "${1#v}" | awk -F. '
        NR == 1 { split($0, floor, ".") }
        NR == 2 {
            for (i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
                if ($i + 0 > floor[i] + 0) exit 0
                if ($i + 0 < floor[i] + 0) exit 1
            }
            exit 0
        }'
}

#
# @description Print the reviewed fallback sha256 of a mise release artifact.
# @arg $1 string The artifact name.
#
function mise_fallback_sha256() {
    case "$1" in
    *-macos-x64.tar.gz) printf '%s\n' "${MISE_FALLBACK_MACOS_X64_SHA256}" ;;
    *-macos-arm64.tar.gz) printf '%s\n' "${MISE_FALLBACK_MACOS_ARM64_SHA256}" ;;
    *-linux-x64.tar.gz) printf '%s\n' "${MISE_FALLBACK_LINUX_X64_SHA256}" ;;
    *-linux-arm64.tar.gz) printf '%s\n' "${MISE_FALLBACK_LINUX_ARM64_SHA256}" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

#
# @description Install standalone `mise`, verified before it runs: the newest cooled-down release
#   when gpg (the signed SHASUMS256.asc) or an authenticated gh (the release attestation) can
#   check it, otherwise the reviewed fallback release and its pinned sha256. The release's own
#   checksum file is checked on every path.
#
function _install_mise_binary() (
    local artifact attestation=0 base_url fallback="" gpg_ready="" installed reviewed signature=0 stage="" tag tmpdir
    if mise_gpg_ready; then gpg_ready=1; fi
    if [ -n "${gpg_ready}" ] || github_attestation_ready; then
        tag="$(github_release_tag "${MISE_RELEASE_REPO}")" || {
            printf 'Could not resolve a %s release.\n' "${MISE_RELEASE_REPO}" >&2
            return 1
        }
    else
        # Neither check can run before mise does, so the reviewed release installs instead,
        # unless a mise at or past it (moved forward by mise self-update) is already there.
        fallback=1
        tag="${MISE_FALLBACK_VERSION}"
        installed="$(mise_installed_version)"
        if [ -n "${installed}" ] && mise_version_at_least "${installed}" "${tag}"; then
            printf 'mise %s stays: it is at or past the reviewed fallback %s.\n' "${installed}" "${tag}"
            return 0
        fi
        printf 'No gpg and no authenticated gh 2.93.0 or newer: installing the reviewed mise %s (assets.mise.fallback).\n' "${tag}"
    fi
    artifact="$(mise_artifact "${tag}")" || return
    base_url="https://github.com/${MISE_RELEASE_REPO}/releases/download/${tag}"
    tmpdir="$(mktemp -d)" || return
    trap 'rm -rf "${tmpdir}"; [ -z "${stage}" ] || rm -f "${stage}"' EXIT
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "${MISE_INSTALL_PATH}")" || return
    stage="$(mktemp "${MISE_INSTALL_PATH}.tmp.XXXXXX")" || return

    # Each curl gets 30 s to connect and fails a transfer under 1 KB/s for 60 s, so a stalled download ends.
    curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 "${base_url}/${artifact}" \
        -o "${tmpdir}/${artifact}" || return
    if [ -n "${gpg_ready}" ]; then
        # The checksums come from the signed text itself, never from an unsigned SHASUMS256.txt.
        if curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 "${base_url}/SHASUMS256.asc" \
            -o "${tmpdir}/SHASUMS256.asc"; then
            verify_mise_shasums_signature "${tmpdir}/SHASUMS256.asc" "${tmpdir}" > "${tmpdir}/SHASUMS256.txt" || signature=$?
        else
            signature=3
        fi
        if [ "${signature}" -eq 3 ] && github_attestation_ready; then
            # The signature's inputs are unavailable, not wrong: the attestation is the check instead.
            printf 'warning: could not fetch the mise release key or SHASUMS256.asc; the release attestation verifies mise %s instead.\n' "${tag}" >&2
            gpg_ready=""
        elif [ "${signature}" -eq 3 ]; then
            printf 'Could not fetch the mise release key or SHASUMS256.asc, and no authenticated gh can verify mise %s instead; nothing was installed.\n' "${tag}" >&2
            return 1
        elif [ "${signature}" -ne 0 ]; then
            printf 'GPG signature check failed for SHASUMS256.asc of mise %s.\n' "${tag}" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    if [ -z "${gpg_ready}" ]; then
        curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 "${base_url}/SHASUMS256.txt" \
            -o "${tmpdir}/SHASUMS256.txt" || return
    fi
    verify_mise_archive "${tmpdir}/${artifact}" "${tmpdir}/SHASUMS256.txt" "${artifact}" || return
    if [ -n "${fallback}" ]; then
        # The reviewed sha256 is the check here; SHASUMS256.txt above only re-checked the download.
        reviewed="$(mise_fallback_sha256 "${artifact}")" || {
            printf 'mise_fallback_sha256 has no reviewed sha256 for %s; nothing was installed.\n' "${artifact}" >&2
            return 1
        }
        printf '%s  ./%s\n' "${reviewed}" "${artifact}" > "${tmpdir}/reviewed.txt"
        verify_mise_archive "${tmpdir}/${artifact}" "${tmpdir}/reviewed.txt" "${artifact}" || {
            printf 'mise %s does not match its reviewed sha256; nothing was installed.\n' "${tag}" >&2
            return 1
        }
    else
        github_release_attestation "${MISE_RELEASE_REPO}" "${tag}" "${tmpdir}/${artifact}" || attestation=$?
        # Status 2 (gh not ready) is enough only after the GPG signature verified the checksums.
        if [ "${attestation}" -ne 0 ] && { [ "${attestation}" -ne 2 ] || [ -z "${gpg_ready}" ]; }; then
            printf 'GitHub release attestation failed for %s; nothing was installed.\n' "${artifact}" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    tar -xzf "${tmpdir}/${artifact}" -C "${tmpdir}" || return
    install -m 0755 "${tmpdir}/mise/bin/mise" "${stage}" || return
    mv -f "${stage}" "${MISE_INSTALL_PATH}"
)

#
# @description Install the standalone `mise` binary and activate it for the caller.
#
function install_mise() {
    local activation
    _install_mise_binary || return
    activation="$("${MISE_INSTALL_PATH}" activate bash)" || return
    eval "${activation}"
}

#
# @description Trust the local `mise.toml` before plugin or tool installation.
#
function trust_mise_config() {
    mise trust --yes
}

#
# @description Install all tools declared for this repository through `mise`.
#
function run_mise_install() {
    # `MISE_CURRENT_VERSION` is interpreted by mise as a tool env override for `current`.
    unset MISE_CURRENT_VERSION
    trust_mise_config || return

    # One bare install takes every declared tool under the config's
    # minimum_release_age (~/.npmrc applies the same window) and skips requests
    # already satisfied, so an installed "latest" needs no registry lookup.
    mise install
}

#
# @description Remove the standalone `mise` binary from the local bin dir.
#
function uninstall_mise() {
    rm "${MISE_INSTALL_PATH}"
}

#
# @description Install `mise` and the configured tools.
#
function main() {
    install_mise || return
    run_mise_install
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/common/sheldon.sh
# @brief Install the Sheldon shell plugin manager.
# @description
#   Builds the newest crates.io release with its packaged Cargo.lock; cargo
#   checks the crate against the registry index checksum. Runs on every chezmoi
#   apply and skips when the newest crate is already installed.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

readonly BIN_DIR="${HOME}/.local/bin"
readonly MISE_BIN="${HOME}/.local/bin/mise"

#
# @description Build and install the crates.io Sheldon release with locked dependencies.
# @exitcode 3 cargo could not download the crate or the index, so nothing was installed.
# @exitcode * cargo's own status for any other failure, a checksum among them (a 3 becomes 1).
#
function install_sheldon() (
    local stage="" status=0 tmpdir
    tmpdir="$(mktemp -d)" || return
    trap 'rm -rf "${tmpdir}"; [ -z "${stage}" ] || rm -f "${stage}"' EXIT
    mkdir -p "${BIN_DIR}" || return
    stage="$(mktemp "${BIN_DIR}/sheldon.tmp.XXXXXX")" || return
    # cargo's errors still reach stderr; the copy tells a download failure from the rest.
    { CARGO_INSTALL_ROOT="${tmpdir}" "${MISE_BIN}" exec -- cargo install \
        --locked --features vendored --registry crates-io sheldon 2>&1 1>&3 | tee "${tmpdir}/cargo.log" >&2; } 3>&1 || status=$?
    if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        # Keep cargo's own status (101 for every error), except that 3 means a download failure here.
        [ "${status}" -ne 3 ] || status=1
        # A checksum is verification, even inside a download error.
        grep -qi 'checksum' "${tmpdir}/cargo.log" && return "${status}"
        grep -qiE 'failed to download|resolve host|failed to update registry|spurious network|timed out' "${tmpdir}/cargo.log" && return 3
        return "${status}"
    fi
    install -m 0755 "${tmpdir}/bin/sheldon" "${stage}" || return
    mv -f "${stage}" "${BIN_DIR}/sheldon"
)

#
# @description Print the installed Sheldon version, or nothing when it is absent or cannot report one.
#
function sheldon_installed_version() {
    local output
    [ -x "${BIN_DIR}/sheldon" ] || return 0
    # A binary that exits non-zero is broken whatever it printed, so it reports no version.
    output="$("${BIN_DIR}/sheldon" --version 2> /dev/null)" || return 0
    printf '%s\n' "${output}" | awk '$1 == "sheldon" { print $2; exit }'
}

#
# @description Print the newest Sheldon version on crates.io, as cargo's own index search reports it.
#
function sheldon_newest_version() {
    "${MISE_BIN}" exec -- cargo search sheldon --limit 1 2> /dev/null |
        awk -F'"' '$1 == "sheldon = " { print $2; found = 1; exit } END { exit !found }'
}

#
# @description Remove the installed `sheldon` binary.
#
function uninstall_sheldon() {
    rm "${BIN_DIR}/sheldon"
}

#
# @description Install Sheldon, or update it when crates.io has a newer release.
#
function main() {
    local installed newest status=0
    installed="$(sheldon_installed_version)"
    newest="$(sheldon_newest_version)" || newest=""
    if [ -n "${installed}" ]; then
        if [ -z "${newest}" ]; then
            printf 'warning: could not look up the newest sheldon crate; sheldon %s stays.\n' "${installed}" >&2
            return 0
        fi
        [ "${installed}" != "${newest}" ] || return 0
    fi
    install_sheldon || status=$?
    # A failed download keeps a working sheldon; a failed check never does.
    if [ "${status}" -eq 3 ] && [ -n "${installed}" ]; then
        printf 'warning: could not download the sheldon %s crate; sheldon %s stays.\n' "${newest}" "${installed}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    return "${status}"
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/macos/arm64/prepare_arm64_system.sh
# @brief Prepare Apple Silicon hosts for the dotfiles setup.
# @description
#   Installs Rosetta on arm64 macOS machines when it is not already present.

set -Eeuo pipefail

        softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license

}

#

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/macos/common/brew.sh
# @brief Install Homebrew and apply repository defaults.
# @description
#   Ensures Homebrew is installed on macOS, resolves untrusted runner-image taps
#   on CI, and disables analytics for the local user.

set -Eeuo pipefail

# Rendered from assets.homebrew-installer in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml; change it there.
readonly HOMEBREW_INSTALL_COMMIT="09c62fc577ec170172b0a184060f141a2c622dc1"
readonly HOMEBREW_INSTALL_SHA256="5f333bbe53bc490e51e7ccb1df8779b3dd6ee73a1a7379efda216edb08ccb148"

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

# The chezmoi script includes scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh before this file; a direct run sources it.
if ! declare -F is_ci_runner > /dev/null; then
    # shellcheck source=scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh
    source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh"
fi

#
# @description Check whether Homebrew is already available on `PATH`.
#
function is_homebrew_exists() {
    command -v brew &> /dev/null
}

#
# @description Install Homebrew when it is not present.
#
function install_homebrew() {
    if ! is_homebrew_exists; then
        (
            local actual installer
            installer="$(mktemp)"
            trap 'rm -f "${installer}"' EXIT
            # 30 s to connect, and a transfer under 1 KB/s for 60 s fails, so a stalled download ends.
            curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 \
                "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/${HOMEBREW_INSTALL_COMMIT}/install.sh" -o "${installer}"
            actual="$(shasum -a 256 "${installer}" | awk '{ print $1 }')"
            [ "${actual}" = "${HOMEBREW_INSTALL_SHA256}" ] || {
                printf 'Homebrew installer checksum mismatch\n' >&2
                return 1
            }
            NONINTERACTIVE=1 /bin/bash "${installer}"
        )
    fi
}

#
# @description Disable Homebrew analytics for the current user.
#
function opt_out_of_analytics() {
    brew analytics off
}

#
# @description On a CI runner, resolve the third-party taps that the runner
#   image ships tapped but untrusted, so `brew install` stops warning about
#   them (https://docs.brew.sh/Tap-Trust). The untrusted taps come from
#   Homebrew's own `brew untrust --tap` listing, and the installed items from
#   `brew list --full-name`, which reads each keg's install receipt and so also
#   lists items from untrusted taps. Least privilege first: trust only the
#   installed formulae and casks of each untrusted tap. A tap with nothing
#   installed has no item to trust; measured on macos-14 (job
#   https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/actions/runs/37030239884/job/110914945531),
#   item-level trust alone cleared azure/bicep and hashicorp/tap but the
#   warning persisted for aws/tap, so only such taps get whole-tap trust.
#   Does nothing outside a GitHub Actions runner (is_ci_runner): an agent
#   shell's `CI=true` on an operator's Mac never trusts a tap.
#
function handle_ci_untrusted_taps() {
    is_ci_runner || return 0

    local listing taps installed tap name formulae="" casks="" with_items="" whole_taps=""
    if ! listing="$(brew untrust --tap 2> /dev/null)"; then
        printf 'brew has no tap trust (no brew untrust command); skipping untrusted tap handling\n' >&2
        return 0
    fi
    # The listing is a header line followed by one indented tap name per line.
    taps="$(sed -n 's/^  //p' <<< "${listing}")"
    [ -n "${taps}" ] || return 0

    installed="$(brew list --formula --full-name)"
    for name in ${installed}; do
        for tap in ${taps}; do
            if [[ "${name}" == "${tap}/"* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow brew names: user/repo/formula vs its tap user/repo
                formulae+=" ${name}"
                with_items+=" ${tap} "
            fi
        done
    done
    installed="$(brew list --cask --full-name)"
    for name in ${installed}; do
        for tap in ${taps}; do
            if [[ "${name}" == "${tap}/"* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow brew names: user/repo/cask vs its tap user/repo
                casks+=" ${name}"
                with_items+=" ${tap} "
            fi
        done
    done
    for tap in ${taps}; do
        if [[ "${with_items}" != *" ${tap} "* ]]; then
            whole_taps+=" ${tap}"
        fi
    done

    # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # Space-separated names, word splitting intended.
    if [ -n "${formulae}" ]; then
        brew trust --formula ${formulae}
    fi
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # Space-separated names, word splitting intended.
    if [ -n "${casks}" ]; then
        brew trust --cask ${casks}
    fi
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # Space-separated names, word splitting intended.
    if [ -n "${whole_taps}" ]; then
        brew trust ${whole_taps}
    fi
}

#
# @description Install Homebrew and apply repository defaults.
#
function main() {
    install_homebrew
    handle_ci_untrusted_taps
    opt_out_of_analytics
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/macos/common/command_line_tool.sh
# @brief Install Xcode Command Line Tools.
# @description
#   Triggers the Apple command line tools installer and waits for the user to
#   confirm the installation has completed.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

#
# @description Install Xcode Command Line Tools when `git` is not available.
#
function install_command_line_tool() {
    local git_cmd_path="/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/git"

    if [ ! -e "${git_cmd_path}" ]; then
        # Install command line developer tool
        xcode-select --install
        # Want for user input
        echo "Press any key when the installation has completed."
        IFS= read -r -n 1 -d ''
        #          │  │    └ The first character of DELIM is used to terminate the input line, rather than newline.
        #          │  │
        #          │  └ returns after reading NCHARS characters rather than waiting for a complete line of input.
        #          │
        #          └ If this option is given, backslash does not act as an escape character.
        #            The backslash is considered to be part of the line. In particular, a backslash-newline
        #            pair may not be used as a line continuation.
    else
        echo "Command line developer tools are installed."
    fi
}

#
# @description Run the command line tools installation flow.
#
function main() {
    install_command_line_tool
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi
