#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-body-edit.sh
# @brief Replace the body of the open pull request of the current branch, the worker seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, the worker seat's lever, allowed only in the form
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-body-edit.sh --body-file *` by `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/worker.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"); the orchestrator's policy denies it. It
#   edits only the pull request of the branch the seat has checked out: `git branch --show-current` must name a
#   branch other than `main`, and `gh pr view --json number,headRefName,state` (the pull request of that branch)
#   must report it as `headRefName` and `OPEN`. The body file is a regular file (not a symlink) of 1 to 65536
#   bytes whose real path is inside `$TMPDIR` or the checkout. The new body must hold exactly one line starting
#   `Program-Unit:`, and it must be `Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>`, the line `regime-ci.py` reads: `<program>` in
#   `regime-init`'s grammar (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) naming a store the checkout holds,
#   `.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/units.tsv` (U71), and a plain unit id (a fix round writes its parent id,
#   `preferences.md` standing order 24); when the current body already carries one such line, the program and the
#   unit must stay the same, so an edit fixes the line or the text but never moves a pull request to another
#   program or unit. Every `## ` heading line and the `Generated with [Claude Code]` footer line of
#   the current body must still be in the new body, so sections are added or rewritten, never dropped. The one
#   write is `gh pr edit <n> --body-file <file>`. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl
#   `alarm`).
# @option --body-file <file> The new body.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `edited pr=<n> branch=<b> program=<program> unit=U<n> sha256=<body sha256>`.
# @exitcode 0 The body was replaced.
# @exitcode 1 A `git` or `gh` read, or the edit, failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the branch, the pull request's state, the body file, or the body's content.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-body-edit.sh --body-file "$TMPDIR/body.md"
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='pr-body-edit.sh'
usage='usage: pr-body-edit.sh --body-file <file>'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
unit_line='^Program-Unit: [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}/U[0-9]+$'
footer_re='Generated with \[Claude Code\]\(https://claude\.com/claude-code\)'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Refuse unless $1 is a regular file of 1 to 65536 bytes inside $TMPDIR or the checkout.
# @arg $1 path The body file.
# @set body_path Its real path.
body_file_check() {
    local file=$1 dir root size
    [[ -f ${file} && ! -L ${file} ]] || refuse "the body file is not a regular file: ${file}"
    case ${file} in # lint-comparisons: allow splits the argument at its last slash; the real path is compared below
    */*) dir=${file%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${file}"
    body_path=${dir}/${file##*/}
    size=$(wc -c < "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
    size=${size//[[:space:]]/}
    if ! [[ ${size} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ((size == 0 || size > 65536)); then
        refuse "the body file must hold 1 to 65536 bytes: ${body_path}"
    fi
    for root in "${TMPDIR:-}" "${toplevel}"; do
        [[ -n ${root} && -d ${root} ]] || continue
        root=$(cd "${root}" && pwd -P) || continue
        [[ ${body_path} == "${root}"/* ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    done
    refuse "the body file is outside \$TMPDIR and the checkout: ${body_path}"
}

# @description Print the lines of file $2 (CR stripped) that match the ERE $1, one per line. The ERE reaches awk
#   through the environment, since `awk -v` would read its backslashes as escapes.
# @arg $1 string The ERE.
# @arg $2 path The file.
lines_matching() {
    LINES_RE=$1 awk '{ sub(/\r$/, "") } $0 ~ ENVIRON["LINES_RE"]' "$2"
}

[[ $# -eq 2 && $1 == --body-file ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
branch=$(git branch --show-current) || fail 'git branch --show-current failed'
[[ -n ${branch} ]] || refuse 'HEAD is detached; switch to the branch of your pull request'
[[ ${branch} != main ]] || refuse 'the current branch is main'
body_file_check "$2"
markers=$(lines_matching '^Program-Unit:' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
[[ -n ${markers} && ${markers} != *$'\n'* && ${markers} =~ ${unit_line} ]] ||
    refuse "the body must hold exactly one line 'Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>' (a plain unit id); it holds: ${markers:-none}"
marker=${markers#Program-Unit: }
program=${marker%/*}
unit=${marker##*/}
[[ -f ${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/units.tsv ]] ||
    refuse "the Program-Unit line names ${program}, but the checkout holds no .orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/units.tsv"

view=$(gh_bounded pr view --json number,headRefName,state --jq '[(.number | tostring), .headRefName, .state] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read the pull request of ${branch}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r number head state <<< "${view}"
[[ ${number} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || fail "gh pr view printed no pull request number: ${number}"
[[ ${head} == "${branch}" ]] || refuse "pull request ${number} is the pull request of ${head}, not of the current branch ${branch}"
[[ ${state} == OPEN ]] || refuse "pull request ${number} is ${state}, not OPEN"

current=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pr-body-edit.XXXXXX") || fail 'mktemp failed'
trap 'rm -f "${current}"' EXIT
gh_bounded pr view "${number}" --json body --jq .body > "${current}" || fail "cannot read the body of pull request ${number}"
old_markers=$(lines_matching "${unit_line}" "${current}") || fail "cannot read ${current}"
if [[ -n ${old_markers} && ${old_markers} != *$'\n'* && ${old_markers#Program-Unit: } != "${marker}" ]]; then
    refuse "the current body names ${old_markers#Program-Unit: }; an edit keeps the program and the unit (the new body names ${marker})"
fi
kept=$(lines_matching "^## |${footer_re}" "${current}") || fail "cannot read ${current}"
new_lines=$(lines_matching '' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ -n ${line} ]] || continue

done <<< "${kept}"

if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
    digest=$(sha256sum < "${body_path}") || digest=''
else
    digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${body_path}") || digest=''
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-close.sh
# @brief Close the pull requests a clean-up table marks `close:`, with the row's text as the comment.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed only in the form
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table *` by `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). The table is a table the orchestrator
#   wrote: a regular file (not a symlink) whose real path is under
#   `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/handouts/` of the main checkout, where the orchestrator seat
#   runs (a linked worktree, a worker's clone, is refused). The lever reads its `## Open pull requests` section,
#   whose header row must be `| PR | branch | opened | files | title | default |`; every row must carry a `#<n>`
#   PR cell and a backticked branch cell, else the whole table is refused before any `gh` call. The selected rows
#   are those whose `default` cell starts with `close:`; `--only <pr>` narrows them to that one row and is refused
#   when the table has no such `close:` row. Then, per row, read-only: `gh pr view <n>` must report `OPEN` and the
#   table's branch as `headRefName`, and `gh pr list --state open --head <branch>` must list no other pull
#   request (#396 and #412 share `tools/anthropic-auth-route-structured`); a row failing that is refused with its
#   own line. A failed `gh` read aborts the run before any close. Only then does each remaining row get
#   `gh pr close <n> --comment <default cell>`. The lever never passes `--delete-branch` (closing one of two pull
#   requests on a shared branch that way would close the other) and never deletes a branch. Each `gh` call is
#   bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @option --from-table <file> The clean-up table.
# @option --only <pr> Close only this row.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One line per selected row, `closed pr=<n> branch=<b>` or `refused pr=<n> reason=<why>`, then
#   `summary closed=<n> refused=<n>`.
# @exitcode 0 Every selected row was closed.
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` read failed (nothing was closed) or a close failed (the lines say which were closed).
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the table's path or shape, no selected row, or at least one row refused (its line
#   says why; the other rows were closed).
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover/handouts/cleanup-table.md
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover/handouts/cleanup-table.md --only 378
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='pr-close.sh'
usage='usage: pr-close.sh --from-table <table.md> [--only <pr>]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
header='| PR | branch | opened | files | title | default |'
# The `## Open pull requests` rows as `<pr>\t<branch>\t<default>`; exit 3 for a missing section or header, 4 for a
# row without a `#<n>` PR cell or a backticked branch cell. `\|` inside a cell is text, not a separator.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # awk source, not shell
table_awk='
function trim(s) { sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", s); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
/^## / { if (in_section) { done = 1 } in_section = ($0 == "## Open pull requests"); next }
!in_section || done { next }
/^[ \t]*$/ { if (rows) { done = 1 } next }
!seen_header { if ($0 != header) { exit 3 } seen_header = 1; next }
/^\|( *:?-+:? *\|)+ *$/ { next }
{
    line = $0
    gsub(/\\\|/, "\001", line)
    n = split(line, cell, "|")
    if (n != 8 || trim(cell[1]) != "" || trim(cell[8]) != "") { exit 4 }
    pr = trim(cell[2]); branch = trim(cell[3]); text = trim(cell[7])
    gsub(/\001/, "|", text); gsub(/\t/, " ", text)
    if (pr !~ /^#[1-9][0-9]*$/ || branch !~ /^`[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]+`$/) { exit 4 }
    rows++
    print substr(pr, 2) "\t" substr(branch, 2, length(branch) - 2) "\t" text
}
END { if (!seen_header) { exit 3 } }
'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

table=''
only=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --from-table)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        table=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    --only)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        only=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
done
[[ -n ${table} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ -z ${only} || ${only} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "--only is not a decimal number: ${only}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
git_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree; run from the main checkout, where the orchestrator writes its tables"
[[ -f ${table} && ! -L ${table} ]] || refuse "the table is not a regular file: ${table}"
case ${table} in
*/*) table_dir=${table%/*} ;;
*) table_dir=. ;;
esac
[[ -n ${table_dir} ]] || table_dir=/
table_dir=$(cd "${table_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${table}"
handouts='^/.+/\.orchestration/orchestrate/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/handouts$'
[[ ${table_dir} =~ ${handouts} && ${table_dir} == "${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/"* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "the table is not under ${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/handouts/: ${table_dir}"

status=0
rows=$(awk -v header="${header}" "${table_awk}" "${table_dir}/${table##*/}") || status=$?
case ${status} in
0) ;;
3) refuse "no '## Open pull requests' section with the header ${header} in ${table}" ;;
4) refuse "a row of '## Open pull requests' in ${table} has no #<n> PR cell or backticked branch cell" ;;
*) refuse "cannot read ${table} (awk exited ${status})" ;;
esac

selected=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text; do
    [[ -n ${pr} && ${text} == close:* ]] || continue
    [[ -z ${only} || ${pr} == "${only}" ]] || continue
    selected+=("${pr}"$'\t'"${branch}"$'\t'"${text}")
done <<< "${rows}"
if ((${#selected[@]} == 0)); then
    [[ -n ${only} ]] && refuse "the table has no close: row for pull request ${only}"
    refuse "the table has no row whose default starts with close:"
fi

closable=()
refused=0
for row in "${selected[@]}"; do
    IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text <<< "${row}"
    view=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,headRefName --jq '[.state, .headRefName] | @tsv') ||
        fail "cannot read pull request ${pr}; nothing was closed"
    IFS=$'\t' read -r state head <<< "${view}"
    if [[ ${state} != OPEN ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=state ${state:-unreadable}, not OPEN"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    if [[ ${head} != "${branch}" ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=head branch ${head} is not the table's ${branch}"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    sharing=$(gh_bounded pr list --state open --head "${branch}" --json number --jq '[.[].number | tostring] | join(",")') ||
        fail "cannot list the open pull requests of ${branch}; nothing was closed"
    if [[ ${sharing} != "${pr}" ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=branch ${branch} is the head of open pull requests ${sharing:-none}"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    closable+=("${row}")
done

closed=0
for row in ${closable[@]+"${closable[@]}"}; do
    IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text <<< "${row}"
    gh_bounded pr close "${pr}" --comment "${text}" >&2 || {
        echo "summary closed=${closed} refused=${refused}"
        fail "gh pr close ${pr} failed after ${closed} closed"
    }
    echo "closed pr=${pr} branch=${branch}"
    closed=$((closed + 1))
done
echo "summary closed=${closed} refused=${refused}"
((refused == 0)) || exit 2

}

# @description Print `<ts>\t<verdict>` of the newest ledger row for pull request $1 at the full sha $2, or nothing
#   when no row names that pair. A ledger whose first line is not the header is a refusal; a failed read exits 1.
#   Both sides of every comparison are strings (`""` appended): awk compares two numeric-looking values as numbers,
#   so two different all-digit shas would otherwise match (U71 audit round 1).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @arg $2 string The 40-hex head sha.
ledger_verdict() {
    local out status=0
    out=$(LEDGER_HEADER=${ledger_header} awk -F'\t' -v pr="$1" -v sha="$2" '
        { sub(/\r$/, "") }
        NR == 1 { if ($0 != ENVIRON["LEDGER_HEADER"]) { bad = 1; exit 3 } next }
        ($3 "") == (pr "") && ($4 "") == (sha "") { found = $1 "\t" $5 }
        END { if (!bad && found != "") print found }
    ' "${ledger}") || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0) printf '%s' "${out}" ;;
    3) refuse "${ledger} does not start with the ledger header (${ledger_header//$'\t'/ })" ;;
    *) fail "cannot read ${ledger}" ;;
    esac
}

# @description Refuse unless the newest ledger row for pull request ${pr} at sha $1 is `correct`.
# @arg $1 string The 40-hex sha the verdict must name.
# @set verdict_ts The row's ts.
require_correct_row() {
    local row verdict
    row=$(ledger_verdict "${pr}" "$1") || exit $?
    [[ -n ${row} ]] || refuse "${ledger} has no row for pull request ${pr} at head ${1} (a short sha never matches)"
    verdict_ts=${row%%$'\t'*}
    verdict=${row#*$'\t'}
    [[ ${verdict} =~ ${correct_re} ]] ||
        refuse "the newest ${ledger} row for pull request ${pr} at ${1} (${verdict_ts}) is not correct: ${verdict}"
}

# @description Set `ledger` to the one store the merge may read (U71, bot P1 4370212009: a caller-chosen ledger.tsv
#   could hold a fabricated row): `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/ledger.tsv` of this main checkout,
#   `<program>` taken from the pull request body's one `Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>` line. No directory from the
#   checkout down and not the ledger is a symlink, each is owned by this user, and `--records` must resolve
#   (`pwd -P`) to exactly that directory; anything else is a refusal.
# @set ledger The canonical ledger path.
resolve_store() {
    local body markers line program path given part
    body=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json body --jq .body) || fail "cannot read the body of pull request ${pr}"
    markers=''
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line=${line%$'\r'}
        [[ ${line} == Program-Unit:* ]] && markers+="${line}"$'\n'
    done <<< "${body}"
    markers=${markers%$'\n'}
    [[ -n ${markers} && ${markers} != *$'\n'* && ${markers} =~ ${program_unit_re} ]] ||
        refuse "the body of pull request ${pr} must hold exactly one line 'Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>'; it holds: ${markers:-none}"
    program=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
    path=${toplevel}
    for part in .orchestration orchestrate "${program}"; do
        path=${path}/${part}
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
            refuse "${path} is not a directory of this user (a symlink or a missing store); the merge reads only the checkout's own store"
    done
    given=$(cd "${records}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || refuse "--records ${records} is no directory"
    [[ ${given} == "${path}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        refuse "--records ${records} is not the program's store ${path} (named by the body's Program-Unit line)"
    ledger=${path}/ledger.tsv
    [[ -f ${ledger} && ! -L ${ledger} && -O ${ledger} && -r ${ledger} ]] ||
        refuse "${ledger} is not a readable regular file of this user"
}

[[ $# -ge 1 ]] || refuse "${usage}"
pr=$1
shift
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"
[[ $# -eq 2 && $1 == --records && -n $2 ]] || refuse "${usage}"
records=$2
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
# The checkout the lever runs in, by its physical path, and it must be the main checkout: a linked worktree (a
# worker's clone) holds a copy of the store that is not the orchestrator's record (U71, bot P1 4370212009).
toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'run from the repository checkout that holds the program store'
[[ -n ${toplevel} && -d ${toplevel} ]] || refuse 'run from the repository checkout that holds the program store'
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
git_dir=$(git -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) ||
    refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree; run from the main checkout, where the orchestrator keeps its store"

view=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid,isDraft \
    --jq '[.state, .baseRefName, .headRefOid, (.isDraft | tostring)] | @tsv') || fail "cannot read pull request ${pr}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r state base head draft <<< "${view}"
[[ ${state} == OPEN ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} is ${state:-unreadable}, not OPEN"
[[ ${base} == main ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} targets ${base:-nothing}, not main"
[[ ${draft} == false ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} is a draft (isDraft=${draft:-unreadable})"
[[ ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || fail "pull request ${pr} has no readable head: ${head}"
resolve_store

require_correct_row "${head}"

status=0
checks=$(gh_bounded pr checks "${pr}" --json bucket,name --jq '.[] | [.bucket, .name] | @tsv') || status=$?
# The second read checks the base as well as the head (U71 audit round 7): `--match-head-commit` pins only the head,
# and a pull request retargeted from main with the same head would otherwise merge into the new base.
again=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json headRefOid,baseRefName --jq '[.headRefOid, .baseRefName] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read the head and base of ${pr} again"
IFS=$'\t' read -r again again_base <<< "${again}"
[[ ${again} == "${head}" ]] || refuse "the head of pull request ${pr} moved from ${head} to ${again:-unreadable} during the checks"
[[ ${again_base} == main ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} was retargeted from main to ${again_base:-unreadable} during the checks"
[[ -n ${checks} ]] || {
    ((status == 0)) && refuse "no check is reported on the head ${head}"
    fail "gh pr checks ${pr} failed (exit ${status}) and printed nothing"
}
red=''
while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket name; do
    case ${bucket} in
    pass | skipping) ;;
    *) red+="${red:+, }${name}=${bucket}" ;;
    esac
done <<< "${checks}"
[[ -z ${red} ]] || refuse "CI is not green on the head ${head}: ${red}"
((status == 0)) || fail "gh pr checks ${pr} exited ${status} although every listed check passed"

merge_status=0
gh_bounded pr merge "${pr}" --squash --match-head-commit "${head}" >&2 || merge_status=$?
after=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,mergeCommit,baseRefName,headRefOid \
    --jq '[.state, (.mergeCommit.oid // ""), .baseRefName, .headRefOid] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read pull request ${pr} after the merge command (exit ${merge_status}); read it before anything else"
IFS=$'\t' read -r state commit merged_base merged_head <<< "${after}"
[[ ${state} == MERGED && ${commit} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] ||
    fail "pull request ${pr} is ${state:-unreadable} after the merge command (exit ${merge_status})"
# A merge this lever did not make (U71 audit round 9): when the pinned merge failed and someone else merged a later
# head, MERGED alone would credit the audited head with that merge, so the merged head must be the audited one.
[[ ${merged_head} == "${head}" ]] ||
    fail "pull request ${pr} merged at head ${merged_head:-unreadable} as ${commit}, not at the audited head ${head} (merge command exit ${merge_status}); that merge is not this verdict's; tell the operator"
# gh pr merge takes no base (`gh pr merge --help`), so a retarget between the second read and the merge call is
# reported here, loudly, with the base it landed on; it cannot be undone by the lever.
[[ ${merged_base} == main ]] ||
    fail "pull request ${pr} merged into ${merged_base:-an unreadable base}, not main: it was retargeted after the last read; tell the operator"
((merge_status == 0)) || echo "${lever}: the merge command exited ${merge_status}, but the pull request is MERGED" >&2
echo "merged pr=${pr} head=${head} commit=${commit} verdict=${verdict_ts}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-thread-reply.sh
# @brief Reply to one review thread of a pull request with a disposition, the orchestrator seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed by the row
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-thread-reply.sh *` of `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). Every argument is checked before the
#   first `gh` call, and the one write is
#   `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<pr>/comments/<comment-id>/replies -F body=@<file>`.
#   `<pr>` and `<comment-id>` are decimal. The body file is a regular file (not a symlink) of 1 to 65536 bytes
#   whose real path is inside `$TMPDIR` or the checkout's `.orchestration/` (the program's store), so no other
#   file of the account can be posted. Its first line is a disposition of `preferences.md` standing order 22:
#   `fixed: <40-hex sha>`, `refuted: <text citing a URL or a file:line>`, `residual: unit=U<n> gate=<clause>`
#   or `residual: operator=<decisions.tsv ts>`; `pr-threads-check.sh` reads the same grammar. `<owner>/<repo>`
#   comes from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`, never from an argument. The comment must be a review comment
#   of that pull request (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/comments/<comment-id>`, its `pull_request_url`
#   ends in `/pulls/<pr>`) and the first comment of its thread (no `in_reply_to_id`), since GitHub takes a reply
#   only to that one. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @arg $2 int The id of the thread's first review comment (`databaseId`, the `#discussion_r<id>` anchor).
# @option --body-file <file> The reply text.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `replied pr=<pr> comment=<id> reply=<new id> url=<html url>`.
# @exitcode 0 The reply was posted.
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` read or the write failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the body file, the disposition, or a comment that is not the thread's first on <pr>.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-thread-reply.sh 480 4365170609 --body-file "$TMPDIR/reply.md"
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='pr-thread-reply.sh'
usage='usage: pr-thread-reply.sh <pr> <comment-id> --body-file <file>'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Succeed when $1, a reply's first line, is a disposition (`preferences.md` standing order 22).
# @arg $1 string The line.
disposition_line() {
    local fixed='^fixed: [0-9a-f]{40}( |$)'
    local refuted='^refuted: .*(https://[^[:space:]]+|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*:[0-9]+)'
    local unit='^residual: unit=U[0-9]+[a-z]? gate=[^[:space:]]'
    local operator='^residual: operator=[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$'
    [[ $1 =~ ${fixed} || $1 =~ ${refuted} || $1 =~ ${unit} || $1 =~ ${operator} ]]
}

# @description Refuse unless $1 is a regular file of 1 to 65536 bytes inside $TMPDIR or <toplevel>/.orchestration.
# @arg $1 path The body file.
# @set body_path Its real path.
body_file_check() {
    local file=$1 dir root size
    [[ -f ${file} && ! -L ${file} ]] || refuse "the body file is not a regular file: ${file}"
    case ${file} in # lint-comparisons: allow splits the argument at its last slash; the real path is compared below
    */*) dir=${file%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${file}"
    body_path=${dir}/${file##*/}
    size=$(wc -c < "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
    size=${size//[[:space:]]/}
    if ! [[ ${size} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ((size == 0 || size > 65536)); then
        refuse "the body file must hold 1 to 65536 bytes: ${body_path}"
    fi
    for root in "${TMPDIR:-}" "${toplevel}/.orchestration"; do
        [[ -n ${root} && -d ${root} ]] || continue
        root=$(cd "${root}" && pwd -P) || continue
        [[ ${body_path} == "${root}"/* ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    done
    refuse "the body file is outside \$TMPDIR and the checkout's .orchestration/: ${body_path}"
}

[[ $# -eq 4 && $3 == --body-file ]] || refuse "${usage}"
pr=$1
comment=$2
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"
[[ ${comment} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}$ ]] || refuse "the comment id is not a decimal number: ${comment}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
body_file_check "$4"
first=$(sed -n '1{s/\r$//;p;}' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
disposition_line "${first}" ||
    refuse "the first line is not a disposition (fixed: <sha> | refuted: <doc or file:line> | residual: unit=U<n> gate=<clause> | residual: operator=<ts>): ${first}"

repo=$(gh_bounded repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner) || fail 'gh repo view failed'
[[ ${repo} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || fail "gh repo view printed no owner/repo: ${repo}"
owner_pr=$(gh_bounded api "repos/${repo}/pulls/comments/${comment}" \
    --jq '[(.pull_request_url | capture("/pulls/(?<n>[0-9]+)$").n), (.in_reply_to_id // 0 | tostring)] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read review comment ${comment} of ${repo}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r comment_pr reply_to <<< "${owner_pr}"
[[ ${comment_pr} == "${pr}" ]] || refuse "review comment ${comment} belongs to pull request ${comment_pr:-none}, not ${pr}"
[[ ${reply_to} == 0 ]] || refuse "review comment ${comment} is a reply (to ${reply_to}); name the thread's first comment"

posted=$(gh_bounded api -X POST "repos/${repo}/pulls/${pr}/comments/${comment}/replies" -F "body=@${body_path}" \
    --jq '[(.id | tostring), .html_url] | @tsv') || fail "the reply to ${comment} on pull request ${pr} failed"
IFS=$'\t' read -r reply url <<< "${posted}"
echo "replied pr=${pr} comment=${comment} reply=${reply} url=${url}"

usage='usage: pr-thread-resolve.sh <pr> <comment-id> [--records <dir>]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # GraphQL variables, not shell

  repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
    pullRequest(number: $pr) {
      headRefOid
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        pageInfo { hasNextPage }
        nodes { id isResolved comments(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { databaseId createdAt body } } }
      }
    }

# <newest reply's first line>` (TSV; the reply is last because it may be empty).
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq source, not shell

  | (["head", .headRefOid, (.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage | tostring)] | @tsv),
    (.reviewThreads.nodes[] | .comments as $c | [.id, (.isResolved | tostring),
      ($c.nodes[0].databaseId | tostring), ($c.nodes[0].createdAt | fromdateiso8601 | tostring),
      ([($c.nodes[0].body // "") | capture("!\\[P(?<p>[0-3]) Badge\\]") | "P" + .p] | first // "-"),
      ($c.totalCount | tostring),
      (($c.nodes[1:] | last | .body // "") | split("\n") | (.[0] // "") | rtrimstr("\r"))] | @tsv)'

# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2

}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {

# @arg $1 int The created epoch of the thread's first comment.

disposition() {

    local fixed='^fixed: ([0-9a-f]{40})( |$)'
    local refuted='^refuted: .*(https://[^[:space:]]+|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*:[0-9]+)'

            return

            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} predates the finding)"
            return
        fi
        echo "fixed ${fix}"

        echo refuted
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${unit} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}

            return

        1) echo "open (residual: no units.tsv row ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/units.tsv" ;;
        esac

        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check decisions.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/decisions.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual operator=${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no decisions.tsv row at ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/decisions.tsv" ;;
        esac

    else

    fi

comment=''
records=''

        else

    -F "pr=${pr}" --jq "${threads_jq}") || fail "cannot list the review threads of pull request ${pr}"

head=''
page=''
thread=''
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id resolved first created severity count reply; do
    if [[ ${id} == head ]]; then
        head=${resolved}
        page=${first}
    elif [[ ${first} == "${comment}" ]]; then
        thread=${id}
        thread_resolved=${resolved}
        thread_created=${created}
        thread_severity=${severity}
        thread_count=${count}
        thread_reply=${reply}
    fi
done <<< "${listing}"
[[ ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} has no readable head"
[[ ${page} == false ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} has more than 100 review threads; resolve it by hand"
[[ -n ${thread} ]] || refuse "no review thread of pull request ${pr} starts with comment ${comment}"
[[ ${thread_resolved} == false ]] || refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} is already resolved"
if ! [[ ${thread_count} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ((thread_count > 100)); then
    refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} has more than 100 comments; resolve it by hand"
fi
[[ ${thread_created} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "unreadable creation time for the thread of comment ${comment}"

[[ ${state} != open* ]] ||
    refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} has no valid disposition, ${state#open }; reply with pr-thread-reply.sh first"

done_id=$(gh_bounded api graphql -f "query=${resolve_mutation}" -f "thread=${thread}" \
    --jq '.data.resolveReviewThread.thread | select(.isResolved) | .id') || fail "resolveReviewThread failed for ${thread}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-update-branch.sh
# @brief Merge main into an open pull request's branch (`gh pr update-branch`), the orchestrator seat's lever.
# @description

#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-update-branch.sh *` of `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). `<pr>` is decimal and checked before the
#   first `gh` call. `gh pr view <pr> --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid` must report `OPEN` and base `main`,
#   else the lever refuses; the one write is `gh pr update-branch <pr>`, GitHub's merge form (never `--rebase`,
#   which rewrites the worker's branch), and the head is read again afterwards. The new head needs its own audit
#   and `correct` ledger row before `pr-merge.sh` merges it (U71: no verdict carries over from the old head). Each
#   `gh` call is bounded
#   by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `updated pr=<pr> old=<head before> new=<head after>`.
# @exitcode 0 The branch was updated (`old` equals `new` when it was already up to date).
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` read or the update failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, a pull request that is not open, or a base other than main.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-update-branch.sh 480
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }

        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2

    }

usage='usage: pr-update-branch.sh <pr>'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"

pr=$1
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"

view=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid --jq '[.state, .baseRefName, .headRefOid] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read pull request ${pr}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r state base old <<< "${view}"
[[ ${state} == OPEN ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} is ${state:-unreadable}, not OPEN"
[[ ${base} == main ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} targets ${base:-nothing}, not main"

gh_bounded pr update-branch "${pr}" >&2 || fail "gh pr update-branch ${pr} failed"
new=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid) || fail "cannot read the new head of ${pr}"
[[ ${new} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || fail "pull request ${pr} has no readable head after the update: ${new}"
echo "updated pr=${pr} old=${old} new=${new}"

# @arg $@ string The `git` arguments.
git_scratch() {
    GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 git --git-dir="${repo}" -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false "$@"
}

# @description Refuse a path by its name alone: a control character (a newline would end the component split of
#   check_path early and leave the leaf unchecked), a place outside `.orchestration/`, or `..`. A deletion candidate
#   gets only this check (U101): it is never read, only removed from the new tree.
# @arg $1 string The repository-relative path.
check_name() {
    local path=$1
    [[ ${path} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || refuse 'a path of the copy set holds a control character' # lint-comparisons: allow a character test on the raw git path

    case ${path} in # lint-comparisons: allow a repository-relative path as git prints it, refused unless under the store
    .orchestration/*) ;;
    *) refuse "a path of the copy set is outside .orchestration/: ${path}" ;;
    esac
    [[ ${path} != *..* ]] || refuse "a path of the copy set holds '..': ${path}" # lint-comparisons: allow refuses a raw git path that holds ..
}

# @description Refuse a path the store listing names (check_name, then): a symlink component, or, when it exists,
#   anything but a regular file whose directory resolves inside the store (U28b F2) or a directory. A directory
#   stands where the index still has a file of that name (the file became a directory, U101): its own files are
#   listed as entries of their own, and the file it replaced is carried as a deletion.
# @arg $1 string The repository-relative path.
check_path() {
    local path=$1 prefix='' part rest source_dir
    check_name "${path}"
    # Split on `/` by parameter expansion (no here-string, so no temporary file can go missing, U101).
    rest=${path}
    while [[ -n ${rest} ]]; do
        part=${rest%%/*}
        if [[ ${rest} == */* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow splits the raw git path into its components
            rest=${rest#*/}
        else
            rest=''
        fi
        prefix=${prefix:+${prefix}/}${part}
        [[ ! -L ${prefix} ]] || refuse "a component of a path of the copy set is a symlink: ${prefix} (in ${path})"
    done
    if [[ -f ${path} ]]; then
        source_dir=$(cd "${path%/*}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${path}"
        [[ ${source_dir} == "${store_root}" || ${source_dir} == "${store_root}"/* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
            refuse "a path of the copy set resolves outside ${store_root}: ${path}"
    elif [[ -e ${path} && ! -d ${path} ]]; then
        refuse "a path of the copy set is not a regular file: ${path}"
    fi
}

base=origin/main
program=''
unit=U20
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --base | --program | --unit)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        case $1 in
        --base) base=$2 ;;
        --program) program=$2 ;;
        --unit) unit=$2 ;;
        esac
        shift 2
        ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
done
[[ ${base} == origin/main ]] || refuse "--base accepts only origin/main: ${base}" # lint-comparisons: allow a git ref name, not a path
[[ ${unit} =~ ^U[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "--unit is not a plain unit id U<n>: ${unit}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
git_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree; run from the main checkout, where the orchestrator writes its records"
cd "${toplevel}" || refuse "cannot enter ${toplevel}"
# U28b F2: the store root itself is no symlink, so every canonical path below is measured against the real store.
top_real=$(pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
[[ -d .orchestration && ! -L .orchestration ]] || refuse ".orchestration is missing or a symlink in ${toplevel}"
store_root=$(cd .orchestration && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}/.orchestration"
[[ ${store_root} == "${top_real}/.orchestration" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse ".orchestration resolves outside ${top_real}: ${store_root}"
if [[ -z ${program} ]]; then
    programs=()
    for dir in .orchestration/orchestrate/*/; do
        dir=${dir%/}
        [[ -d ${dir} ]] && programs+=("${dir##*/}")
    done
    ((${#programs[@]} == 1)) || refuse "name the program with --program; .orchestration/orchestrate/ holds ${#programs[@]}"
    program=${programs[0]}
fi
[[ ${program} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$ ]] || refuse "the program name is outside [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*: ${program}"
records=.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
# U28b F2: no component of the store directory is a symlink (git would list the files below a linked one too).
for prefix in .orchestration/orchestrate "${records}"; do
    [[ ! -L ${prefix} ]] || refuse "a component of a path of the copy set is a symlink: ${prefix} (in ${records}/)"
done
[[ -d ${records} ]] || refuse "no program directory ${records}"
# U101: the words no copy may contain; the file itself is never copied, deleted or published.
words=${records}/redact-words.txt
if [[ -e ${words} || -L ${words} ]]; then
    check_path "${words}"
    [[ -f ${words} ]] || refuse "${words} is not a regular file"
    words_real=$(cd "${records}" && pwd -P)/redact-words.txt || refuse "cannot resolve ${words}"
else
    words_real=''
fi
# The commit's identity is the operator's, read once here and handed to commit-tree as GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_*.
# `git config --get` exits 1 for a key that is unset and with another status when the configuration cannot be read:
# measured on git 2.56.0 (2026-10-28), 128 for an unparsable file, where the manual says 3. Any status other than 0
# and 1 is a failure here, so the reader is right under both. An empty value is refused here, before any branch
# exists, where commit-tree would otherwise refuse it later. The same reader serves origin's URL (audit of 0c7bf092).
# @arg $1 string The git function to read with (`git` reads the user configuration too, `git_plain` does not).
# @arg $2 string The configuration key.
# @arg $3 string The variable that receives the value.
read_config() {
    local value status=0
    value=$("$1" config --get "$2") || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0) [[ -n ${value} ]] || refuse "git config $2 is empty" ;;
    1) refuse "git config $2 is unset" ;;
    *) fail "cannot read git config $2 (git config exited ${status})" ;;
    esac
    printf -v "$3" '%s' "${value}"
}
author_name='' author_email='' push_url=''
read_config git user.name author_name
read_config git user.email author_email
# U101: origin's URL, read once here: main is fetched from it and the sync pushed to it (below); https only.
read_config git_plain remote.origin.url push_url
case ${push_url} in # lint-comparisons: allow the URL's scheme as configured, the push target itself
https://?*) ;;
*) refuse "the push needs an https origin URL, not ${push_url}" ;;
esac

scratch=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/records-sync.XXXXXX") || fail 'mktemp failed'
trap cleanup EXIT
# U101: the whole commit is built in a new repository in the scratch directory, which has no config, includes,
# hooks or attributes of the checkout's: origin's main is fetched into it from the https URL, the copies are hashed
# into it with --no-filters, and the tree, the commit and the push are made there. The checkout is only read: its
# listings, its store files and its config's user.name/user.email (above).
repo=${scratch}/repo.git
git_plain init --quiet --bare --template= "${repo}" || fail 'git init --bare for the sync failed'
git_scratch -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' \
    fetch --quiet --no-tags "${push_url}" refs/heads/main || fail 'git fetch main from origin failed'
main=$(git_scratch rev-parse --verify 'FETCH_HEAD^{commit}') || fail 'cannot read the fetched main'
main_tree=$(git_scratch rev-parse --verify "${main}^{tree}") || fail 'cannot read the tree of main'
# U101: the copy set is the store's files on disk (tracked or not, not ignored), compared with origin/main by
# content; the checkout's HEAD, however stale, is never the base. Each listing goes to a file and is read
# NUL-delimited: a git failure, even after output, and a listing whose last entry has no NUL end (cut short) refuse
# here, before any copy, commit or gh call.
listing=${scratch}/listing
# Audit of 0c7bf092: `git ls-files` warns and exits 0 for a directory it cannot open, and a file it then leaves out
# of the listing is absent from the store as far as this lever can see, which is a deletion. So the store is walked
# first (find exits non-zero for a directory it cannot read, and each directory is checked readable and
# searchable), and any warning of the listing refuses the run as well; neither output is shown (a store path may
# hold a redact word).
find "${records}" -type d -print0 > "${scratch}/dirs" 2> "${scratch}/walk.err" ||
    refuse "a directory under ${records}/ cannot be read or entered; nothing was created"
dir=''
while IFS= read -r -d '' dir; do
    [[ -r ${dir} && -x ${dir} ]] || refuse "a directory under ${records}/ cannot be read or entered; nothing was created"
done < "${scratch}/dirs"
[[ -z ${dir} ]] || refuse "the walk of ${records}/ ends mid-entry; nothing was created"
# Audit of 7b3c2718: the listing is the one index read in the checkout, and a `core.fsmonitor` hook set in any
# configuration the checkout reads would run inside it (and could write into the store before the copy). The
# command line turns it off, with the hooks path; the user's ignore rules (core.excludesFile) still apply.
git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- "${records}/" \
    > "${listing}" 2> "${scratch}/listing.err" || fail 'git ls-files failed'
[[ ! -s ${scratch}/listing.err ]] ||
    refuse "git ls-files warned while listing ${records}/ (its output is withheld); nothing was created"
files=()
present=$'\n'
path=''
while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
    [[ ${path} != "${words}" ]] || continue # lint-comparisons: allow both are repository-relative paths as git prints them
    check_path "${path}"
    if [[ -f ${path} && ${present} != *$'\n'"${path}"$'\n'* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow repository-relative paths as git prints them
        files+=("${path}")
        present+=${path}$'\n'
    fi
done < "${listing}"
[[ -z ${path} ]] || refuse "the listing of ${records}/ ends mid-entry; nothing was created"
# Full entries (`<mode> blob <oid>` TAB path): the deletions come from them, and the expected change set below
# compares each copy with its entry on main.
git_scratch ls-tree -r -z "${main}" -- "${records}/" > "${listing}" || fail "git ls-tree ${base} failed"
gone=()
base_entries=$'\n'
entry=''
while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
    path=${entry#*$'\t'}
    check_name "${path}"
    base_entries+=${path}$'\t'${entry%%$'\t'*}$'\n'
    [[ ${path} != "${words}" && ${present} != *$'\n'"${path}"$'\n'* ]] || continue # lint-comparisons: allow repository-relative paths as git prints them
    gone+=("${path}")
done < "${listing}"
[[ -z ${entry} ]] || refuse "the listing of ${base}:${records}/ ends mid-entry; nothing was created"
((${#files[@]} + ${#gone[@]} > 0)) || refuse "nothing to sync under ${records}/"

# The masker and the scanner are main's validator, alone in a tools tree whose `home/` holds main's top-level entry
# names (empty), so its home-path pattern skips the repository's own `home/<entry>` paths as in a checkout; a main
# without `home/` gives an empty one.
tools=${scratch}/tools
mkdir -p "${tools}/scripts" "${tools}/home" || fail 'cannot make the tools tree'
git_scratch cat-file blob "${main}:scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" > "${tools}/scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" ||
    fail "cannot read scripts/validate-agent-assets.py of ${base}"
git_scratch ls-tree -z --name-only "${main}" -- home/ > "${scratch}/home-entries" || fail "cannot list home/ of ${base}"
while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
    entry=${entry#home/}
    [[ -n ${entry} && ${entry} != *[/[:cntrl:]]* && ${entry} != . && ${entry} != .. ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow a tree entry name as git prints it
        fail "home/ of ${base} holds an unusable entry name"
    mkdir "${tools}/home/${entry}" || fail 'cannot make the tools tree'
done < "${scratch}/home-entries"
# U101: the copies are masked and scanned in the scratch directory, and these same files are what hash-object
# writes, so the committed bytes are the scanned bytes.
copies=${scratch}/copies
masked=()
for path in ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}; do
    mkdir -p "${copies}/${path%/*}" || fail "mkdir for ${path} failed"
    cp -p "${path}" "${copies}/${path}" || fail "cp ${path} failed"
    masked+=("${copies}/${path}")
done
if ((${#masked[@]})); then
    # U101: neither tool's output is shown. The masker prints each copy's path and, on a key collision, the original
    # keys; either may hold a redact word or a secret. Both go to files in the scratch directory (removed on exit),
    # and a failure says only that it happened and the exit status.
    status=0
    uv run --no-project python -I "${tools}/scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" --mask-secrets "${masked[@]}" \
        > "${scratch}/mask.log" 2>&1 || status=$?
    ((status == 0)) || fail "masking the copies failed (exit ${status}); its output is withheld, nothing was published"
    # U101: after masking, no copy may still name a secret, a home path or a redact word, its path included.
    scan=(--scan-identifiers)
    [[ -z ${words_real} ]] || scan+=(--redact-words "${words_real}")
    (cd "${copies}" && uv run --no-project python -I "${tools}/scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" "${scan[@]}" -- "${files[@]}") \
        > "${scratch}/scan.log" 2>&1 || status=$?
    ((status != 1)) ||
        refuse 'the identifier scan found a secret, a home path or a redact word in the masked copies (exit 1); its output is withheld, nothing was published'
    ((status == 0)) || fail "the identifier scan failed (exit ${status}); its output is withheld, nothing was published"
fi

# U101: the new tree is main's tree in a private index, the deletions removed first (a file that became a directory,
# or the reverse, frees its name), then each masked copy hashed with --no-filters and entered by mode and object id.
# The expected change set is computed alongside: every deletion, and every copy whose `<mode> blob <oid>` differs
# from its entry on main.
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=${scratch}/index
git_scratch read-tree "${main}" || fail 'git read-tree failed'
expected=${scratch}/expected
: > "${expected}" || fail 'cannot write the expected change set'
# A bare repository has no work tree, which `update-index --force-remove` asks for; an `--index-info` line of mode 0
# removes the path from the index without one. The zero object id has main's length (SHA-1 or SHA-256).
zero=${main//?/0}
for path in ${gone[@]+"${gone[@]}"}; do
    printf '0 %s\t%s\0' "${zero}" "${path}" | git_scratch update-index -z --index-info ||
        fail "git update-index removing ${path} failed"
    printf '%s\0' "${path}" >> "${expected}" || fail 'cannot write the expected change set'
done
for path in ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}; do
    blob=$(git_scratch hash-object -w --no-filters -- "${copies}/${path}") || fail "git hash-object ${path} failed"
    mode=100644
    if [[ -x ${copies}/${path} ]]; then
        mode=100755
    fi
    git_scratch update-index --add --cacheinfo "${mode},${blob},${path}" || fail "git update-index ${path} failed"
    if [[ ${base_entries} != *$'\n'"${path}"$'\t'"${mode} blob ${blob}"$'\n'* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a repository-relative path and an object id as git prints them
        printf '%s\0' "${path}" >> "${expected}" || fail 'cannot write the expected change set'
    fi
done
new_tree=$(git_scratch write-tree) || fail 'git write-tree failed'
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
# U101: the tree's change against main must be exactly the computed set, as sorted NUL lists.
changed=${scratch}/changed
git_scratch diff-tree -r --no-renames --name-only -z "${main_tree}" "${new_tree}" > "${changed}" ||
    fail 'git diff-tree failed'
LC_ALL=C sort -z "${expected}" > "${expected}.sorted" || fail 'cannot sort the expected change set'
LC_ALL=C sort -z "${changed}" > "${changed}.sorted" || fail 'cannot sort the change set'
cmp -s "${expected}.sorted" "${changed}.sorted" ||
    refuse 'the new tree changes other paths than the copy set; nothing was committed or pushed'
[[ -s ${changed} ]] || refuse 'the copies equal origin/main; nothing to sync'
count=$(tr -cd '\000' < "${changed}" | wc -c) || fail 'cannot count the changed paths'
count=${count//[[:space:]]/}

remote_heads=$(git_scratch -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' \
    ls-remote --heads "${push_url}" 'refs/heads/records/*') || fail 'git ls-remote origin failed'
# U28b F6: a local branch occupies its number too, whatever left it behind.
local_heads=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/heads/records/') || fail 'git for-each-ref failed'
pr_heads=$(gh_plain pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName') ||
    fail 'gh pr list failed'
last=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "${remote_heads}" "${local_heads}" "${pr_heads}" |
    PROGRAM=${program} awk '{ ref = $NF; sub(/^refs\/heads\//, "", ref) }
        ref ~ "^records/(sync|program-store|" ENVIRON["PROGRAM"] "-sync)-[0-9]+$" { n = ref; sub(/.*-/, "", n); if (n + 0 > max) max = n + 0 }
        END { print max + 0 }') || fail 'cannot number the sync'
n=$((last + 1))
branch=records/sync-${n}
[[ ${branch} =~ ^records/sync-[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse "the branch is outside records/sync-<n>: ${branch}"

units=$(git_scratch diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -U0 "${main_tree}" "${new_tree}" -- "${records}/units.tsv" |
    sed -n -E 's/^\+(U[0-9]+[a-z]?)\t.*/\1/p' | sort -u | paste -sd ' ' -) || fail 'cannot list the units'
decisions=$(git_scratch diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -U0 "${main_tree}" "${new_tree}" -- "${records}/decisions.tsv" |
    sed -n -E 's/^\+([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]+Z)\t.*/\1/p' | sort -u | paste -sd ' ' -) ||
    fail 'cannot list the decisions'
title="chore(records): ${program} sync ${n}"
message=$(printf '%s\n\n%s\n\n%s\n' "${title}" \
    "Carries ${count} file(s) of ${records}/ from the main checkout, compared with origin/main (records-sync.sh)." \
    "${footer}") || fail 'cannot write the commit message'
# U101: author and committer come only from the environment set here, the identity read at the start.
commit=$(printf '%s\n' "${message}" |
    GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=${author_name} GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=${author_email} \
        GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=${author_name} GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=${author_email} \
        git_scratch commit-tree "${new_tree}" -p "${main}" -F -) || fail 'git commit-tree failed'
git_scratch -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' \
    push --quiet "${push_url}" "${commit}:refs/heads/${branch}" || fail "git push ${branch} failed; nothing was opened"
body=${scratch}/body.md
# U108: the `## Contract` section is what pr-audit.sh judges the pull request against (a body without one is
# refused), so every records sync gets an orchestrator verdict. Only the program name is interpolated.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the backticks are Markdown code spans
contract=(
    "The changed paths are the store's files (\`.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/\`, tracked or untracked and not git-ignored, \`redact-words.txt\` excluded) whose masked copy or executable mode differs from origin/main, plus every path origin/main holds under that directory that the listing does not hold as a regular file; the new tree's change set against origin/main is checked to equal exactly that set."
    'No path lies outside that directory.'
    'Every copy was masked with `validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets` and passed its `--scan-identifiers`, with the program'"'"'s `redact-words.txt` when present.'
    'The commit was built in a repository with no user, system or checkout configuration, and pushed over https with no user configuration.'
    'Left out: the content of the records is not reviewed for truth, only by the identifier scan.'
)
{
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the backticks are Markdown code spans
    printf '## Summary\n\nRecords sync %s of `%s` (%s file(s)), carried by `records-sync.sh` from the main checkout and compared with origin/main; every copy was masked with `validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets` and passed its `--scan-identifiers`.\n\n' "${n}" "${program}" "${count}"
    printf -- '- units.tsv rows added or changed: %s\n' "${units:-none}"
    printf -- '- decisions.tsv rows added or changed: %s\n\n' "${decisions:-none}"
    printf '## Contract\n\n'
    printf -- '- %s\n' "${contract[@]}"
    printf '\nProgram-Unit: %s/%s\n\n' "${program}" "${unit}"
    printf '%s\n' "${pr_footer}"
} > "${body}" || fail 'cannot write the body'
url=$(gh_plain pr create --base main --head "${branch}" --title "${title}" --body-file "${body}") ||
    fail "gh pr create failed; the branch ${branch} is pushed"
echo "synced branch=${branch} files=${count} pr=${url}"
</code></pre>

docs.text: Regime-cutover U16, a coordinator lever pre-authorized by Bash(scripts/orchestrator/worktree-gc.sh *) (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Pre-authorized levers"). The candidates are the worktrees of this checkout (git worktree list --porcelain -z) under <toplevel>/.claude/worktrees/, except the quarantine <toplevel>/.claude/worktrees/.gc-quarantine/; every other worktree, the main one and the omp seats included, is never listed. A candidate qualifies when its tree is clean (git status --porcelain --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all prints nothing: git worktree remove deletes ignored files without asking, so a tree holding one, an .env say, is kept; and no index entry carries the assume-unchanged or skip-worktree flag, git ls-files -v tag lowercase or S, since an edit to such a file is invisible to git status and to the removal's own check) and its work landed, the first of: its head is reachable from origin/main (git merge-base --is-ancestor); it landed by content (every path git diff --no-renames --name-only -z <merge-base> <head> names holds in origin/main the entry it holds in the head, mode and object, or is absent from both: the case of a squash merge with no later commit; no merge runs, so no configured merge driver or merge= attribute can answer, and a git failure is an error row); or its head is the headRefOid of a merged pull request of this repository (gh pr list --state merged --head <branch> --json number,headRefOid --limit 100, detached --search <sha>). A branch name alone never counts: a commit pushed after a squash merge is not in main, and --head also matches a fork's branch of the same name. A locked or missing worktree is kept. The listing is read field by field on its NUL separators, so a path cannot forge a record; a candidate whose path contains a newline is an error row. Each candidate prints one row <verdict>\t<path>\t<ref>\t<reason> (a newline in the path printed as \n), verdict gc (qualifies), keep or error, then each quarantined worktree a quarantine row with its age, then one summary row.
